Here, because concentration born of development is intended, access one-pointedness is called 'sensual-sphere concentration.' 'Having made it a dominant factor': that is, thinking, 'If there is concentration for one with desire, may I also have it so,' and having made desire the dominant factor, the foremost, the chief, and the precedent. 'One obtains concentration': the meaning is, thus whatever concentration one obtains, this is called concentration due to desire, that is, concentration with desire as the dominant factor. In the same way, concentration due to energy, and so on, should be understood.

Catukkabhedeti catukkavasena samādhippabhedaniddese. Aññattha sampayogavasena vicārena saha vattamāno vitakko pañcakanaye dutiyajjhāne viyojitopi na suṭṭhu viyojitoti, tena saddhiṃyeva vicārasamatikkamaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “vitakkavicārātikkamena tatiya”nti. Dvidhā [M 1.0115] bhinditvā catukkabhede vuttaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānanti yojanā. Pañcajhānaṅgavasenāti pañcannaṃ jhānānaṃ aṅgabhāvavasena samādhissa pañcavidhatā veditabbā.

‘In the fourfold division’: that is, in the exposition of the divisions of concentration by way of the fourfold method. In another context, initial thought, occurring together with sustained thought by way of association, although dissociated in the second jhāna of the fivefold method, is not well dissociated; therefore, to show the overcoming of sustained thought together with it, it is said, 'the third by the overcoming of initial and sustained thought.' The connection is made by splitting into two the second jhāna mentioned in the fourfold method. ‘By way of the five jhāna factors’: that is, the fivefold nature of concentration should be understood by way of the state of being factors of the five jhānas.

40. Vibhaṅgeti ñāṇavibhaṅge. Tattha hi “jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesavodāna”nti, ettha “saṃkilesa”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha hānabhāgiyo dhammoti apaguṇehi paṭhamajjhānādīhi vuṭṭhitassa saññāmanasikārānaṃ kāmādianupakkhandanaṃ. Visesabhāgiyo dhammoti paguṇehi paṭhamajjhānādīhi vuṭṭhitassa saññāmanasikārānaṃ dutiyajjhānādianupakkhandanaṃ. Tenāha “paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhi”ntiādi. Tassattho (vibha. aṭṭha. 828) – apaguṇassa paṭhamassa jhānassa lābhīnaṃ tato vuṭṭhitaṃ ārammaṇavasena kāmasahagatā hutvā saññāmanasikārā samudācaranti codenti tudanti, tassa kāmānupakkhandānaṃ saññāmanasikārānaṃ vasena sā paṭhamajjhānapaññā hāyati, tasmā hānabhāginī paññā. Avitakkasahagatāti avitakkaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ santato paṇītato manasi karoto ārammaṇavasena avitakkasahagatā samudācaranti paguṇapaṭhamajjhānato vuṭṭhitaṃ dutiyajjhānādhigamatthāya codenti tudanti, tassa dutiyajjhānānupakkhandānaṃ saññāmanasikārānaṃ vasena paṭhamajjhānapaññā visesabhūtassa dutiyajjhānassa uppattiyā padaṭṭhānatāya visesabhāginī paññā. Taṃsampayutto samādhi idhādhippeto. Iminā nayenāti iminā paṭhamajjhāne vuttena vidhinā dutiyajjhānādīsupi hānabhāgiyadhammo, visesabhāgiyadhammo ca veditabbo.

40. ‘In the Vibhaṅga’: that is, in the Analysis of Knowledge. Indeed, therein it is stated, 'the defilement and purification of jhāna, liberation, concentration, and attainment'; in this context, 'defilement,' and so on, are spoken of. Therein, 'a factor of the portion of decline' is the tending of perception and attention towards sensual pleasures, etc., for one who has arisen from the unmastered first jhāna, etc. 'A factor of the portion of distinction' is the tending of perception and attention towards the second jhāna, etc., for one who has arisen from the mastered first jhāna, etc. For that reason, it was said, 'one who is an obtainer of the first jhāna,' etc. The meaning of that is: for those who have obtained the unmastered first jhāna, upon arising from it, perceptions and attention associated with sensual pleasure by way of the object occur, urge, and torment them. By way of these perceptions and attentions that tend towards sensual pleasures, that wisdom of the first jhāna declines; therefore, the wisdom is of the portion of decline. ‘Accompanied by that which is without initial thought’: for one who attends to the second jhāna, which is without initial thought, as peaceful and sublime, perceptions and attention accompanied by that which is without initial thought occur by way of the object. For one who has arisen from the mastered first jhāna, they urge and torment them for the sake of attaining the second jhāna. By way of these perceptions and attentions that tend towards the second jhāna, the wisdom of the first jhāna, because of being the proximate cause for the arising of the distinguished second jhāna, is wisdom of the portion of distinction. The concentration associated with that wisdom is intended here. ‘By this method’: that is, by this method explained in the case of the first jhāna, the factor of the portion of decline and the factor of the portion of distinction should be understood in the case of the second jhāna, etc., as well.

Dasapalibodhavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Ten Impediments

41. Ariyamaggasampayuttoti [V 1.0108] lokuttaraappamāṇaapariyāpannaggahaṇena lokiyehi asādhāraṇato, sappītikādiggahaṇena sādhāraṇato ca ariyamaggasampayutto samādhi vutto. Bhāvito hoti saññāya sampayuttattā. Tanti ariyamaggasamādhiṃ. Visunti paññābhāvanāya visuṃ katvā na vadāma.

41. 'Associated with the noble path' means that concentration associated with the noble path is said to be uncommon in relation to worldly states because of its inclusion of the supramundane, the immeasurable, and the unincluded; and common because of its inclusion of that with rapture and so forth. It is developed because it is associated with wisdom. 'That' refers to the noble path concentration. 'Separately' means we do not speak of it as made separate from the development of wisdom.

Kammaṭṭhānabhāvanaṃ [M 1.0116] paribundheti uparodheti pavattituṃ na detīti palibodho ra-kārassa la-kāraṃ katvā, paripanthoti attho. Upacchinditvāti samāpanena, saṅgahaṇena vā uparundhitvā, apalibodhaṃ katvāti attho.

An impediment (palibodha) obstructs and hinders the development of meditation subjects, not allowing it to proceed; it is so called by changing the letter 'r' (in 'paribodha') to 'l'; the meaning is an obstacle (paripantha). 'Having cut off' means having made it free from impediments, either by bringing the associated task to completion or by providing assistance, thus removing the obstruction.

Āvasanti etthāti āvāso. Paricchedavasena veṇiyati dissatīti pariveṇaṃ. Vihāre bhikkhūnaṃ taṃ taṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ. Svāyaṃ āvāso. Navakammādīsūti ādi-saddena āvāsassa tadaññaṃ abhivuddhikāraṇaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Kāraṇenāti “chāyūdakasampannaṃ sulabhabhikkha”ntiādinā kāraṇena. Apekkhavāti sālayo.

'They dwell here,' thus a dwelling (āvāsa). 'It is seen as enclosed by boundaries,' thus a private dwelling (pariveṇa). In a monastery, this means the various dwelling places for monks. This is the dwelling. In 'new construction and so forth,' the word 'and so forth' includes other causes for the improvement of the dwelling. 'By reason' means by reasons such as 'endowed with shade and water, with alms easy to obtain,' and so forth. 'Having expectation' means being attached.

Tatrāti tasmiṃ palibodhābhāve. Pācīnakhaṇḍarājinti puratthimadisāyaṃ pabbatakhaṇḍānaṃ antare vanarājiṭṭhānaṃ. “Nāmā”ti iminā tassa padesassa ayaṃ samaññāti dasseti. Paṭisāmitamevāti niccakālaṃ paṭisāmetvāva vihārato nikkhamāmīti dasseti. Dhātunidhānaṭṭhānanti kāyabandhanadhammakaraṇanhānasāṭikaakkhakadhātusaṅkhātānaṃ paribhogasarīradhātūnaṃ nidahitaṭṭhānaṃ. Īdisassa ayaṃ thero viya alaggacittassa. Etena “bhikkhunā nāma āvāse evarūpena bhavitabba”nti ovādo dinno hoti. Ito paresupi vatthūsu eseva nayo.

'There' means in the absence of impediments. 'Pācīnakhaṇḍarāji' refers to a place with a line of forest between mountain ridges in the eastern direction. By 'named,' it shows that this is the designation of that place. 'Always tidied up' means that he shows, 'I leave the monastery only after always tidying it up.' 'A place for depositing relics' refers to a place for enshrining relics of use and bodily relics, namely, a waistband, water-strainer, bathing cloth, and collar-bone relic. 'Of such a one' means like this elder, with an unattached mind. By this, the instruction is given: 'A monk should be of such a nature in the dwelling.' This same method applies to the stories that follow as well.

Kulanti kulaggahaṇena kulamanussānaṃ gahaṇaṃ gāmaggahaṇena gāmavāsīnaṃ viya. Upaṭṭhākakulampīti pi-saddena pageva ñātikulanti dasseti. Uddesatthanti uddisāpanatthaṃ, pāṭhaṃ uddisāpetvā sajjhāyitunti attho. Idhevāti imasmiṃyeva padese, yattha katthaci vihāreti attho. Taṃ vihāranti taṃ koraṇḍakavihāraṃ.

'Family' (kula) means that by the term 'family' is understood the people of the family, just as by the term 'village' is understood the village-dwellers. In 'even a supporter family,' the word 'even' shows 'how much more so a family of relatives.' 'For the purpose of recitation' means for the purpose of having the text recited; the meaning is having had the text recited in order to chant it from memory. 'Here itself' means in this very region, in any monastery whatsoever. 'That monastery' means that Koraṇḍaka monastery.

Upagatoti [V 1.0109] vassaṃ upagato. Sadāti gatakālato pabhuti visesato pavāritadivasato paṭṭhāya sabbadā divase divase. Paridevamānāti taṃtaṃvilapanavasena vividhaṃ paridevantī. Sabbaṃ pavattinti attanā tattha diṭṭhakālato paṭṭhāya pacchā samāgamapariyosānaṃ daharassa sabbaṃ pavattiṃ.

'He has entered' means he has undertaken the rains residence. 'Always' means from the time of his departure onwards, especially from the day of the Pavāraṇā onwards, always, day after day. 'Lamenting' means she laments in various ways, by way of various kinds of wailing. 'All that occurred' means the entire course of events concerning the young monk, from the time she saw him there until their final meeting.

Kāyasakkhinti [M 1.0117] “passa ima”nti mukhapaṭiggāhakaṃ katvā. Rathavinītapaṭipadanti dasakathāvatthukittanapubbikaṃ rathavinītūpamāhi vibhāvitaṃ rathavinītasutte (ma. ni. 1.252) āgataṃ sattavisuddhipaṭipadaṃ. Nālakapaṭipadanti “moneyyaṃ te upaññissa”ntiādinā (su. ni. 706) satthārā nālakattherassa desitapaṭipadaṃ. Tuvaṭakapaṭipadanti “mūlaṃ papañcasaṅkhāyā”tiādinā (su. ni. 922) bhagavatā desitapaṭipadaṃ. Tattha hi yathākkamaṃ –

'As a body-witness' means having made him a direct recipient, saying, 'Behold this one.' 'The practice of the Chariot-Relay' is the path of the seven purifications that comes in the Rathavinīta Sutta, made clear by the similes of the chariot-relay, and preceded by the extolling of the ten topics for discussion. 'The practice of Nālaka' is the path taught by the Teacher to the Elder Nālaka, beginning with, 'I will proclaim to you the sage's state' (Snp 706). 'The practice of Tuvaṭaka' is the path taught by the Blessed One, beginning with, 'The root is the reckoning of proliferation' (Snp 922). Therein, in due order—

“Na munī gāmamāgamma, kulesu sahasā care;

Ghāsesanaṃ chinnakatho, na vācaṃ payutaṃ bhaṇe”. (su. ni. 716);

'A sage, on entering a village, should not hastily associate with families. Having cut off talk, he should not utter speech calculated for the purpose of seeking food.'

“Gāme ca nābhisajjeyya, lābhakamyā janaṃ na lapayeyyā”ti. (su. ni. 935) –

'One should not be attached in the village; out of desire for gain, one should not speak ingratiatingly to the people.'

Evamādikā paramappicchakathā āgatā. Catupaccayasantosabhāvanārāmatādīpakanti cīvarādīsu catūsu paccayesu santosassa, bhāvanārāmatāya ca pakāsakaṃ.

Such talk on extreme fewness of wishes is found here. 'The illuminator of contentment with the four requisites and delight in development' means that which reveals contentment with the four requisites such as robes, and delight in development.

Labbhatīti lābho. Tenāha “cattāro paccayā”ti. Mahāparivāreti vipulaparivāre. Piṇḍapātaṃ tāva dentā buddhapūjāpattacīvarādīni tassa parivārāni katvā denti, tathā cīvarādidānepi. Bāhullikapiṇḍapātikāti piṇḍapātikā hutvā paccayabāhullikā. Vadantīti purimadivase bhikkhāya āhiṇḍanakāle yathāsutaṃ vadanti. Niccabyāvaṭo upāsakādīnaṃ saṅgaṇhane.

'It is obtained' (labbhati), thus it is gain (lābho). Therefore, he said, 'the four requisites.' 'With a great retinue' means with a large following. When giving almsfood, for instance, they give offerings to the Buddha, a bowl, robes, and so forth, making them accompaniments to that almsfood; similarly when giving robes and so forth. 'An alms-goer concerned with abundance' means those who, while being alms-food-eaters, strive for an abundance of requisites. 'They speak' means they speak about what they heard while wandering for alms on the previous day. 'Constantly busy' means always occupied with taking care of lay supporters and others.

Tassāti gaṇassa. Soti gaṇapalibodho. Evanti idāni vuccamānākārena gaṇavācakassa pariyesanampi lahukameva icchitabbanti āha “yojanato paraṃ agantvā”ti. Attano kammanti samaṇadhammamāha.

'Of that' means of the group. 'That' is the impediment related to the group. 'Thus': by this is meant that, in the manner now being described, even the search for a group-reciter should be desired as something simple. Thus he said, 'not having gone beyond a yojana.' By 'one's own work' he refers to the ascetic's duties.

Katākateti [V 1.0110] kate ca akate ca kamme jānanavasena ussukkaṃ āpajjitabbaṃ, katākateti vā appake ca mahante ca kate, yathā “phalāphale”ti. Sace bahuṃ avasiṭṭhanti sambandho. Bhārahārā saṅghakiccapariṇāyakā.

'Done and undone' refers to the diligence that should be applied by way of knowing actions done and actions not done; or 'done and undone' can also refer to actions done, whether small or great, like the phrase 'fruits and non-fruits.' 'If much remains'—this is the connection. The 'bearers of the burden' are those who manage the Saṅgha’s affairs.

Pabbajjāpekkhoti [M 1.0118] sīhaḷadīpe kira kuladārakānaṃ pabbajjā āvāhavivāhasadisā, tasmā taṃ paricchinnadivasaṃ atikkametuṃ na sakkā. “Sace taṃ alabhanto na sakkoti adhivāsetu”ntiādinā samāpanena palibodhupacchedo vutto, byatirekato pana “sace taṃ alabhanto sakkoti adhivāsetuṃ, araññaṃ pavisitvā samaṇadhammova kātabbo”ti ayamattho dassitoti saṅgahaṇena palibodhupacchedo veditabbo. Esa nayo sesesupi.

'One who expects ordination'—it is said that in Sri Lanka, for young men of good family, ordination is like a wedding ceremony; therefore, it is impossible to let that appointed day pass. The cutting off of the impediment is spoken of by the conclusion, beginning with, 'If one, failing to obtain that, cannot endure.' By contrast, the meaning is shown by stating, 'If one, failing to obtain that, can endure, then one should enter the forest and practice the duties of a renunciant'; thus, the cutting off of the impediment should be understood by grasping this contrast. This method applies to the rest as well.

Tathāti yathā upajjhāyo gilāno yāvajīvaṃ upaṭṭhātabbo, tathā upasampāditaantevāsiko attano kammavācaṃ vatvā upasampādito.

'Similarly' means: just as a sick preceptor is to be attended to for life, so too a pupil whom one has given the higher ordination, that is, one who was ordained after one has recited the formal act (kammavācā) oneself.

Yo koci rogoti mūlabhūto, anubandho vā attano uppanno. Anamataggeti anu anu amatagge anādimati.

'Whatever illness' means a primary or a consequential illness that has arisen in oneself. 'In what is without known beginning' (anamatagge) refers to this beginningless saṃsāra, whose starting point is unknown and is followed successively.

“Gantho”ti iminā ganthapalibodho idha vuttoti āha “pariyattiharaṇa”nti. Sajjhāyādīhīti sajjhāyadhāraṇaparicayapucchādīhi. Itarassāti abyāvaṭassa. Yassa ganthadhuraṃ vissajjetvā ṭhitassāpi gantho vattateva, na tassa gantho palibodho. Yathā tamhi tamhi vatthumhi āgatattherānaṃ, nāpi sabbena sabbaṃ aganthapasutassa. Majjhimapaṇṇāsako āgacchati, suttapadesānaṃ vārānañca sadisatāya byāmuyhanato. Puna na olokessāmīti kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvā ganthadhuraṃ vissajjemīti attho.

By this term 'text', the impediment of texts is spoken of here; thus he said 'the carrying of the scriptural learning.' 'By recitation and so forth' means by recitation, retention, familiarity, questioning, and so on. 'For the other' means for one who is unengaged. For one who, even after having relinquished the burden of texts, is still fluent in them, the texts are not an impediment—just as for the elders mentioned in various accounts. Nor, for that matter, is it an impediment for one who is not devoted to texts at all. The Majjhima Paṇṇāsaka comes to mind due to confusion arising from the similarity of portions of the suttas and their sections. 'I will not look again' means: 'Having taken up a meditation subject, I will relinquish the burden of texts.'

Gāmavāsikattherehīti anurādhapuravāsīhi. Anuggahetvāti aggahetvā tattha paricayaṃ akatvā. Pañcanikāyamaṇḍaleti dīghāgamādike pañcapi nikāye sikkhitaparisāya. Parivattessāmīti vaṇṇayissāmi. Suvaṇṇabherinti seṭṭhabheriṃ. Katamācariyānaṃ uggahoti katamesaṃ ācariyānaṃ uggaho, kena parivattīyatīti adhippāyo. Ācariyamaggoti ācariyānaṃ kathāmaggo. Attano ācariyānanti attano kathetuṃ yuttānaṃ ācariyānaṃ. Suvinicchitā sabbā tipiṭakapariyatti [V 1.0111] etasmiṃ atthīti sabbapariyattiko, tepiṭakoti attho. Pīṭhe nisinno tato otaritvā bhūmiyaṃ taṭṭikāya nisīditvā. Gatakassāti paṭipattigamanena gatassa diṭṭhasaccassa. Cīvaraṃ pārupitvāti ācariyassa apacitidassanatthaṃ [M 1.0119] parimaṇḍalaṃ cīvaraṃ pārupitvā. Sāṭheyyābhāvato uju. Kāraṇākāraṇassa ājānanato ājānīyo.

'By the elders residing in the village' means by those residing in Anurādhapura. 'Not having learned' means not having taken it up, not having become familiar with it there. 'In the circle of the five Nikāyas' means in the assembly that has learned the five Nikāyas, beginning with the Dīgha Nikāya. 'I will expound' means I will explain. 'The golden drum' means the excellent drum. 'Of which teachers is this the learning?' The intention is: 'Of which teachers is this the learning? By what method is it to be explained?' 'The teachers' path' means the teachers' way of discourse. 'Of one's own teachers' means of teachers suitable to teach oneself. 'Because all the Tipiṭaka learning is well-decided in this person, he is called a sabbapariyattiko'; the meaning is a tepiṭako. Seated on a chair, he descended from there and sat on the ground on a reed mat. 'Of one who has gone' means of one who has gone by the going of practice, one who has seen the truth. 'Having put on the robe' means having put on the robe evenly for the purpose of showing respect to the teacher. Because of the absence of deceit, he is upright. Because of knowing what is cause and what is not cause, he is discerning.

Pothujjanikāti puthujjane bhavā. Dupparihārā bahuparissayatāya. Tathā hissā uttānaseyyakadārako, taruṇasassañca nidassitaṃ. Vipassanāya palibodho samathayānikassa, na vipassanāyānikassa. Yebhuyyena hi jhānalābhī samathayānikova hoti vipassanāsukhato. Itarenāti samathatthikena. Avasesā nava palibodhā.

'Pertaining to a worldling' means that which arises in a worldling. It is difficult to maintain because of having many dangers. Indeed, for this, an infant lying on its back and a tender seedling are given as examples. For one whose vehicle is serenity, it is a hindrance to insight; it is not for one whose vehicle is insight. For, generally, one who has attained jhāna is indeed one whose vehicle is serenity, because of the ease of practicing insight. 'By the other' means by one who desires serenity. The remaining nine are the impediments.

Kammaṭṭhānadāyakavaṇṇanā

An Exposition on the Giver of a Meditation Subject

42. Kammaṭṭhāne niyutto kammaṭṭhāniko, bhāvanamanuyuñjanto. Tena kammaṭṭhānikena. Paricchinditvāti “imasmiṃ vihāre sabbe bhikkhū”ti evaṃ paricchinditvā. Sahavāsīnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. Muducittatanti attani muducittataṃ janeti, ayañca sahavāsīnaṃ cittamaddavajananādiattho “manussānaṃ piyo hotī”tiādinayappavattena mettānisaṃsasuttena (a. ni. 11.15; paṭi. ma. 2.22; mi. pa. 4.4.6) dīpetabbo. Anolīnavuttiko hoti sammāpaṭipattiyaṃ. Dibbānipi ārammaṇāni pageva itarāni. Sabbattha sabbasmiṃ samaṇakaraṇīye, sabbasmiṃ vā kammaṭṭhānānuyoge. Pubbāsevanavasena atthayitabbaṃ. Yogassa bhāvanāya anuyuñjanaṃ yogānuyogo, tadeva karaṇīyaṭṭhena kammaṃ, tassa yogānuyogakammassa ṭhānaṃ nipphattihetu.

42. One engaged in a meditation subject is a kammaṭṭhānika, one who constantly applies himself to development. By that meditator. 'Having determined' means having determined thus: 'All the bhikkhus in this monastery...' Of the bhikkhus dwelling together. 'Gentleness of mind' means one generates gentleness of mind in oneself; and this meaning, beginning with the generation of gentleness of mind towards co-residents, should be shown by the Mettānisaṃsa Sutta, which proceeds by the method beginning 'he is dear to human beings...' He is of unshrinking conduct in right practice. Not even divine objects overwhelm him, how much less other objects. Everywhere, in every duty of a recluse, or in every application to a meditation subject. It should be desired by way of prior association. The application to the development of the practice is yogānuyogo. That very thing, in the sense of what ought to be done, is kamma. The basis of that work of application to the practice is the cause of its accomplishment.

Niccaṃ pariharitabbattāti sabbatthakakammaṭṭhānaṃ viya ekadāva ananuyuñjitvā sabbakālaṃ pariharaṇīyattā anuyuñjitabbattā. Evamādiguṇasamannāgatanti piyabhāvādīhi guṇehi sampannaṃ. Kalyāṇamitto hi saddhāsampanno hoti sīlasampanno sutasampanno cāgasampanno vīriyasampanno satisampanno samādhisampanno paññāsampanno. Tattha saddhāsampattiyā saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṃ, kammaphalañca, tena sammāsambodhiyā hetubhūtaṃ sattesu hitesitaṃ na pariccajati. Sīlasampattiyā sattānaṃ piyo hoti garu bhāvanīyo codako pāpagarahī vattā vacanakkhamo, sutasampattiyā saccapaṭiccasamuppādādipaṭisaṃyuttānaṃ gambhīrānaṃ kathānaṃ kattā hoti, cāgasampattiyā appiccho hoti [V 1.0112] santuṭṭho pavivitto asaṃsaṭṭho, vīriyasampattiyā āraddhavīriyo hoti attahitaparahitapaṭipattiyaṃ, satisampattiyā [M 1.0120] upaṭṭhitassati hoti, samādhisampattiyā avikkhitto samāhitacitto, paññāsampattiyā aviparītaṃ pajānāti. So satiyā kusalākusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ gatiyo samannesamāno paññāya sattānaṃ hitāhitaṃ yathābhūtaṃ jānitvā samādhinā tattha ekaggacitto hutvā vīriyena satte ahitaṃ nisedhetvā hite niyojeti. Tena vuttaṃ “piyo…pe… niyojakoti evamādiguṇasamannāgata”nti.

‘Because it should be constantly maintained’ means because it should be maintained and practiced at all times, not practiced only once like an all-purpose meditation subject. ‘Endowed with such qualities’ means endowed with qualities beginning with being dear. For a good friend is endowed with faith, virtue, learning, generosity, energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. Therein, through accomplishment in faith, he has faith in the enlightenment of the Tathāgata and in kamma and its fruit; thereby he does not abandon the desire for the welfare of beings, which is a cause for perfect full enlightenment. Through accomplishment in virtue, he becomes dear to beings, respected, worthy of esteem, an admonisher, a reprover of evil, an instructor, and one who is patient when corrected. Through accomplishment in learning, he becomes a speaker of profound discourses connected with the truths, dependent origination, and so on. Through accomplishment in generosity, he is of few wishes, content, secluded, and unentangled. Through accomplishment in energy, he is of aroused energy in the practice for his own welfare and the welfare of others. Through accomplishment in mindfulness, he is of established mindfulness; through accomplishment in concentration, he is undistracted, with a concentrated mind; through accomplishment in wisdom, he understands without distortion. He, with mindfulness, while thoroughly investigating the destinations of wholesome and unwholesome states, with wisdom knows as it really is what is for the welfare and non-welfare of beings; with concentration, having become one-pointed in mind therein, with energy, he restrains beings from what is not for their welfare and urges them towards what is for their welfare. Therefore it was said: ‘dear… and so on… one who urges,’ thus endowed with such qualities.

Taṃ pana kalyāṇamittaṃ paramukkaṃsagataṃ dassetuṃ “mamaṃ hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Kārakabhāvaṃ yogakammassa. Pakāseti attānaṃ paṭipattiyā amoghabhāvadassanena samuttejanāya, sampahaṃsanāya ca, nanu kathesi paveṇipālanatthanti adhippāyo. Evarūpoti pesalo hutvā bahussuto. Tantidharoti suttadharo tattha kehicipi asaṃhīro. Vaṃsānurakkhakoti buddhānubuddhavaṃsassa anurakkhako. Paveṇipālakoti paveṇiyā ācariyuggahaṇassa anupālako. Ācariyamatikoti ācariyamatiyaṃ niyutto tassā anativattanato. Na attanomatiṃ pakāseti kathetīti na attanomatiko, attano matiṃ paggayha vattā na hotīti attho.

Furthermore, to show that good friend as having reached the highest excellence, 'For me...' and so on was said. The state of being the agent of the work of the practice. He reveals himself—for the purpose of inspiring and gladdening—by showing the unfailing nature of his practice. The intention is: 'Did you not speak for the purpose of protecting the lineage?' 'Of such a kind' means being virtuous and very learned. 'A bearer of the textual tradition' means a bearer of the suttas, unshakable therein by anyone. 'A guardian of the lineage' means a protector of the lineage of the Buddha and his disciples. 'A protector of the tradition' means a guardian of the tradition of the teachers' learning. 'Of the teacher's view' means one who is devoted to the teacher's view, because of not transgressing it. Because he does not proclaim or state his own opinion, he is 'not of his own opinion'; the meaning is that he is not one who speaks extolling his own opinion.

“Pubbe vuttakhīṇāsavādayo”tiādi ekaccakhīṇāsavato bahussutova kammaṭṭhānadāne seyyoti dassanatthaṃ āraddhaṃ. Tattha pubbe vuttakhīṇāsavādayoti “yaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ gahetukāmo”tiādinā vuttakhīṇāsavādikā. Uggahaparipucchānaṃ visodhitattāti uggahetabbato “uggaho”ti laddhanāmāya kammaṭṭhānupakārāya pāḷiyā, tadatthaṃ paripucchanato “paripucchā”ti laddhasamaññāya atthasaṃvaṇṇanāya ca visesato sodhitattā niggumbaṃ nijjaṭaṃ katvā gahitattā. Ito cito ca suttañca kāraṇañca sallakkhetvāti pañcasupi nikāyesu ito cito ca tassa tassa kammaṭṭhānassa anurūpaṃ suttapadañceva suttānugataṃ yuttiñca suṭṭhu upalakkhetvā. Sappāyāsappāyaṃ yojetvāti yassa kammaṭṭhānaṃ ācikkhati, tassa upakārānupakāraṃ yuttiṃ magganena yojetvā, samādāya vā sammadeva hadaye ṭhapetvāti attho. Mahāmaggaṃ dassentoti kammaṭṭhānavidhiṃ mahāmaggaṃ katvā dassento.

The phrase ‘previously mentioned are the arahants and others’ and so on is begun to show that, compared to some arahants, the very learned one is superior in giving meditation subjects. Herein, ‘previously mentioned are the arahants and others’ refers to the arahants and others mentioned by the phrase ‘one who wishes to undertake a meditation subject’ and so on. ‘Because they have purified learning and questioning’ means that the Pāḷi, which is called ‘learning’ because it is to be learned and is beneficial to the meditation subject, and the commentary on the meaning, which is called ‘questioning’ because it inquires into that meaning, have been especially purified, and thus grasped after being made free from entanglement and complexity. ‘Having carefully considered the suttas and reasons here and there’ means having well discerned in all five Nikāyas, from here and there, both the sutta passages appropriate to each meditation subject and the reasoning that accords with the suttas. ‘Applying what is suitable and unsuitable’ means applying, by seeking out the reasoning, what is beneficial or unbeneficial to the one to whom the meditation subject is being taught; or it means properly placing it in the heart after undertaking it. ‘Showing the great path’ means showing the method of the meditation subject as a great path.

Sabbatthāti [M 1.0121] tattha tattha vihāre. Vattapaṭipattiṃ kurumānenāti paviṭṭhakāle āgantukavattaṃ, nikkhamanakāle gamikavattanti yathārahaṃ taṃ taṃ vattaṃ pūrentena. Sabbapārihāriyatelanti sabbesaṃ aṅgānaṃ[V 1.0113], sabbesaṃ vā bhikkhūnaṃ atthāya pariharitabbatelaṃ. Ṭhapemīti anujānāpanaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ sammāvattaṃ paññattanti sambandho. Ekadivasaṃ sāyaṃ vissajjitenāpīti yojanā. Ārocetabbaṃ āgamanakāraṇaṃ. Sappāyavelā sarīracittānaṃ kallasamayo.

‘Everywhere’ means in each and every dwelling place. ‘Practicing the proper conduct’ means fulfilling the duties for incoming bhikkhus at the time of entering and the duties for departing bhikkhus at the time of leaving, fulfilling each duty as appropriate. ‘All oil for maintenance’ means oil to be used for the benefit of all the limbs, or for the benefit of all the bhikkhus. ‘I set aside’ is a word indicating permission. ‘That which is rightly practiced is prescribed’—this is the connection. ‘Even if dismissed in the evening of one day’—this is the construction. The reason for coming should be announced. A suitable time is a time when the body and mind are fit.

Cariyāvaṇṇanā

An Explanation of Conduct

43. Santāne rāgassa ussannabhāvena caraṇaṃ pavatti rāgacariyā, sā sassatāsayādayo viya daṭṭhabbā. Tathā dosacariyādayo. Saṃsaggo sampayogārahavasena veditabbo, yathā “rāgamohacariyā dosamohacariyā”tiādi. Sannipāto ekasantatipariyāpannatāvasena, yathā “rāgadosacariyā rāgadosamohacariyā”tiādi. Imā eva hi sandhāya “aparāpi catasso”ti vuttaṃ. Tathāti yathā rāgādīnaṃ, tathā saddhādīnaṃ saṃsaggasannipātavasena saddhābuddhicariyā saddhāvitakkacariyā buddhivitakkacariyā saddhābuddhivitakkacariyāti. Imā aparāpi catasso. Evanti saṃsaggasannipātavasena. Saṃsagganti saṃsajjanaṃ missīkaraṇaṃ “rāgasaddhācariyā dosasaddhācariyā”tiādinā. Anekāti tesaṭṭhi, tato atirekāpi vā, tā pana asammohantena saṃyuttasuttaṭīkāyaṃ vitthārato dassitāti tattha vuttanayena veditabbā. “Pakatī”ti iminā asati paṭipakkhabhāvanāyaṃ tattha tattha santāne cariyāya sabhāvabhūtataṃ dasseti. Ussannatā aññadhammehi rāgādīnaṃ adhikatā, yato rāgacariyādīnaṃ paccayasamavāye rāgādayo balavanto honti, abhiṇhañca pavattanti. Tāsaṃ vasenāti channaṃ mūlacariyānaṃ vasena chaḷeva puggalā honti. Aññathā anekapuggalā siyuṃ, tathā ca sati adhippetatthasiddhi ca na siyāti adhippāyo.

43. Due to the predominance of lust in one’s mental continuum, the occurrence of conduct is lustful conduct; this should be understood similarly to eternalistic inclinations and so on. The same applies to hateful conduct and so on. Association should be understood by way of suitability for conjunction, as in “lust-delusion conduct, hate-delusion conduct,” and so on. Combination should be understood by way of inclusion within a single continuum, as in “lust-hate conduct, lust-hate-delusion conduct,” and so on. Indeed, it is with reference to these that it is said, “There are another four.” Similarly, just as with lust and so on, so too with faith and so on—through association and combination, there is faith-wisdom conduct, faith-discursive thought conduct, wisdom-discursive thought conduct, and faith-wisdom-discursive thought conduct. These are another four. Thus, it is by way of association and combination. Association means joining or mixing, as in “lust-faith conduct, hate-faith conduct,” and so on. ‘Many’ refers to sixty-three, or even more. However, these are explained in detail in the Sub-commentary on the Connected Discourses, so they should be understood according to the method stated there by one who is not confused. By the word “natural disposition,” it is shown that, in the absence of counteractive development, the conduct in those various mental continuums is of that intrinsic nature. Predominance is the superiority of lust and so on over other mental states, due to which, when the conditions for lustful conduct and so on converge, lust and the like become strong and arise frequently. By way of them, that is, by way of the six root conducts, there are only six types of individuals. Otherwise, there would be many types of individuals, and if that were so, the intended purpose would not be achieved—this is the intention.

Saddhā balavatī hoti rāgussanne santāne tadanuguṇassa dhammassa niyogato adhikabhāvasambhavato. Tenāha “rāgassa āsannaguṇattā”ti, sinehapariyesanāpariccajanehi sabhāgadhammattāti attho. Sabhāgo hi dūrepi āsanneyevāti sabhāgatālakkhaṇamidha āsannaggahaṇaṃ. Tattha saddhāya siniyhanaṃ pasādavasena akālussiyaṃ alūkhatā[M 1.0122], rāgassa pana rañjanavasena. Saddhāya pariyesanaṃ adhimuccanavasena tanninnatā, rāgassa taṇhāyanavasena. Saddhāya apariccajanaṃ okappanavasena anupakkhandanaṃ, rāgassa abhisaṅgavasenāti evaṃ bhinnasabhāvānampi [V 1.0114] tesaṃ yathā alūkhatādisāmaññena sabhāgatā, evaṃ taṃsamaṅgīnampi puggalānanti āha “rāgacaritassa saddhācarito sabhāgo”ti.

Faith is strong in a mental continuum where lust is predominant, because of the necessary arising of an abundant state of a quality conforming to it. Hence it is said, “because of nearness in quality to lust,” meaning they share a similar nature through affection, seeking, and non-abandonment. For what is similar, even when far, is near; thus, the term ‘nearness’ here indicates the characteristic of similarity. In this context, the affection of faith is its unturbid and non-coarse nature, by way of clarity; for lust, however, it is by way of attachment. The seeking of faith is the inclination towards its object, by way of conviction; for lust, it is by way of craving. The non-abandonment of faith is a plunging into its object, by way of confidence; for lust, it is by way of clinging. Thus, although their intrinsic natures are different, just as they have a similarity through the commonality of non-coarseness and so on, so too do the individuals endowed with them. Therefore, it is said, “The person of faithful temperament is similar to the person of lustful temperament.”

Paññā balavatī hoti dosussanne santāne tadanuguṇassa dhammassa niyogato adhikabhāvasambhavato. Tenāha “dosassa āsannaguṇattā”ti, anallīyanapariyesanaparivajjanehi sabhāgadhammattāti attho. Tattha paññāya ārammaṇassa anallīyanaṃ tassa yathāsabhāvāvabodhavasena visaṃsaṭṭhatā, dosassa pana byāpajjanavasena. Paññāya pariyesanaṃ yathābhūtadosapavicayo, dosassa abhūtadosanijigīsā. Paññāya parivajjanaṃ nibbindanādivasena ñāṇutrāso, dosassa ahitādhānavasena chaḍḍananti evaṃ bhinnasabhāvānampi tesaṃ yathā anallīyanādisāmaññena sabhāgatā, evaṃ taṃsamaṅgīnampi puggalānanti āha “dosacaritassa buddhicarito sabhāgo”ti.

Wisdom is strong in a mental continuum where hatred is predominant, because of the necessary arising of an abundant state of a quality conforming to it. Therefore, it is said, “because of nearness in quality to hate,” meaning they share a similar nature through non-adherence, investigation, and avoidance. Here, wisdom's non-adherence to its object is its unentanglement, by way of understanding its true nature as it is; for hate, however, it is by way of ill-will. Wisdom's investigation is the scrutiny of faults as they actually are; for hate, it is the seeking of unreal faults. Wisdom's avoidance is the fear that is knowledge, by way of disenchantment and so on; for hate, it is casting aside by way of causing harm. Thus, although their intrinsic natures are different, just as they have a similarity through the commonality of non-adherence and so on, so too do the individuals endowed with them. Therefore, it is stated, “The person of intellectual temperament is similar to the person of hateful temperament.”

Antarāyakarā vitakkāti micchāvitakkā micchāsaṅkappā uppajjanti mohussanne santāne tadanuguṇassa dhammassa yebhuyyena pavattisabbhāvato. Tenāha “mohassa āsannalakkhaṇattā”ti, anavaṭṭhānacañcalabhāvehi sabhāgadhammattāti attho. Tattha vitakkassa anavaṭṭhānaṃ parikappavasena savipphāratāya, mohassa sammūḷhatāvasena byākulatāya. Tathā vitakkassa lahuparivitakkanena tadaṅgacalatāya cañcalatā, mohassa anogāḷhatāyāti evaṃ bhinnasabhāvānampi tesaṃ yathā anavaṭṭhānādisāmaññena sabhāgatā, evaṃ taṃsamaṅgīnampi puggalānanti āha “mohacaritassa vitakkacarito sabhāgo”ti.

Obstructive thoughts, that is, wrong thoughts and wrong intentions, arise in a continuum where delusion is abundant, due to the prevalence of a state that is in accordance with it. Therefore, it is said, 'because of its nearness in characteristic to delusion,' the meaning of which is: because of being a similar phenomenon through the states of instability and agitation. Therein, the instability of thought is due to its expansiveness by way of conceptualizing, while that of delusion is due to its confusion by way of bewilderment. Likewise, the agitation of thought is due to its fickleness in swift thinking, while that of delusion is due to its non-penetration. Thus, just as they, although having different natures, are similar through the commonality of instability and so on, so too are the persons endowed with them. Therefore, it is said, 'the discursive character is similar to the deluded character'.

Taṇhā rāgoyeva sabhāvato, tasmā rāgacariyāvinimuttā taṇhācariyā natthīti attho. Taṃsampayuttoti tena rāgena sampayutto, dosādayo viya tena vippayutto natthīti adhippāyo. Tadubhayanti taṇhāmānadvayaṃ. Nātivattatīti sabhāvato, sampayogavasena ca na atikkamitvā vaṭṭati. Kāmañcettha yathā rāgadosehi sampayogavasena saha [M 1.0123] vattamānassapi mohassa ussannatāvasena visuṃ cariyābhāvo, na kevalaṃ mohasseva, tathā saddhābuddhivitakkānaṃ. Evaṃ rāgena satipi sampayoge mānassāpi visuṃ cariyābhāvo yutto siyā, evaṃ santepi rāgapaṭighamānadiṭṭhivicikicchāvijjānaṃ viya anusayaṭṭho imesaṃ rāgādīnaṃyeva āveṇiko cariyaṭṭhoti, nattheva mānacariyā. Yato cariyā “pakatī”ti vuttā. Pakati ca sabhāvoti. Eteneva diṭṭhiyāpi visuṃ cariyābhāvābhāvo saṃvaṇṇitoti daṭṭhabbo. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana mohacariyantogadhāva [V 1.0115] diṭṭhicariyāti dassetuṃ “mohanidānattā cā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha ca-saddena sampayogaṃ samuccinoti mohanidānattā, mohasampayuttattā cāti.

Craving is by nature just lust; therefore, the meaning is that there is no craving-character separate from the lust-character. 'Associated with it' means associated with that lust; the intention is that, unlike hatred and so on, it is not dissociated from it. 'That pair' refers to the pair of craving and conceit. 'It does not transgress' means it does not occur by transgressing, both by nature and by way of association. And here, just as for delusion, even when it co-exists with lust and hatred by way of association, there is a separate character by way of its predominance—and not only for delusion, but likewise for faith, wisdom, and thought—so too, even though there is association with lust, it might be suitable for conceit also to have a separate character. Even so, just as the meaning of 'underlying tendency' is unique to lust, aversion, conceit, views, doubt, and ignorance, the meaning of 'character' is unique only to these beginning with lust. Therefore, there is no conceit-character. For this reason, character is called 'nature,' and nature is 'intrinsic nature.' By this very reason, it should be understood that the absence of a separate character for views is also explained. In the commentary, however, to show that the character of views is included within the character of delusion, it is said, 'Because it has delusion as its cause, and...' Therein, with the word 'and,' it combines association: because it has delusion as its cause, and because it is associated with delusion.

44. Kiṃ sappāyanti kīdisaṃ senāsanādisappāyaṃ. Pubbāciṇṇaṃ purimajātīsu ācaritaṃ. Ekacceti upatissattheraṃ sandhāyāha. Tena hi vimuttimagge tathā vuttaṃ. Pubbe kirāti kira-saddo arucisūcanattho. Iṭṭhappayogo manāpakiriyā. Subhakammabahulo yebhuyyena sobhanakammakārī. Na sabbe rāgacaritā eva honti, aluddhānampi pubbe iṭṭhappayogasubhakammabahulatāsambhavato, saggā cavitvā idhūpapattisambhavato ca. Etena asati pubbahetuniyāme yathāvuttakāraṇamattena na tesaṃ luddhatā, luddhabhāvahetukā ca rāgacariyāti imamatthaṃ dasseti.

44. What is suitable? What kind of suitable lodging, etc. 'Previously practiced' means practiced in former lives. 'Some' refers to the Elder Upatissa. Indeed, it is stated thus by him in the Vimuttimagga. In 'Formerly, it is said,' the word 'kira' has the meaning of indicating displeasure. 'Application of the agreeable' is doing what is pleasant. 'One with many beautiful actions' is one who generally does beautiful actions. Not all are of a lustful character, because even for those without greed, there is the possibility of having previously applied the agreeable and had many beautiful actions, and because there is the possibility of being reborn here after passing away from heaven. By this, it shows this meaning: in the absence of a fixed prior cause, their greediness and the lustful character caused by the state of greed do not arise merely from the reason as stated.

Itareti chedanādikammabahulā nirayādito idhūpapannā ca na sabbe dosamohacaritā eva hontīti yojanā. Idhāpi yathāvuttakāraṇassa kodhanabhāve, mūḷhabhāve ca anekantikattā dosamohacaritatāyapi anekaṃsikatā veditabbā. Dhātūnaṃ ussadaniyamo yadi pamāṇato, so natthi, atha sāmatthiyato, sopi ekaṃsiko na upalabbhatīti dassento āha “yathāvutteneva nayena ussadaniyamo nāma natthī”ti. Tattha yathāvuttenevāti “dvinnaṃ pana dhātūna”ntiādinā vuttappakāreneva. Dosaniyameti semhādidosādhikatāya rāgādicarito hotīti dosavasena cariyāniyame “semhādhiko rāgacarito”ti vatvā puna “semhādhiko mohacarito”ti, “vātādhiko mohacarito”ti vatvā puna “vātādhiko rāgacarito”ti ca vuttattā tampi dosavasena niyamavacanaṃ pubbāparaviruddhameva. Aparicchinnavacananti [M 1.0124] paricchedakārikāya paññāya na paricchinditvā vuttavacanaṃ, anupaparikkhitavacananti attho.

Others—those with many actions of cutting and so on, and those reborn here from hell and so on—are not all of a hateful and deluded character; this is the connection. Here too, because the afore-mentioned reason is not conclusive with regard to the state of anger and the state of delusion, the state of having a hateful and deluded character should also be understood as not being absolute. Showing that if the fixed rule of predominance of the elements is by measure, it does not exist, or if it is by capacity, that too is not found to be one-sided, he said: 'By the method just stated, there is no such thing as a fixed rule of predominance.' Therein, 'by the method just stated' means by the manner stated beginning with 'of the two elements...'. Regarding the fixed rule by humors: in the fixed rule of character by way of humors—that due to an excess of humors like phlegm, one has a character of lust, etc.—because, after saying 'one with excess phlegm has a lustful character,' it is then said 'one with excess phlegm has a deluded character'; and after saying 'one with excess wind has a deluded character,' it is then said 'one with excess wind has a lustful character,' that statement of a fixed rule by way of humors is also self-contradictory. 'An un-demarcated statement' means a statement spoken without having demarcated it with discriminating wisdom; the meaning is an unexamined statement.

Ussadakittaneti vipākakathāyaṃ gahitaussadakittane. Pubbahetuniyāmenāti purimabhave pavattalobhādihetuniyāmena. Niyāmoti ca tesaṃyeva lobhādīnaṃ paṭiniyato lubbhanādisabhāvo daṭṭhabbo. Lobho ussado etesanti lobhussadā, ussannalobhā, lobhādhikāti attho. Amohussadā cāti ettha ca-saddo sampiṇḍanattho. Tena ye ime lobhussadatādīnaṃ paccekaṃ vomissato ca cuddasa pabhedā icchitā, te anavasesato sampiṇḍeti yathāvuttesu chasveva tesaṃ antogadhattā. Phalabhūtā cettha lobhussadatādayo daṭṭhabbā.

In 'the mention of predominance' means in the mention of predominance taken up in the discussion of results. 'By the fixed rule of prior causes' means by the fixed rule of causes such as greed that occurred in a previous existence. And 'fixed rule' should be understood as the specific intrinsic nature of those very things, greed and so on, such as clinging. 'Greed is predominant in them, thus they are greed-predominant' means those with predominant greed, those with excess greed. Here in 'and not-delusion-predominant,' the word 'ca' has the meaning of grouping. By it, it groups together without remainder those fourteen divisions—which are intended individually and in combination—of the states of greed-predominance and so on, because they are included within the six just mentioned. And here, the states of greed-predominance and so on should be understood as being the result.

Idāni [V 1.0116] taṃ nesaṃ lobhussadatādīnaṃ paccekaṃ vomissakatādiṃ vibhāgena dassetuṃ “yassa hī”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Kammāyūhanakkhaṇeti kammakaraṇavelāyaṃ. Lobho balavāti lobho tajjāya paccayasāmaggiyā sāmatthiyato adhiko hoti. Alobho mandoti tappaṭipakkho alobho dubbalo. Kathaṃ panete lobhālobhā aññamaññaṃ ujuvipaccanīkabhūtā ekakkhaṇe pavattantīti? Na kho panetaṃ evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ “ekakkhaṇe pavattantī”ti. Nikantikkhaṇaṃ pana āyūhanapakkhiyameva katvā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Eseva nayo sesesupi. Pariyādātunti abhibhavituṃ na sakkoti. Yo hi “evaṃsundaraṃ evaṃvipulaṃ evaṃmahagghañca na sakkā dātu”ntiādinā amuttacāgatādivasena pavattāya cetanāya sampayutto alobho, so sammadeva lobhaṃ pariyādātuṃ na sakkoti. Dosamohānaṃ anuppattiyā, tādisapaccayalābhena ca adosāmohā balavanto. Tasmāti lobhādosāmohānaṃ balavabhāvato, alobhadosamohānañca dubbalabhāvatoti vuttameva kāraṇaṃ paccāmasati. Soti taṃsamaṅgīpuggalo. Tena kammenāti tena lobhādiupanissayavatā kusalakammunā. Sukhasīloti sakhilo. Tamevatthaṃ “akkodhano”ti pariyāyena vadati.

Now, to show by way of distinction the predominance of greed and so forth in them, whether individually or in combination, the passage beginning 'yassa hī' is commenced. 'Kammāyūhanakkhaṇe' means at the time of performing kamma. 'Lobho balavā' means greed is strong, being excessive by its potency due to the combination of conditions appropriate to it. 'Alobho mando' means its opposite, non-greed, is weak. But how can these, greed and non-greed, which are directly opposed to each other, arise in a single moment? This should not be understood as 'they arise in a single moment.' Rather, it is stated thus by considering the moment of craving as belonging to the side of accumulation. This is the method in the remaining cases as well. 'Pariyādātuṃ' means it is not able to overpower. For the non-greed associated with the volition that arises from a lack of free giving, with the thought, 'Such a beautiful, vast, and valuable object cannot be given,' is truly unable to overpower greed. Due to the non-arising of hatred and delusion, and due to obtaining such a condition, non-hatred and non-delusion are strong. 'Tasmā' (Therefore) reviews the very reason that was stated: because of the strength of greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion, and the weakness of non-greed, hatred, and delusion. 'So' (he) refers to the person endowed with that kamma. 'Tena kammena' (by that kamma) means by that wholesome kamma which has greed and so forth as its decisive support. 'Sukhasīlo' means amiable. It states that very meaning by the synonym 'akkodhano' (not wrathful).

Purimanayenevāti pubbe vuttanayānusārena mandā alobhādosā lobhadose pariyādātuṃ na sakkonti, amoho pana balavā mohaṃ pariyādātuṃ sakkotīti evaṃ tattha tattha vāre yathārahaṃ atidesattho [M 1.0125] veditabbo. Duṭṭhoti kodhano. Dandhoti mandapañño. Sīlakoti sukhasīlo.

'Purimanayenevāti' means according to the method previously stated: weak non-greed and non-hatred are not able to overpower greed and hatred, but strong non-delusion is able to overpower delusion. Thus, the meaning of this extended application should be understood appropriately in each respective section. 'Duṭṭho' means wrathful. 'Dandho' means of dull wisdom. 'Sīlako' means of pleasant conduct.

Ettha ca lobhavasena, dosamohalobhadosalobhamohadosamohalobhadosamohavasenāti tayo ekakā, tayo dukā, eko tikoti lobhādiussadavasena akusalapakkheyeva satta vārā, tathā kusalapakkhe alobhādiussadavasenāti cuddasa vārā labbhanti. Tattha alobhadosāmohā, alobhādosamohā, alobhadosamohā balavantoti āgatehi kusalapakkhe tatiyadutiyapaṭhamavārehi dosussadamohussadadosamohussadavārā gahitā eva honti, tathā akusalapakkhe lobhādosamohā, lobhadosāmohā, lobhādosāmohā balavantoti āgatehi tatiyadutiyapaṭhamavārehi adosussadaamohussadaadosāmohussadavārā gahitā evāti akusalakusalapakkhesu tayo tayo vāre antogadhe katvā aṭṭheva vārā dassitā. Ye pana ubhayesaṃ missatāvasena lobhālobhussadavārādayo apare ekūnapaññāsa vārā dassetabbā, te alabbhanato eva na dassitā. Na hi ekasmiṃ santāne antarena avatthantaraṃ “lobho ca balavā, alobho cā”tiādi yujjatīti, paṭipakkhavasena vā hi etesaṃ balavadubbalabhāvo, sahajātadhammavasena [V 1.0117] vā. Tattha lobhassa tāva paṭipakkhavasena alobhena anadhibhūtatāya balavabhāvo, tathā dosamohānaṃ adosāmohehi. Alobhādīnaṃ pana lobhādiabhibhavanato, sabbesañca samānajātiyamabhibhuyya pavattivasena sahajātadhammato balavabhāvo. Tena vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “lobho balavā alobho mando, adosāmohā balavanto dosamohā mandā”ti. So ca nesaṃ mandabalavabhāvo purimūpanissayato tathā āsayassa paribhāvitatāya veditabbo.

And here, by way of greed, hatred, delusion, greed-hatred, greed-delusion, hatred-delusion, and greed-hatred-delusion—thus three singles, three doubles, and one triple—there are seven sections on the unwholesome side itself due to the predominance of greed and so forth. Similarly, on the wholesome side, due to the predominance of non-greed and so forth, there are another seven sections. Thus, fourteen sections are obtained. Therein, by the third, second, and first sections on the wholesome side, which are stated as 'non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion are strong,' the sections of predominant hatred, predominant delusion, and predominant hatred-delusion are indeed included. Similarly, on the unwholesome side, by the third, second, and first sections, which are stated as 'greed, hatred, and delusion are strong,' the sections of predominant non-hatred, predominant non-delusion, and predominant non-hatred-non-delusion are indeed included. Thus, having included three sections each within the unwholesome and wholesome sides, only eight sections are shown. But the other forty-nine sections that should be shown, such as the section of predominant greed and non-greed, arising from the mixture of both sides, are not shown precisely because they are not obtainable. For it is not fitting that in a single continuum, without an intervening state, 'both greed is strong and non-greed is strong,' and so forth. For their being strong or weak is either by way of opposition or by way of co-arisen phenomena. Therein, greed's being strong is, by way of opposition, due to its not being overpowered by non-greed; similarly for hatred and delusion by non-hatred and non-delusion. But the strength of non-greed and the others is from overpowering greed and the rest, and for all of them, their strength is by way of co-arisen phenomena, due to prevailing by overpowering those of a similar nature. Therefore, it is stated in the commentary: 'Greed is strong, non-greed is weak; non-hatred and non-delusion are strong, hatred and delusion are weak.' And their state of being weak or strong should be understood as arising from previous decisive support and from the disposition having been cultivated.

Yo luddhoti vuttoti yo ussadakittane “luddho”ti vutto, ayaṃ idha cariyāvicāre “rāgacarito”ti veditabbo. Duṭṭhadandhāti “duṭṭho, dandho”ti ca vuttā yathākkamaṃ dosamohacaritā. Paññavāti sātisayaṃ sappañño. Yato saddhāvitakkesu vijjamānesupi buddhicaritoti vuccati. Alobhādosānaṃ [M 1.0126] balavabhāvo saddhūpanissayatāya vinā na hotīti āha “aluddhaaduṭṭhā pasannapakatitāya saddhācaritā”ti.

He who is called 'greedy'—that is, he who in the description of predominance is called 'greedy'—should here in the investigation of conduct be understood as 'one of greedy temperament.' 'Duṭṭhadandhā' refers to those who are called 'ill-natured' and 'slow,' who are, respectively, of hateful and deluded temperament. 'Paññavā' means exceedingly wise. Because, although faith and thought are present, he is called 'one of intellectual temperament.' Because the strength of non-greed and non-hatred does not occur without faith as a decisive support, it says: 'Not greedy and not hateful, due to their serene nature, they are of faithful temperament.'

Ayañca nayo sādhāraṇato vuttoti nibbattitapubbahetuniyāmavaseneva buddhicaritādikepi dassetuṃ “yathā vā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha amohaparivārenāti amohaparikkhittena, upanissayato sampayogato ca paññāya abhisaṅkhatenāti attho. Sesapadattayepi eseva nayo. Lobhādinā vomissaparivārenāti ettha lobhamohādinā aññamaññaaviruddhavomissaparivārenāti attho. Avirodho ca yugaggāhavasena appavattiyā veditabbo. Tathā hi saddhānusāridhammānusārigottāni aññamaññampi bhinnasabhāvāneva. Ekaṃsena ca missakacariyāpi sampaṭicchitabbā pubbahetuniyāmena cariyāsiddhito. Tathā ceva ussadakittanaṃ pavattaṃ yathārahaṃ lobhālobhādīnaṃ vipākassa paccayabhāvato. Tenāha paṭisambhidāmagge (paṭi. ma. 1.232) –

And this method is stated generally; therefore, to show that even in the case of the intellectual temperament and so forth it is determined solely by the power of past causes that have produced it, the passage beginning 'yathā vā' was stated. Therein, 'with a retinue of non-delusion' means encompassed by non-delusion; the meaning is 'specially conditioned by wisdom through decisive support and through association.' This is the method in the remaining three terms as well. Here, in 'with a mixed retinue of greed, etc.,' the meaning is 'with a mixed retinue of greed, delusion, etc., that are not mutually opposed.' And the non-opposition should be understood as non-occurrence by way of being taken as a pair. For indeed, the lineages of the faith-follower and the Dhamma-follower are of different natures from each other. And a mixed temperament should also be definitely accepted, because the temperament is established by the determination of past causes. And in that very way the description of predominance proceeds, because of being a condition for the result of greed, non-greed, etc., as is appropriate. Therefore, it is said in the Paṭisambhidāmagga:

“Gatisampattiyā ñāṇasampayutte katamesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ hetūnaṃ paccayā upapatti hoti? Kusalakammassa javanakkhaṇe tayo hetū kusalā tasmiṃ khaṇe jātacetanāya sahajātapaccayā honti, tena vuccati kusalamūlapaccayāpi saṅkhārā. Nikantikkhaṇe dve hetū akusalā tasmiṃ khaṇe jātacetanāya sahajātapaccayā honti, tena vuccati akusalamūlapaccayāpi saṅkhārā. Paṭisandhikkhaṇe tayo hetū abyākatā tasmiṃ khaṇe jātacetanāya sahajātapaccayā honti, tena vuccati nāmarūpapaccayāpi viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayāpi nāmarūpa”nti –

'By the accomplishment of a good destination, associated with knowledge, through which of the eight roots does arising occur? At the moment of the impulsion of wholesome kamma, three wholesome roots are conascent conditions for the volition born in that moment; thus it is said that formations are also conditioned by wholesome roots. At the moment of inclination, two unwholesome roots are conascent conditions for the volition born in that moment; thus it is said that formations are also conditioned by unwholesome roots. At the moment of relinking, three indeterminate roots are conascent conditions for the volition born in that moment; thus it is said that consciousness is also conditioned by name-and-form, and name-and-form is also conditioned by consciousness.'

Ādi[V 1.0118]. Pubbahetuniyāmena ca yathā tihetukassa paññāveyyattiyaṃ, na tathā duhetukassa. Yathā ca duhetukassa itikattabbatā nepakkaṃ, na tathā ahetukassa. Evaṃ lobhussadādayo puggalā rāgacaritādayo hontīti niṭṭhamettha gantabbanti. Yathāvuttamatthaṃ nigamavasena dassetuṃ “evaṃ lobhādīsū”tiādi vuttaṃ.

And so forth. And by the principle of prior causes, just as there is sharpness of wisdom for a tri-rooted person, so it is not for a di-rooted person. And just as there is maturity of wisdom concerning what ought to be done for a di-rooted person, so it is not for a rootless person. Thus, persons in whom greed is prominent, and so forth, are of lustful temperament, and so forth—this is the conclusion to be reached here. To show the meaning as stated by way of a summary, 'Thus, in the case of greed and so forth,' and so forth, was said.

45. Tatrāti [M 1.0127] tasmiṃ pucchāvacane. Nayoti jānananayo. Puggalādhiṭṭhānena vuttopi attho dhammamukheneva paññāyatīti dhammādhiṭṭhānenāha “cariyāyo vibhāvaye”ti. Pakatigamanenāti akittimena sabhāvagamanena. Cāturiyenāti cāturabhāvena siṅgārena. Ukkuṭikanti asamphuṭṭhamajjhaṃ. Khaṇanto viyāti bhūmiṃ khaṇanto viya. Anukaḍḍhitanti pādanikkhepasamaye kaḍḍhanto viya pādaṃ nikkhipati. Tenassa padaṃ anukaḍḍhitaṃ pacchato añchitaṃ hoti. Paribyākulāyāti parito āluḷitāya. Chambhito viyāti vitthāyanto viya. Bhīto viyāti keci. Sahasānupīḷitanti aggapādena, paṇhiyā ca sahasāva sannirujjhitaṃ. Vivaṭṭacchadassāti vinivaṭṭacchadanassa pahīnakilesassa. Idamīdisaṃ padanti bhagavato padaṃ disvā vadati.

45. Herein: in that statement of inquiry. Method: the method of knowing. Although the meaning is stated with a person as the basis, it is understood only by way of the Dhamma; therefore, with the Dhamma as the basis, he said, 'He should explain the modes of conduct.' 'By natural movement': by unartificial, innate movement. 'By elegance': by a state of grace, by adornment. 'Squatting': with the middle part of the body not touching the ground. 'As if digging': as if digging the ground. 'Dragged': at the time of placing the foot, he places it as if dragging it. By that, his foot is dragged, pulled backwards. 'In a very agitated manner': stirred up all around. 'As if stiffened': as if timid. 'As if afraid,' say some. 'Suddenly pressed down': suddenly pressed down with the forefoot and the heel. 'Of one with the covering removed': of one whose covering has been removed, who has abandoned the defilements. 'This footprint is of such a kind': seeing the Blessed One's footprint, he speaks.

Pāsādikanti pasādāvahaṃ. Madhurākāranti iṭṭhākāraṃ. Thaddhākāranti thambhitākāraṃ. Ataramānoti nataramāno, saṇikanti attho. Samodhāyāti sammadeva odhāya avikkhipitvā. Nipajjitvāti kāyapasāraṇalakkhaṇāya nipajjāya seyyāya nipajjitvā sayati niddāyati. Pakkhittakāyoti avakkhittakāyo avaso viya sahasā patitakāyo. Dussaṇṭhānanti virūpasannivesaṃ. Vikkhittakāyoti ito cito ca khittaaṅgapaccaṅgo.

'Inspiring confidence': bringing forth confidence. 'Of sweet appearance': of a desirable appearance. 'Not hurrying': not being hasty; the meaning is 'gently.' 'Having placed it down well': having placed it down properly, without scattering it. 'Having lain down': having lain down in the posture of lying down, which is characterized by stretching out the body, he sleeps, he falls asleep. 'With body thrown down': having a body that is thrown down, like one not in control of oneself, with a body that has fallen suddenly. 'Of bad posture': of an ungraceful arrangement. 'With body scattered': having major and minor limbs thrown here and there.

Samparivattakanti samparivattitvā. Āloḷayamāno vālikākacavarāni ākulayanto.

'Tossing and turning': repeatedly turning over and over. Stirring up and making a mess of the sand and rubbish.

Nipuṇamadhurasamasakkaccakārīti sukosallaṃ sundaraṃ avisamaṃ sābhisaṅkhārañca karaṇasīlo. Gāḷhathaddhavisamakārīti thiraṃ asithilaṃ visamañca karaṇasīlo. Aparicchinnaṃ apariniṭṭhitaṃ.

'One who acts skillfully, sweetly, evenly, and carefully': one who is in the habit of acting with skill, beautifully, evenly, and with special preparation. 'One who acts forcefully, rigidly, and unevenly': one who is in the habit of acting firmly, not loosely, and unevenly. 'Undelimited, unfinished': not brought to a conclusion, or not completed.

Mukhapūrakanti mukhassa pūraṇaṃ mahantaṃ. Arasapaṭisaṃvedīti narasapaṭisaṃvedī. Bhājane chaḍḍentoti bhojanabhājane sitthāni chaḍḍento. Mukhaṃ makkhentoti bahimukhaṃ makkhento.

'A mouthful': a large filling of the mouth. 'Not sensitive to the taste': not experiencing the taste. 'Dropping in the bowl': dropping lumps of food in the food bowl. 'Smearing the mouth': smearing the area outside the mouth.

Kilantarūpo [V 1.0119] viyāti tassa asahanena khedappatto viya. Aññāṇupekkhāyāti aññāṇabhūtāya upekkhāya. Aññāṇasaṅkhātāya upekkhāyāti keci.

'As if weary': as if having reached exhaustion through being unable to endure that object. 'With the equanimity of ignorance': with equanimity that has become ignorance. Some say, 'with equanimity that is reckoned as ignorance.'

Māyādīsu [M 1.0128] santadosapaṭicchadanalakkhaṇā māyā. Asantaguṇapakāsanalakkhaṇaṃ sāṭheyyaṃ. Unnatilakkhaṇo māno. Asantaguṇasambhāvanāmukhena paṭiggahaṇe amattaññutālakkhaṇā pāpicchatā. Santaguṇasambhāvanāmukhena paṭiggahaṇe amattaññutālakkhaṇā mahicchatā. Sakalābhena asantussanalakkhaṇā asantuṭṭhitā. Vijjhanaṭṭhena siṅgaṃ, siṅgāratānāgarikabhāvasaṅkhātaṃ kilesasiṅgaṃ. Attano sarīrassa, cīvarādiparikkhārassa ca maṇḍanavasena pavattaṃ loluppaṃ cāpalyaṃ. Evamādayoti ettha ādi-saddena ahirikānottappamadappamādādayo saṅgayhanti.

Among deceit and so forth, deceit (māyā) has the characteristic of concealing existing faults. Fraud (sāṭheyya) has the characteristic of proclaiming non-existing qualities. Conceit (māna) has the characteristic of haughtiness. Evil desire (pāpicchatā) has the characteristic of not knowing the measure in accepting things, by means of esteeming non-existing qualities. Great desire (mahicchatā) has the characteristic of not knowing the measure in accepting things, by means of esteeming existing qualities. Discontent (asantuṭṭhitā) has the characteristic of not being satisfied with one's own gain. A 'horn' (siṅga) is so called in the sense of piercing; the horn of the defilements is reckoned as the state of elegance and urbanity. Greed (loluppa) and fickleness (cāpalya) are that which proceeds by way of adorning one's own body and requisites such as robes. Here, by the word 'and so forth' (ādi), shamelessness, lack of moral dread, intoxication, heedlessness, and the like are included.

Parāparādhassa upanayhanalakkhaṇo upanāho. Paresaṃ guṇamakkhaṇalakkhaṇo makkho. Parassa guṇe ḍaṃsitvā apanento viya yugaggāhalakkhaṇo paḷāso. Parasampattiusūyanalakkhaṇā issā. Attasampattinigūhanalakkhaṇaṃ macchariyaṃ. Idha ādi-saddena dovacassatāpāpamittatādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo.

Hostility (upanāha) has the characteristic of binding to another's offense. Contempt (makkho) has the characteristic of disparaging others' virtues. Contentiousness (paḷāsa) has the characteristic of rivalry, as if biting and removing another's virtues. Envy (issā) has the characteristic of being jealous of another's fortune. Stinginess (macchariya) has the characteristic of concealing one's own fortune. Here, by the word 'and so forth' (ādi), the inclusion of such things as being difficult to correct and having evil friends should be understood.

Anussāhanaṃ thinaṃ. Asattivighāto middhaṃ. Cetaso avūpasamo uddhaccaṃ. Vippaṭisāro kukkuccaṃ. Saṃsayo vicikicchā. Ayoniso daḷhaggāho ādhānaggāhitā. Yathāgahitassa micchāgāhassa dubbiveṭhiyatā duppaṭinissaggiyatā. Idha ādi-saddena muṭṭhasaccaasampajaññādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo.

Sloth (thina) is lack of striving. Torpor (middha) is the impairment of energy. Restlessness (uddhacca) is the non-pacification of the mind. Worry (kukkucca) is remorse. Doubt (vicikicchā) is uncertainty. Dogmatic adherence (ādhānaggāhitā) is firm grasping in an improper way; it is the difficulty of disentangling and the difficulty of relinquishing a wrongly grasped view. Here, by the word 'and so forth' (ādi), the inclusion of forgetfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and the like should be understood.

Muttacāgatāti vissaṭṭhacāgatā nissaṅgapariccāgo. Yathā māyādayo, tathā pavattā akusalakkhandhā, yathā ariyānaṃ dassanakāmatādayo, tathā pavattā kusalakkhandhā veditabbā.

'Open-handed generosity': the state of giving freely, relinquishment without attachment. Just as deceit and so forth are unwholesome aggregates that have occurred in a certain way, so too the desire to see the noble ones and so forth should be understood as wholesome aggregates that have occurred in a certain way.

Pasādanīyaṭṭhānaṃ nāma vatthuttayaṃ. Saṃvejanīyaṭṭhānāni jātiādīni. Kusalānuyogeti kusaladhammabhāvanāyaṃ. “Evañca evañca karissāmī”ti kiccānaṃ rattibhāge parivitakkanaṃ rattiṃ dhūmāyanā. Tathāvitakkitānaṃ tesaṃ divasabhāge anuṭṭhānaṃ divā pajjalanā. Hurāhuraṃ dhāvanāti ito cito ca tattha tattha ārammaṇe cittavosaggo. Tenevāha “idaṃ pure cittamacāri cārikaṃ, yenicchakaṃ [V 1.0120] yatthakāmaṃ yathāsukha”nti (dha. pa. 326), “cittamassa vidhāvatī”ti (saṃ. ni. 1.55) ca.

The places for inspiration (pasādanīyaṭṭhāna) are the Triple Gem. The places for urgency (saṃvejanīyaṭṭhāna) are birth and so forth. 'Devotion to the wholesome' (kusalānuyoga) is in the cultivation of wholesome states. 'Smoldering by night' (rattiṃ dhūmāyanā) is the pondering over tasks in the night-time, thinking, “I will do this and that.” 'Blazing by day' (divā pajjalanā) is the non-undertaking during the day-time of those tasks thus pondered. 'Running here and there' (hurāhuraṃ dhāvanā) is the release of the mind towards this and that object here and there. Therefore it was said: “Formerly this mind wandered on its journey as it wished, as it liked, as it pleased” (Dhp. 326), and “his mind runs about” (SN 1.55).

Dhammappavattidassanādi [M 1.0129] ca pāḷiyaṃ, aṭṭhakathāyañca anāgatamevāti na sakkā vattunti “sabbākārenā”ti vuttaṃ. Kiñci kiñci āgatampi atthevāti hi adhippāyo. “Na sārato paccetabba”nti vatvā tattha kāraṇaṃ dassento “rāgacaritassa hī”tiādimāha. Appamādavihārinoti tattha vinidhāya bhāvaṃ paṭipajjanena appamādakārino. Bhinnalakkhaṇā iriyāpathādayoti cāturiyena acāturiyena saṇikaṃ, sahasā ca gamanādayo. Na upapajjantīti na yujjanti. Pucchitvā jānitabbanti dhammappavattiādiṃ pucchitvā jānitabbaṃ.

Because it cannot be said that the arising of phenomena, seeing, and so forth are not found at all in the Pāli or the commentary, the phrase 'in every way' was stated. The intention is that something or other has indeed been mentioned. Having said, 'It should not be trusted as authoritative,' and showing the reason therein, he said, 'For one of a lustful temperament,' and so on. 'Those who dwell heedfully' means those who practice heedfulness by setting aside their natural disposition and practicing accordingly. 'Postures, etc., of varied characteristics' means walking and so on, gracefully and ungracefully, slowly and quickly. 'They do not arise' means they are not suitable. 'It should be known by asking' means the arising of phenomena and so forth should be known by asking.

46. Sappāyaṃ hitaṃ, kilesavighātīti attho. Adhotavedikanti aparisuddhaparikkhepavedikaṃ. Bhūmaṭṭhakanti bhūmitaleyeva uṭṭhāpitaṃ uparimatalarahitaṃ. Ekato onatassa pabbatapādassa heṭṭhābhāgo akatabhittibhūmiparikammo akatapabbhāro. Jatukābharitanti adhomukhāhi olambamānamukhāhi khuddakavaggulīhi paripuṇṇaṃ. Oluggavilugganti chinnabhinnaṃ. Ujjaṅgalaṃ lūkhadhūsaraṃ chāyūdakarahitaṃ. Sīhabyagghādibhayena sāsaṅkaṃ. Durūpanti virūpaṃ. Dubbaṇṇanti asundaravaṇṇaṃ, dussaṇṭhānaṃ vā. Jālākārena katapūvaṃ jālapūvaṃ. Sāṇi viya kharasamphassanti sāṇiphalako viya dukkhasamphassaṃ. Bhārikabhāvena, antarantarā tunnakaraṇena ca kicchapariharaṇaṃ. Āṇigaṇṭhikāhatoti āṇinā, gaṇṭhiyā ca hatasobho. Idaṃ rāgacaritassa sappāyaṃ, evamassa kilesasamudācāro na hotīti adhippāyo. Eseva nayo sesesupi.

46. Suitable (sappāya) means beneficial; the meaning is that it destroys defilements. 'With a low railing' (adhotavedika) means having an unclean surrounding railing. 'On the ground floor' (bhūmaṭṭhaka) means erected on the ground level itself, without an upper story. The lower part of a mountain base sloping on one side, with unprepared walls and ground, is an 'unprepared slope' (akatapabbhāro). 'Filled with bats' (jatukābharita) means filled with small bats hanging with their heads down. 'Dilapidated' (oluggavilugga) means cut and broken. 'A wilderness' (ujjaṅgala) is rough and dust-colored, devoid of shade and water. 'Arousing apprehension' (sāsaṅka) due to danger from lions, tigers, etc. 'Ugly' (durūpa) means deformed. 'Of poor color' (dubbaṇṇa) means of unattractive color, or of poor shape. A 'net-cake' (jālapūva) is a cake made in the manner of a net. 'Harsh to the touch like hemp cloth' (sāṇi viya kharasamphassa) means having an unpleasant touch like a hempen board. 'Difficult to maintain' (kicchapariharaṇa) due to its weight and needing to be stitched in between. 'Marred by pegs and knots' (āṇigaṇṭhikāhata) means its beauty is destroyed by pegs and knots. This is suitable for one of a lustful temperament; the intention is that in this way the arising of defilements does not occur for him. This same method applies to the remaining temperaments as well.

Disāmukhanti disābhimukhaṃ, abbhokāsābhimukhanti adhippāyo. Mahākasiṇanti mahantaṃ kasiṇamaṇḍalaṃ. Sesaṃ senāsanādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ mohacaritassa, taṃ dosacaritassa vuttasadisameva.

The term disāmukha means 'facing a direction'; the intention is 'facing an open space.' The term mahākasiṇa means 'a large kasiṇa-disk.' As for the rest that should be said regarding lodgings and so on for one of a deluded temperament, it is just like what was said for one of a hateful temperament.

Vitakkavidhāvanasseva paccayo hoti yathā taṃ āyasmato meghiyattherassa. Darīmukheti pabbatavivare. Parittanti suppasarāvamattaṃ.

It becomes a condition for the very scattering of thoughts, as it was for the Venerable Meghiya. The term darīmukha means 'in a mountain cleft.' The term paritta means 'about the size of a winnowing basket or a pot-lid.'

Pabhedaparicchedato nidānaparicchedato vibhāvanaparicchedato sappāyaparicchedatoti paccekaṃ pariccheda-saddo yojetabbo. Vibhāvanāti “ayaṃ rāgacarito”tiādinā jānanavibhāvanā. Ekaccakasiṇānussatiṭṭhānamattassa [V 1.0121] pasaṅgena kathitattā vuttaṃ “na ca tāva cariyānukūlaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ sabbākārena āvikata”nti.

The word pariccheda should be applied to each individually: 'by way of the section on classification,' 'by way of the section on cause,' 'by way of the section on demonstration,' and 'by way of the section on suitability.' The term vibhāvanā is the demonstration of knowing, such as, 'This person is of a lustful temperament,' and so on. Because only certain kasiṇa and recollection meditation subjects were mentioned in passing, it was said: 'And the meditation subject suitable for one’s temperament has not yet been revealed in every way.'

Cattālīsakammaṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Forty Meditation Subjects

47. Saṅkhātaniddesatoti [M 1.0130] saṅkhātānaṃ “cattālīsāyā”ti saṅkhyāvasena gahitānaṃ uddiṭṭhānaṃ niddesato. “Ettha ettakāni upacārajjhānāvahāni, ettakāni appanājjhānāvahānī”ti upacārappanāvahato. “Ettakāni ekajjhānikāni, ettakāni dukatikajjhānikāni, ettakāni sakalajjhānikānī”ti jhānappabhedato. “Etesu aṅgasamatikkamo, etesu ārammaṇasamatikkamo”ti evaṃ samatikkamato. “Ettakānettha vaḍḍhetabbāni, ettakāni na vaḍḍhetabbānī”ti vaḍḍhanāvaḍḍhanato. Ārammaṇatoti sabhāvadhammanimittanavattabbavasena, calitācalitavasena ca ārammaṇavibhāgato. Bhūmitoti kāmāvacarādibhūmivibhāgato. Gahaṇatoti diṭṭhādivasena gahaṇavibhāgato. Paccayatoti āruppādīnaṃ yathārahaṃ paccayabhāvato. Cariyānukūlatoti rāgacariyādīnaṃ anukūlabhāvato.

47. By 'detailed explanation of the enumerated' is meant: by way of the detailed explanation of those that have been concisely stated, taken up by way of number as 'forty'. By 'conducive to access and attainment': 'Herein, so many are conducive to access jhāna, so many are conducive to attainment jhāna.' By 'the distinction of jhānas': 'So many are conducive to a single jhāna, so many are conducive to two and three jhānas, so many are conducive to all jhānas.' By 'transcendence': 'In these there is the transcending of factors, in these there is the transcending of the object.' By 'developing and not developing': 'Herein, so many are to be developed, so many are not to be developed.' By 'the object': by way of the division of the object according to intrinsic nature, sign, and what is not to be newly designated. By 'the plane': by way of the division of planes, such as the sense-sphere plane and others. By 'grasping': by way of the division of grasping through seeing and so on. By 'condition': by way of being a condition for the formless attainments and so on, as is appropriate. By 'suitability to temperament': by way of suitability for the lustful temperament and so on.

Kammaṭṭhānānīti ārammaṇabhāvena yogakammassa pavattiṭṭhānāni. Catukkajjhānikāti catubbidharūpāvacarajjhānavanto, tesaṃ ārammaṇabhūtāti attho. Catukkanayavasena cetaṃ vuttaṃ. Tikacatukkajjhānikesūti tikajjhānikesu purimesu brahmavihāresu, catukkajjhānikesu ānāpānakasiṇesu. Sesesūti vuttāvasesesu ekavīsatiyā kammaṭṭhānesu.

By 'meditation subjects' is meant: they are the ground for the occurrence of the yogi's practice, by way of being its object. By 'conducive to four jhānas' is meant: possessing the fourfold form-sphere jhānas; the meaning is that these meditation subjects serve as objects for them. This is stated according to the fourfold method. Regarding 'in the subjects conducive to three and four jhānas': this refers to the first divine abodes, which are conducive to three jhānas, and to mindfulness of breathing and the kasiṇas, which are conducive to four jhānas. By 'the rest' is meant: in the remaining twenty-one meditation subjects that were mentioned.

Dibbacakkhunā diṭṭhahadayarūpassa sattassa cittaṃ ādikammiko cetopariyañāṇena paricchindituṃ sakkoti, na itarassāti kasiṇapharaṇaṃ cetopariyañāṇassa paccayo hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “parasattānañca cetasā cittamaññātuṃ samattho hotī”ti. Okāsena paricchinnattāti attano ṭhitokāsena paricchinnattā. Tathā uggahakosallassa sampāditattā paricchinnākāreneva tāni upatiṭṭhanti, tasmā na tattha vaḍḍhanāti adhippāyo. Sace pana koci vaḍḍheyya, na tena koci guṇoti dassento āha “ānisaṃsābhāvā cā”ti. “Tesu panā”tiādinā tameva ānisaṃsābhāvaṃ vivarati. Yasmā vaḍḍhitesu kuṇaparāsiyeva vaḍḍhati, avaḍḍhitepi kāmarāgavikkhambhanā [V 1.0122] hotiyeva, tasmā ānisaṃsābhāvo. Vibhūtāti vipulārammaṇatāya supākaṭā, vaḍḍhitanimittatāya appamāṇārammaṇabhāvena paribyattāti attho.

With the divine eye, a beginner can discern the mind of a being whose heart-basis is visible, but not of another. Thus, kasiṇa-pervasion is a condition for the knowledge of others' minds. Therefore, it is said, "One is capable of knowing the minds of other beings with one's own mind." By 'defined by space' is meant: defined by the space where one is situated. Similarly, because the skill in grasping the sign has been accomplished, they appear in a clearly defined manner. Therefore, the intended meaning is that there is no development in that regard. But if someone were to develop it, no benefit would arise from that. Showing this, he said, "And because of the absence of benefit." By 'Moreover, regarding these...' he explains that very absence of benefit. For when they are developed, only a heap of corpses increases, and even when not developed, the suppression of sensual lust certainly occurs. Hence, there is an absence of benefit. By 'manifest' is meant: very clear due to having a vast object; and because of being a developed sign, it is very distinct due to its object being immeasurable—this is the meaning.

Kevalanti [M 1.0131] sakalaṃ anavasesaṃ. “Pathaviṃ ima”nti vacanaṃ upaṭṭhānākārena vuttaṃ, na nimittassa vaḍḍhanenāti adhippāyo. Lābhittāti sātisayaṃ lābhitāya, ukkaṃsagatavasibhāvatoti attho. Thero hi paramāya vasipattiyā assamaṇḍale assaṃ sārento viya yattha tattha nisinnopi ṭhitopi taṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjateva. Tenassa samantato nimittaṃ vaḍḍhitaṃ viya upaṭṭhāsi. Tena vuttaṃ “sabbadisāsū”tiādi.

By 'entire' is meant: whole, without remainder. The phrase "this earth" is stated in the manner of its appearance, not by way of developing the sign—this is the intended meaning. By 'having obtained' is meant: because of having obtained it exceedingly, because of the state of mastery having reached excellence. Indeed, the Elder, due to having reached supreme mastery, enters that jhāna wherever he sits or stands, just as one would drive a horse in a riding ground. Thus, the sign appeared to him from all around as if it were developed. Therefore, it is said, "in all directions," and so on.

Vuttāti dhammasaṅgahe vuttā. Mahanteti vipule. Ninnathalādivasena hi ekadese aṭṭhatvā samantato gahaṇavasena sakalasarīre nimittaṃ gaṇhantassa taṃ mahantaṃ hoti. Mahante vā sarīre. Appaketi sarīrassa ekadese nimittaṃ gaṇhātīti yojanā. Appake vā khuddake dārakasarīre. Etanti asubhanimittaṃ. Ādīnavanti “asubharāsi eva vaḍḍhati, na ca koci ānisaṃso”ti vuttaṃ ādīnavaṃ.

By 'stated' is meant: stated in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī. By 'great' is meant: extensive. For, when one is not established in one part of the body, such as a low or high place, but grasps the sign in the entire body by encompassing it all around, that sign becomes great. Or, in a great body. By 'small' is meant: one grasps the sign in one part of the body—this is the connection. Or, in the small body of a young child. By 'this' is meant: the sign of foulness. By 'danger' is meant: the danger that is stated as: "Only the heap of foulness increases, and there is no benefit whatsoever."

Sesānipi na vaḍḍhetabbānīti saṅkhepato vuttamatthaṃ upapattito vivarituṃ “kasmā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Picupiṇḍādivasena upaṭṭhahantampi nimittaṃ vātasaṅghātasannissayanti katvā vuttaṃ “vātarāsiyeva vaḍḍhatī”ti. Okāsena paricchinnanti nāsikaggamukhanimittādiokāsena saparicchedaṃ. Vāyokasiṇavaḍḍhane viya na ettha koci guṇo, kevalaṃ vātavaḍḍhanamevāti āha “sādīnavattā”ti. Tesanti brahmavihārānaṃ. Nimittanti ārammaṇaṃ. Na ca tena attho atthīti tena sattarāsivaḍḍhanena pathavīkasiṇādivaḍḍhane viya kiñci payojanaṃ natthi. Pariggahavasenāti apariggahitassa bhāvanāvisayassa pariggahavasena, na nimittavaḍḍhanavasena. Tenāha “ekāvāsadviāvāsādinā”tiādi. Etthāti brahmavihārabhāvanāyaṃ. Yadayanti yaṃ paṭibhāganimittaṃ ayaṃ yogī. Sīmāsambhedeneva hettha upacārajjhānuppatti, na nimittuppattiyā. Yadi evaṃ kathaṃ parittādiārammaṇatā jhānassāti āha “parittaappamāṇārammaṇatāpettha pariggahavasenā”ti, katipaye satte pariggahetvā pavattā mettādayo parittārammaṇā, bahuke appamāṇārammaṇāti attho. Ākāsaṃ kasiṇugghāṭimattā na vaḍḍhetabbanti yojanā. Vakkhati vā yaṃ tena sambandhitabbaṃ. Parikappajameva ārammaṇaṃ vaḍḍhetuṃ sakkā, na itaranti āha “na hi sakkā sabhāvadhammaṃ [V 1.0123] vaḍḍhetu”nti[M 1.0132]. Āruppānaṃ parittaappamāṇārammaṇatā parittakasiṇugghāṭimākāse, vipulakasiṇugghāṭimākāse ca pavattiyā veditabbā. Sesāni buddhānussatiādīni dasa kammaṭṭhānāni. Animittattāti paṭibhāganimittābhāvā.

To explain with reasoning the meaning stated briefly as, 'The remaining should also not be developed,' the words 'why?' and so on are said. Even when the sign appears like a lump of cotton, considering it as dependent on a mass of wind, it is said, 'only the mass of wind increases.' By 'defined by space' is meant: it has boundaries by way of its location, such as the tip of the nose or the sign at the mouth. As in the development of the wind kasiṇa, there is no benefit here; it is merely the development of wind—thus he said, 'because it is disadvantageous.' By 'their' is meant: of the divine abodes. By 'sign' is meant: the object. 'And there is no purpose in that' means: by that development of the mass of beings, there is no benefit whatsoever, as there is in the development of the earth kasiṇa and so on. By 'by way of grasping' is meant: by way of grasping the object of meditation that has not yet been grasped, not by way of developing the sign. Therefore, he said, 'by one dwelling, two dwellings,' and so on. 'Here' means: in the development of the divine abodes. 'Whatever' means: whatever counterpart sign this yogi...
