Tattha “arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno lokavidū”ti imehi padehi phalasampattivasena buddhaguṇā vibhāvitā. “Anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussāna”nti imehi sattūpakāravasena buddhaguṇā pakāsitā. “Buddho”ti iminā phalavasena, sattūpakāravasena ca buddhaguṇā vibhāvitā. “Sugato bhagavā”ti pana imehi padehi hetuphalasattūpakāravasena buddhaguṇā vibhāvitāti veditabbaṃ.

Another method: in brief, the Buddha’s qualities are threefold by way of cause, fruit, and benefit to beings. Therein, by the terms ‘Arahaṃ, Sammāsambuddho, Vijjācaraṇasampanno, Lokavidū,’ the Buddha’s qualities are revealed by way of the attainment of fruit. By the terms ‘Anuttaro Purisadammasārathi, Satthā Devamanussānaṃ,’ the Buddha’s qualities are declared by way of benefit to beings. By the term ‘Buddho,’ the Buddha’s qualities are revealed by way of fruit and by way of benefit to beings. But by the terms ‘Sugato’ and ‘Bhagavā,’ it should be understood that the Buddha’s qualities are revealed by way of cause, fruit, and benefit to beings.

145. Tassāti [M 1.0265] buddhānussatikammaṭṭhānikassa yogino. Evanti “tatrāyaṃ nayo”tiādinā vuttappakārena. Tasmiṃ samayeti buddhaguṇānussaraṇasamaye. Rāgapariyuṭṭhitanti rāgena pariyuṭṭhitaṃ, pariyuṭṭhānappattehi rāgehi sahitaṃ cittaṃ araññamiva corehi tena pariyuṭṭhitanti vuttaṃ, tassa pariyuṭṭhānaṭṭhānabhāvato, pariyuṭṭhitarāganti attho. Yaṃ vā rāgassa pariyuṭṭhānaṃ, taṃ taṃsahite citte upacaritanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etasmiṃ pakkhe rāgenāti rāgena hetunāti [V 1.0250] attho. Ujugatamevāti pageva kāyavaṅkādīnaṃ apanītattā, cittassa ca anujubhāvakarānaṃ māyādīnaṃ abhāvato, rāgādipariyuṭṭhānābhāvena vā onatiunnativirahato ujubhāvameva kataṃ. Atha vā ujugatamevāti kammaṭṭhānassa vīthiṃ otiṇṇatāya līnuddhaccavigamanato majjhimasamathanimittapaṭipattiyā ujubhāvameva gataṃ. Tathāgataṃ ārabbhāti tathāgataguṇe ārammaṇaṃ katvā.

145. ‘Tassa’ refers to the yogī practicing the meditation of recollecting the Buddha. ‘Evaṃ’ means in the manner spoken of beginning with ‘tatrāyaṃ nayo,’ and so on. ‘Tasmiṃ samaye’ refers to the time of recollecting the Buddha’s qualities. ‘Rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṃ’ means assailed by lust; the mind accompanied by lust that has reached the state of assailing is said to be ‘assailed’ by it, like a forest by thieves, because it is the place where that assailing occurs. The meaning is ‘a mind with assailing lust.’ Alternatively, it should be understood that the ‘assailing’ of lust is figuratively applied to the mind accompanied by it. In this case, ‘rāgena’ means ‘because of lust.’ ‘Ujugatam eva’ means it has been made straight, since bodily crookedness and so on have already been removed, and because of the absence of deceit and so on which make the mind crooked; or, because of being free from bending down and rising up due to the absence of the assailing of lust and so on. Alternatively, ‘ujugatam eva’ means it has gone to a state of straightness by having entered the path of the meditation subject, through the removal of sloth and restlessness, and by the practice leading to the middle sign of serenity. ‘Tathāgataṃ ārabbha’ means having made the qualities of the Tathāgata the object.

Iccassāti iti assa. “So bhagavā itipi araha”ntiādinā pubbe vuttappakārena buddhaguṇe anuvitakkayatoti sambandho. Evanti “neva tasmiṃ samaye”tiādinā vuttanayena. Buddhaguṇapoṇāti buddhaguṇaninnā. “Vitakkavicārā pavattantī”ti etena buddhaguṇasaṅkhātaṃ kammaṭṭhānaṃ vitakkāhataṃ, vitakkapariyāhataṃ, punappunaṃ anumajjanañca karotīti dasseti. Pīti uppajjatīti bhāvanāvasena upacārajjhānanipphādikā balavatī pīti uppajjati. Pītimanassa vuttappakārapītisahitacittassa. Kāyacittadarathāti kāyacittapassaddhīnaṃ paṭipakkhabhūtā sukhumāvatthā uddhaccasahagatā kilesā. Paṭippassambhantīti sannisīdanti. Anukkamena ekakkhaṇeti yadā buddhaguṇārammaṇā bhāvanā uparūpari visesaṃ āvahantī pavattati, tadā nīvaraṇāni vikkhambhitāneva honti, kilesā sannisinnāva honti, suvisadāni saddhādīni indriyāni honti, bhāvanāya paguṇatāya vitakkavicārā sātisayaṃ paṭukiccāva honti, balavatī pīti uppajjati, pītipadaṭṭhānā passaddhi savisesā jāyati, passaddhakāyassa samādhipadaṭṭhānaṃ sukhaṃ thirataraṃ hutvā pavattati, sukhena anubrūhitaṃ cittaṃ kammaṭṭhāne sammadeva samādhiyati. Evaṃ anukkamena pubbabhāge vitakkādayo uparūpari paṭupaṭutarabhāvena pavattitvā bhāvanāya majjhimasamathapaṭipattiyā indriyānañca ekarasabhāvena paṭutamāni hutvā ekakkhaṇe jhānaṅgāni uppajjanti. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ bhagavatā –

‘Iccassa’ is ‘iti assa.’ The connection is: for him who is reflecting upon the Buddha’s qualities in the manner previously stated, beginning with ‘That Blessed One is indeed an Arahaṃ….’ ‘Evaṃ’ means in the way spoken of beginning with ‘neva tasmiṃ samaye….’ ‘Buddhaguṇapoṇā’ means inclined towards the Buddha’s qualities. By ‘initial and sustained application occur,’ it shows that one strikes, strikes all around, and repeatedly rubs the meditation subject called ‘the Buddha’s qualities.’ ‘Pīti uppajjati’ means: by way of the development, strong rapture that produces access concentration arises. ‘Pītimanassa’ means of one whose mind is accompanied by rapture of the aforesaid kind. ‘Kāyacittadarathā’ means defilements accompanied by restlessness, which are subtle in state and are the opposite of bodily and mental tranquility. ‘Paṭippassambhanti’ means they settle down. Regarding ‘gradually, in a single moment’: when the development with the Buddha’s qualities as its object proceeds, bringing about progressively higher distinction, then the hindrances are already suppressed, the defilements are already settled, the faculties of faith and so on are very clear. Due to the proficiency of the development, initial and sustained application become exceedingly effective. Strong rapture arises. Tranquility, which has rapture as its proximate cause, arises with special distinction. For one with a tranquil body, the happiness that is the proximate cause of concentration becomes very firm and proceeds. The mind, augmented by happiness, becomes rightly concentrated on the meditation subject. Thus, gradually, in the preliminary stage, initial application and so on, having occurred with progressively greater keenness, become extremely keen due to the practice of the middle serenity of the development and due to the faculties having a single function, and in a single moment the jhāna factors arise. In reference to which it was said by the Blessed One:

“Yasmiṃ[M 1.0266], mahānāma, samaye ariyasāvako tathāgataṃ anussarati, nevassa tasmiṃ samaye rāgapariyuṭṭhitaṃ cittaṃ hoti…pe… sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyatī”ti (a. ni. 6.10).

‘Mahānāma, at the time when a noble disciple recollects the Tathāgata, at that time his mind is not assailed by lust… the mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated.’

Kasmā panettha jhānaṃ appanāpattaṃ na hotīti āha “buddhaguṇānaṃ pana gambhīratāyā”tiādi. Gambhīre hi ārammaṇe gambhīre udake patitanāvā viya samathabhāvanā patiṭṭhaṃ [V 1.0251] na labhati, “gambhīratāyā”ti ca iminā sabhāvadhammatāpi saṅgahitā. Sabhāvadhammo hi gambhīro na paññatti. Nanu ca tajjāpaññattivasena sabhāvadhammo gayhatīti? Saccaṃ gayhati pubbabhāge, bhāvanāya pana vaḍḍhamānāya paññattiṃ samatikkamitvā sabhāveyeva cittaṃ tiṭṭhati. Nanu ca sabhāvadhammepi katthaci appanā samijjhati dutiyāruppajjhānādīti? Saccaṃ samijjhati, tañca kho ekappakāre ārammaṇe, idaṃ pana nānappakāranti dassento “nānappakāraguṇānussaraṇādhimuttatāyā”ti āha. Evampi yathā nānappakāresu kesādikoṭṭhāsesu manasikāraṃ pavattentassa ekasmiṃyeva koṭṭhāse appanāvasena bhāvanā avatiṭṭhati, evamidha kasmā na hotīti? Visamoyaṃ upaññāso. Tattha hi satipi koṭṭhāsabahubhāve ekappakāreneva bhāvanā vattati paṭikkūlākārasseva gahaṇato, idha pana nānappakārena guṇānaṃ nānappakārattā, na ayamekasmiṃyeva guṇe ṭhātuṃ sakkoti bhāvanābalena paccakkhato buddhaguṇesu upaṭṭhahantesu saddhāya balavabhāvato. Teneva hi “adhimuttatāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Yadi upacārappattaṃ jhānaṃ hoti, kathaṃ buddhānussatīti vuttanti āha “tadeta”ntiādi.

Why does jhāna not reach absorption here? To this, it is said, 'Because of the profundity of the Buddha's qualities,' and so on. For in a profound object, like a boat that has fallen into deep water, serenity meditation does not find a footing. And by this term 'profundity,' the state of being an intrinsic nature is also included. For an intrinsic nature is profound, not a concept. Is it not so that an intrinsic nature is grasped by means of a concept derived from it? True, it is grasped in the preliminary stage; but as the meditation develops, the mind, having transcended the concept, abides in the intrinsic nature itself. Is it not so that in some cases of an intrinsic nature, such as the second formless jhāna and so on, absorption is accomplished? True, it is accomplished, but that is in an object of a single kind. This, however, is of various kinds. To show this, it is said, 'because of the inclination towards recollecting the various kinds of qualities.' Even so, just as for one who applies attention to the various parts such as the hair of the head, etc., the meditation, by way of absorption, finally settles on just one part, why does it not happen so here? This comparison is unequal. For there, although there is a multiplicity of parts, the meditation proceeds in only one way because of grasping only the aspect of repulsiveness. Here, however, because the qualities are of various kinds, the meditation proceeds in various ways. This yogi is not able to remain on just one quality, because of the strength of faith when the Buddha's qualities become directly present through the power of meditation. For that very reason, it is said, 'because of inclination.' If the jhāna reaches access concentration, how is it called 'recollection of the Buddha'? To this, it is said, 'This...' and so on.

Sagāravo hoti sappatisso, satthu guṇasarīrassa paccakkhato upaṭṭhahanato. Tatoyeva saddhāvepullaṃ aveccappasādasadisaṃ saddhāmahattaṃ. Buddhaguṇānaṃ anussaraṇavasena bhāvanāya pavattattā sativepullaṃ. Tesaṃ paramagambhīratāya, nānappakāratāya ca paññāvepullaṃ. Tesaṃ uḷārapuññakkhettatāya puññavepullañca adhigacchati. Pītipāmojjabahulo hoti pītisambojjhaṅgaṭṭhānīyattā buddhānussatiyā. Bhayabheravasaho buddhaguṇārammaṇāya satiyā bhayabheravābhibhavanato. Tenāha bhagavā “anussaretha sambuddhaṃ, bhayaṃ tumhāka no siyā”ti (saṃ. ni. 1.249 thokaṃ visadisaṃ). Dukkhādhivāsanasamattho buddhānussatiyā sarīradukkhassa padumapalāse udakassa viya vinivaṭṭanato[M 1.0267]. Saṃvāsasaññanti sahavāsasaññaṃ. Buddhabhūmiyaṃ cittaṃ namati buddhaguṇānaṃ mahantabhāvassa paccakkhato upaṭṭhānato. Buddhānussatibhāvanāya sabbadā buddhaguṇānaṃ citte viparivattanato vuttaṃ “sammukhā satthāraṃ passato viyā”ti. Uttari appaṭivijjhantoti imāya bhāvanāya upari taṃ adhiṭṭhānaṃ katvā saccāni appaṭivijjhanto. Sugatiparāyaṇoti sugatisamparāyo.

He becomes reverent and respectful because of the direct appearance of the Teacher's body of qualities. Therefore, he attains an abundance of faith, a greatness of faith similar to unwavering confidence. Because the meditation proceeds by way of recollecting the Buddha's qualities, he attains an abundance of mindfulness. Because of their supreme profundity and their various kinds, he attains an abundance of wisdom. Because they are an excellent field of merit, he also attains an abundance of merit. He becomes abundant in rapture and gladness because the recollection of the Buddha is a basis for the enlightenment factor of rapture. He is able to withstand fear and terror because mindfulness that has the Buddha's qualities as its object overcomes fear and terror. Therefore the Blessed One said: 'Recollect the Sambuddha, and fear will not be yours.' He becomes capable of enduring suffering because, through the recollection of the Buddha, bodily suffering rolls off like water from a lotus leaf. 'Perception of living together' means the perception of dwelling together. His mind inclines towards the state of a Buddha because of the direct appearance of the greatness of the Buddha's qualities. Because, through the meditation on the recollection of the Buddha, the Buddha's qualities are constantly revolving in the mind, it is said: 'as if seeing the Teacher face to face.' 'Not penetrating further' means: not penetrating the truths higher than this meditation, having made it a foundation. 'Bound for a happy destiny' means having a happy destiny as his future destination.

Appamādanti appamajjanaṃ sakkaccaṃ anuyogaṃ. Kayirāthāti kareyya. Sumedhasoti sundarapañño[V 1.0252]. Evaṃ mahānubhāvāyāti vuttappakārena nīvaraṇavikkhambhanādisamatthena satthari sagāravabhāvādihetubhūtena mahatā sāmatthiyena samannāgatāya.

'Heedfulness' means non-negligence, respectful application. 'Kayirātha' means 'kareyya' (one should do). 'Sumedhaso' means 'one with good wisdom.' 'Thus of great power' means: endowed with great capability, which, in the manner described, is able to suppress the hindrances, etc., and is the cause for the state of reverence towards the Teacher, etc.

2. Dhammānussatikathāvaṇṇanā

2. Exposition of the Discourse on the Recollection of the Dhamma

146. Dhammānussatinti ettha padattho, sabhāvattho ca ādito vuttoyevāti taṃ anāmasitvā bhāvanāvidhānameva dassetuṃ “dhammānussatiṃ bhāvetukāmenāpī”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Kasmā panettha buddhānussatiyaṃ viya “aveccappasādasamannāgatenā”ti na vuttaṃ. Nanu etā paṭipāṭiyā cha anussatiyo ariyasāvakānaṃ vasena desanaṃ āruḷhāti? Saccametaṃ, evaṃ santepi “parisuddhasīlādiguṇānaṃ puthujjanānampi ijjhantī”ti dassanatthaṃ “aveccappasādasamannāgatenā”ti idha na vuttaṃ, ariyasāvakānaṃ pana sukhena ijjhantīti. Tathāpi pāḷiyaṃ āgatattā ca buddhānussatiniddese vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ, ayañca vicāro parato āgamissateva.

146. Regarding 'Recollection of the Dhamma,' here the meaning of the word and the intrinsic meaning have already been stated at the beginning. Therefore, without touching upon that, in order to show only the method of cultivation, the passage beginning 'One who wishes to develop the recollection of the Dhamma...' is started. Why is it not stated here, as in the recollection of the Buddha, 'endowed with unwavering confidence'? Is it not so that these six recollections, in sequence, are taught with reference to noble disciples? This is true. Even so, in order to show that 'they are accomplished even by worldlings who possess qualities such as completely pure virtue,' the phrase 'endowed with unwavering confidence' is not stated here. For noble disciples, however, they are accomplished with ease. Nevertheless, because it is found in the Pāḷi, it was stated in the exposition on the recollection of the Buddha—thus it should be understood. And this investigation will indeed come up later.

147. Pariyattidhammopīti pi-saddena lokuttaradhammaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Itaresūti sandiṭṭhikādipadesu. Lokuttaradhammovāti avadhāraṇaṃ nippariyāyena sandiṭṭhikādiatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, pariyāyato panete pariyattidhammepi sambhavanteva. Tathā hi pariyattidhammo bahussutena āgatāgamena paramena satinepakkena samannāgatena paññavatā ādikalyāṇatādivisesato sayaṃ daṭṭhabboti sandiṭṭhiko. Ācariyapayirupāsanāya vinā na labbhāti ce? Lokuttaradhammepi samāne kalyāṇamittasannissayeneva sijjhanato, tathā satthusandassanepi. “Sandiṭṭhiyā jayatī”ti ayaṃ panattho titthiyanimmaddane nippariyāyatova labbhati[M 1.0268], kilesajaye pariyāyato paramparāhetubhāvato. “Sandiṭṭhaṃ arahatī”ti ayampi attho labbhateva, sabbaso saṃkilesadhammānaṃ pahānaṃ, vodānadhammānaṃ paribrūhanañca uddissa pavattattā. Ayañca attho “ye kho tvaṃ, gotami, dhamme jāneyyāsi, ime dhammā sarāgāya saṃvattanti no virāgāya, saññogāya saṃvattanti no visaññogāya, saupādānāya saṃvattanti no anupādānāya. Ekaṃsena, gotami, dhāreyyāsi ‘neso dhammo, neso vinayo, netaṃ satthusāsana’”nti (cūḷava. 406; a. ni. 8.53), “dhammāpi vo, bhikkhave, pahātabbā, pageva adhammā”ti (ma. ni. 1.240) ca evamādīhi suttapadehi vibhāvetabbo. Akālikādhigamupāyatāya akāliko. Vijjamānatāparisuddhatāhi ehipassavidhiṃ arahatīti ehipassiko. Tato eva vaṭṭadukkhanittharaṇatthikehi [V 1.0253] attano citte upanayanaṃ, cittassa vā tattha upanayanaṃ arahatīti opaneyyiko. Vimuttāyatanasīse ṭhatvā paricayena sammadeva atthavedaṃ, dhammavedañca labhantehi paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhīti. Evaṃ sandiṭṭhikādipadesu pariyattidhammampi pakkhipitvā manasikāro yujjateva.

147. In the phrase 'the Dhamma of learning also' (Pariyattidhammopi), the particle ‘pi’ includes the supramundane Dhamma. ‘In other cases’ refers to the terms such as ‘directly visible’. ‘The supramundane Dhamma alone’ is an exclusive statement made directly with reference to the meaning of ‘directly visible’, etc. Figuratively, however, these meanings are also possible in the Dhamma of learning. For indeed, the Dhamma of learning is ‘directly visible’ (sandiṭṭhika) because it is to be seen for oneself—by way of its special qualities such as being good in the beginning—by a wise person who is learned, has mastered the scriptures, and is endowed with supreme mindfulness and maturity. If it is asked, ‘Is it not unattainable without attending on a teacher?’ That is the same for the supramundane Dhamma as well, because it is accomplished only through reliance on a good friend; likewise in seeing the Teacher. The meaning ‘one conquers through direct insight’ (sandiṭṭhiyā jayati) is obtained directly in the crushing of heretics; it is obtained figuratively in the conquering of defilements, because it is a cause in a causal sequence. The meaning ‘it is worthy of being seen for oneself’ (sandiṭṭhaṃ arahatī) is also attainable, because it proceeds with the aim of completely abandoning defiling states and cultivating purifying states. And this meaning should be clarified by such sutta passages as: ‘Gotami, if you know that these qualities lead to passion, not dispassion; to bondage, not liberation; to clinging, not non-clinging... you should definitely conclude, “This is not the Dhamma, this is not the Vinaya, this is not the Teacher’s instruction”’, and ‘Bhikkhus, even the Dhamma should be abandoned, how much more so the non-Dhamma’. It is ‘timeless’ (akālika) because it is a means for the attainment of the timeless. It is ‘inviting inspection’ (ehipassika) because, due to its existence and its thorough purity, it is worthy of the exhortation ‘come and see’. For that very reason, it is ‘leading inwards’ (opaneyyiko) because it is worthy of being brought into one’s own mind by those who desire to escape from the suffering of the round, or of the mind being brought to it. It is ‘to be known individually by the wise’ (paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhi) who, standing on the summit which is the ground of liberation, through practice, rightly obtain joy in the meaning and joy in the Dhamma. Thus, having included the Dhamma of learning in the terms such as ‘directly visible’, attention is indeed appropriate.

Sāti gāthā. Samantabhadrakattāti sabbabhāgehi sundarattā. Dhammassāti sāsanadhammassa. Kiñcāpi avayavavinimutto samudāyo nāma paramatthato koci natthi, yesu pana avayavesu samudāyarūpena avekkhitesu “gāthā”ti samaññā, taṃ tato bhinnaṃ viya katvā saṃsāmivohāraṃ āropetvā dassento “paṭhamena pādena ādikalyāṇā”tiādimāha. “Ekānusandhika”nti idaṃ nātibahuvibhāgaṃ yathānusandhinā ekānusandhikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, itarassa pana teneva desetabbadhammavibhāgena ādimajjhapariyosānabhāgā labbhantīti. Nidānenāti kāladesadesakaparisādiapadisanalakkhaṇena nidānaganthena. Nigamanenāti “idamavocā”tiādikena (saṃ. ni. 1.249), “iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti (a. ni. 10.27) vā yathāvuttatthanigamanena.

The verse in the Sāti Sutta. ‘Samantabhadraka’ means being beautiful in all parts. ‘Of the Dhamma’ refers to the Dhamma of the Dispensation. Although, in an ultimate sense, there is no such thing as an aggregate separate from its parts, nevertheless, when certain parts are viewed as an aggregate, the term ‘verse’ is conventionally applied. Making it as if distinct from those parts, and applying the conventional usage of possessor and possessed, the commentator, wishing to show this, said, ‘With the first line, it is good in the beginning,’ and so on. ‘With a single connection’ (ekānusandhika) is said with reference to a sutta that is not very divided and has a single, sequential connection. For another kind of sutta, however, the beginning, middle, and end parts are obtained by the very division of the Dhamma to be taught. ‘By the introduction’ means by the introductory composition which has the characteristic of indicating the time, place, speaker, audience, etc. ‘By the conclusion’ refers to phrases like ‘Thus he spoke,’ etc., or ‘Thus, whatever was said, this was said in reference to that,’ or by a concluding statement that summarizes the meaning as already stated.

Ayaṃ kathā visesato suttapiṭakasaṃvaṇṇanāti katvā suttapiṭakavasena dhammassa ādikalyāṇādikaṃ dassetvā idāni suttapiṭakavinayapiṭakānaṃ vasena taṃ dassetuṃ “sanidānasauppattikattā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sanidānasauppattikattāti yathāvuttanidānena sanidānatāya, saaṭṭhuppattikatāya [M 1.0269] ca. Veneyyānaṃ anurūpatoti sikkhāpadapaññattiyā, dhammadesanāya ca taṃtaṃsikkhāpadabhāvena paññāpiyamānassa veneyyajjhāsayānurūpaṃ pavattiyamānassa anurūpato. Atthassāti desiyamānassa ca sīlādiatthassa. “Taṃ kissa hetu (saṃ. ni. 1.249)? Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave”tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 3.95) tattha tattha hetūpamāgahaṇena hetudāharaṇayuttato.

This treatise is especially a commentary on the Sutta Piṭaka. Having shown the Dhamma's quality of being 'good in the beginning', etc., by way of the Sutta Piṭaka, now, in order to show it by way of both the Sutta Piṭaka and the Vinaya Piṭaka, it is said, 'because it has an introduction and an occasion of arising,' and so on. Therein, 'because it has an introduction and an occasion of arising' means because of having an introduction as previously stated, and because of having an occasion of arising. ‘Because of its suitability for those to be trained’ refers to its suitability to the disposition of those to be trained, by way of the laying down of training rules and the teaching of the Dhamma, being established as each training rule and proceeding in accordance with their disposition. ‘Of the meaning’ pertains to the meaning of virtue and so on, which is being taught. Because it is endowed with reasons and examples, through the taking up of reasons and similes here and there with phrases such as, ‘For what reason is that? Just as, bhikkhus...’

Evaṃ suttavinayavasena pariyattidhammassa ādimajjhapariyosānakalyāṇataṃ dassetvā idāni tīṇi piṭakāni ekajjhaṃ gahetvā taṃ dassetuṃ “sakalopī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha sāsanadhammoti –

Having thus shown the quality of the Dhamma of learning of being good in the beginning, middle, and end by way of the Suttas and Vinaya, now, taking the three Piṭakas together, in order to show this, it is said, 'the whole,' and so on. Therein, 'the Dhamma of the Dispensation' is –

“Sabbapāpassa [V 1.0254] akaraṇaṃ, kusalassa upasampadā;

Sacittapariyodapanaṃ, etaṃ buddhāna sāsana”nti. (dha. pa. 183; dī. ni. 2.90) –

The non-doing of all evil, the undertaking of the wholesome, the purification of one's own mind—this is the teaching of the Buddhas.

Evaṃ vuttassa satthusāsanassa pakāsako pariyattidhammo. Sīlena ādikalyāṇo sīlamūlakattā sāsanassa. Samathādīhi majjhekalyāṇo tesaṃ sāsanasampattiyā vemajjhabhāvato. Nibbānena pariyosānakalyāṇo tadadhigamato uttarikaraṇīyābhāvato. Sāsane sammāpaṭipatti nāma paññāya hoti, tassā ca sīlaṃ, samādhi ca mūlanti āha “sīlasamādhīhi ādikalyāṇo”ti. Paññā pana anubodhapaṭivedhavasena duvidhāti tadubhayampi gaṇhanto “vipassanāmaggehi majjhekalyāṇo”ti āha. Tassa nipphatti phalaṃ, kiccaṃ nibbānasacchikiriyā, tato paraṃ kattabbaṃ natthīti dassento āha “phalanibbānehi pariyosānakalyāṇo”ti. Phalaggahaṇena vā saupādisesanibbānamāha, itarena itaraṃ, tadubhayañca sāsanasampattiyā osānanti āha “phalanibbānehi pariyosānakalyāṇo”ti.

The Dhamma of learning is the expounder of the Teacher's Dispensation thus stated. It is good in the beginning with virtue, for virtue is the root of the Dispensation. It is good in the middle with serenity and so forth, because they are central to the accomplishment of the Dispensation. It is good in the end with Nibbāna, since after its attainment there is nothing further to be done. In the Dispensation, right practice is by way of wisdom, and of that wisdom, virtue and concentration are the root; therefore, it is said, 'it is good in the beginning with virtue and concentration.' Wisdom, however, is twofold by way of understanding and penetration; encompassing both, it is said, 'it is good in the middle with insight and the paths.' Its completion is the fruit, its task being the realization of Nibbāna; showing that beyond this there is nothing more to be done, it is said, 'it is good in the end with the fruit and Nibbāna.' Alternatively, by the taking of 'fruit', Nibbāna with residue remaining is indicated; by the other, that without residue. And since both are the conclusion of the accomplishment of the Dispensation, it is said, 'it is good in the end with the fruit and Nibbāna.'

Buddhassa subodhitā sammāsambuddhatā, tāya ādikalyāṇo tappabhavattā. Sabbaso saṃkilesappahānaṃ vodānaṃ, pāripūrī ca dhammasudhammatā, tāya majjhekalyāṇo taṃsarīrattā. Satthārā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipatti saṅghasuppaṭipatti, tāya pariyosānakalyāṇo, tāya sāsanassa loke suppatiṭṭhitabhāvato. Tanti sāsanadhammaṃ. Tathattāyāti yathattāya bhagavatā dhammo desito, tathattāya tathabhāvāya. So pana abhisambodhi paccekabodhi sāvakabodhīti tividho[M 1.0270], ito aññathā nibbānādhigamassa abhāvato. Tattha sabbaguṇehi aggabhāvato, itarabodhidvayamūlatāya ca paṭhamāya bodhiyā ādikalyāṇatā, guṇehi vemajjhabhāvato dutiyāya majjhekalyāṇatā, tadubhayāvaratāya, tadosānatāya ca sāsanadhammassa tatiyāya pariyosānakalyāṇatā vuttā.

The Buddha's perfect understanding is Perfect Self-Enlightenment; by that, the Dhamma is excellent in the beginning, because it has that Buddha as its source. The abandoning of defilements in every way, the purification, and the complete fulfillment is the good nature of the Dhamma (dhammasudhammatā); by that, it is excellent in the middle, because it has that Dhamma as its essence. The practice in the way instructed by the Teacher is the good practice of the Sangha (saṅghasuppaṭipatti); by that, it is excellent in the end, because by that the Dispensation is well-established in the world. The text is the Dhamma of the Dispensation. 'For the state of being so' means: the Dhamma was taught by the Blessed One for the state of being as it is, for the state of being such. That, however, is threefold: supreme enlightenment, individual enlightenment, and disciple enlightenment, because apart from these, there is no attainment of Nibbāna. Among these, through the first enlightenment, the excellence in the beginning is stated, because of its supremacy in all qualities and because of its being the root of the other two enlightenments. Through the second, the excellence in the middle is stated, because of the intermediate nature of its qualities. And through the third, the excellence in the end of the Dhamma of the Dispensation is stated, because of its inferiority to both of those and because it has that as its conclusion.

Esoti sāsanadhammo. Nīvaraṇavikkhambhanatoti vimuttāyatanasīse ṭhatvā saddhammaṃ suṇantassa nīvaraṇānaṃ vikkhambhanasambhavato. Vuttaṃ hetaṃ –

This is the Dhamma of the Dispensation. 'Because of the suppression of the hindrances' means: because for one who, having stood in the supreme basis for liberation, listens to the true Dhamma, the suppression of the hindrances is possible. For this has been said:

“Yathā yathāvuso, bhikkhuno satthā vā dhammaṃ deseti, aññataro vā garuṭṭhāniyo sabrahmacārī[V 1.0255], tathā tathā so tattha labhati atthavedaṃ labhati dhammaveda”nti (a. ni. 5.26).

‘Friends, in whatever way the Teacher teaches the Dhamma to a bhikkhu, or another fellow monk in the position of a teacher does, in that very way he, in regard to that Dhamma, experiences the inspiration of the meaning and experiences the inspiration of the Dhamma.’

“Yasmiṃ, bhikkhave, samaye ariyasāvako ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti, pañcassa nīvaraṇāni tasmiṃ samaye pahīnāni hontī”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.219) –

‘Monks, at the time when a noble disciple listens to the Dhamma with an attentive ear, at that time the five hindrances are abandoned for him.’

Ca ādi. Samathavipassanāsukhāvahanatoti samathasukhassa ca vipassanāsukhassa ca sampādanato. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘Because it brings the bliss of serenity and insight’ means: because it accomplishes the bliss of serenity and the bliss of insight. And this was also said:

“So vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukha”ntiādi (dī. ni. 1.279; ma. ni. 2.138).

‘Quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, he enters and abides in the first jhāna, which has initial and sustained thought, with joy and bliss born of seclusion...’

Tathā –

Likewise:

“Yato yato sammasati, khandhānaṃ udayabbayaṃ;

Labhatī pītipāmojjaṃ, amataṃ taṃ vijānataṃ;

Amānusī ratī hoti, sammā dhammaṃ vipassato”ti ca. (dha. pa. 374, 373);

‘Whenever one comprehends the arising and passing away of the aggregates, one obtains joy and gladness. That is the Deathless for those who know. For one who rightly sees the Dhamma with insight, there is a non-human delight.’

Tathāpaṭipannoti yathā samathavipassanāsukhaṃ āvahati, yathā vā satthārā anusiṭṭhaṃ, tathā paṭipanno sāsanadhammo. Tādibhāvāvahanatoti chaḷaṅgupekkhāvasena iṭṭhādīsu tādibhāvassa lokadhammehi anupalepassa āvahanato. Esa bhagavā vuttanayena tividhakalyāṇaṃ dhammaṃ desento yaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ, maggabrahmacariyañca pakāseti, taṃ yathānurūpaṃ atthasampattiyā sātthaṃ, byañjanasampattiyā sabyañjananti yojanā.

‘Practiced accordingly’ means: the Dhamma of the Dispensation is practiced in such a way that it brings the bliss of serenity and insight, or as it was instructed by the Teacher. ‘Because of bringing about the state of being such’ means: because of bringing about, by means of six-factored equanimity, the state of being ‘such’ in regard to the desirable and so on, and non-adherence to worldly conditions. This Blessed One, while teaching the Dhamma with threefold excellence in the manner stated, reveals the holy life of the Dispensation and the holy life of the Path. That, according to what is appropriate, is meaningful (sāttha) due to the accomplishment of the meaning, and is well-phrased (sabyañjana) due to the accomplishment of the letter. This is the connection.

Tattha [M 1.0271] avisesena tisso sikkhā, sakalo ca tantidhammo sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “katamesānaṃ kho, bhante, buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ brahmacariyaṃ naciraṭṭhitikaṃ ahosī”tiādi (pārā. 18). Sabbasikkhānaṃ maṇḍabhūtasikkhattayasaṅgahito ariyamaggo maggabrahmacariyaṃ. Yaṃ sandhāya [V 1.0256] vuttaṃ “khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīya”nti (mahāva. 23; saṃ. ni. 5.186). Yathānurūpanti yathārahaṃ. Sikkhattayasaṅgahaṃ hi sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ atthasampattiyā sātthaṃ. Maggabrahmacariye vattabbameva natthi. Atthasampattiyāti sampannatthatāya. Sampattiattho hi idha saha-saddo. Itaraṃ pana yathāvuttenatthena sātthaṃ, sabyañjanañca. Ye panettha “vacanasabhāvaṃ sātthaṃ, atthasabhāvaṃ sabyañjana”nti vibhajitvā vadanti, taṃ na sundaraṃ, tathā vibhattassa pariyattidhammassa abhāvato. Saddatthā hi abhinnarūpā viya hutvā viniyogaṃ gacchanti. Tathā hi nesaṃ lokiyāmissībhāvaṃ paṭijānanti. Satipi vā bhede “sabyañjana”nti ettha yadi tulyayogo adhippeto “saputto āgato”tiādīsu viya, evaṃ sati “atthapaṭisaraṇā, bhikkhave, hotha, mā byañjanapaṭisaraṇā”ti atthappadhānavādo bādhito siyā, atha vijjamānatāmattaṃ “salomako sapakkhako”tiādīsu viya byañjanasampatti aggahitā siyā. Tasmā aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayeneva attho gahetabbo.

Therein, without distinction, the three trainings and the entire textual Dhamma are the holy life of the Dispensation. With reference to this it was said: ‘For which Buddhas, venerable sir, was the holy life not long-lasting?’ and so on. The Noble Path, which is the essence of all trainings and is comprised of the three trainings, is the holy life of the Path. With reference to this it was said: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done.’ ‘According to what is appropriate’ means ‘as is fitting.’ Indeed, the holy life of the Dispensation, which is comprised of the three trainings, is meaningful (sāttha) due to the accomplishment of the meaning. Regarding the holy life of the Path, there is nothing at all to be said. ‘Due to the accomplishment of the meaning’ means because of having an accomplished meaning. Indeed, here the prefix 'sa-' has the meaning of ‘accomplishment’ (sampatti). The other part, however—the holy life of the textual Dhamma—is both meaningful and well-phrased for the reason stated. But those who here analyze and say, ‘'sāttha' has the nature of the expression, and 'sabyañjana' has the nature of the meaning’—that is not good, because there is no such division in the scriptural Dhamma. For words and meanings, being as if inseparable, come into usage. Thus, worldly scholars acknowledge their intermingling. Or, even if there is a distinction, if in the phrase ‘well-phrased’ (sabyañjana) an equal connection is intended, as in ‘he came with his son,’ then the teaching that emphasizes the meaning—‘Bhikkhus, take recourse to the meaning, not to the letter’—would be contradicted. Or if merely the fact of its presence is intended, as in ‘hairy and feathered,’ the accomplishment of the letter would not be grasped. Therefore, the meaning should be taken only in the way stated in the commentary.

Sātthaṃ sabyañjananti ettha nettinayenāpi atthaṃ dassetuṃ “saṅkāsana…pe… sabyañjana”nti vuttaṃ. Tattha yadipi nettiyaṃ byañjanamukhena byañjanatthaggahaṇaṃ hotīti “akkharaṃ pada”ntiādinā (netti. 4 dvādasapada) byañjanapadāni paṭhamaṃ uddiṭṭhāni, idha pana pāḷiyaṃ “sātthaṃ sabyañjana”nti āgatattā atthapadāniyeva paṭhamaṃ dassetuṃ “saṅkāsanapakāsanā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha saṅkhepato kāsanaṃ dīpanaṃ saṅkāsanaṃ “maññamāno bhikkhu baddho mārassa, amaññamāno mutto”tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 3.64) viya. Tattakena hi tena bhikkhunā paṭividdhaṃ. Tenāha “aññātaṃ bhagavā”tiādi. Paṭhamaṃ kāsanaṃ pakāsanaṃ. Ādikammasmiṃ hi ayaṃ pasaddo “paññapeti paṭṭhapetī”tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 2.20) viya. Tikkhindriyāpekkhaṃ cetaṃ padadvayaṃ uddesabhāvato. Tikkhindriyo hi saṅkhepato paṭhamañca vuttamatthaṃ paṭipajjati[M 1.0272]. Saṃkhittassa vitthāravacanaṃ, sakiṃ vuttassa puna vacanañca vivaraṇavibhajanāni. Yathā “kusalā dhammā”ti saṅkhepato sakiṃyeva ca vuttassa atthassa “katame dhammā kusalā? Yasmiṃ samaye kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ citta”ntiādinā (dha. sa. 1) vitthārato vivaraṇavasena, vibhajanavasena ca puna vacanaṃ. Majjhimindriyāpekkhametaṃ padadvayaṃ niddesabhāvato. Vivaṭassa vitthāratarābhidhānaṃ, vibhattassa ca pakārehi ñāpanaṃ veneyyānaṃ cittaparitosanaṃ uttānīkaraṇapaññāpanāni. Yathā “phasso hotī”tiādinā (dha. sa. 2) vivaṭavibhattassa atthassa “katamo tasmiṃ samaye phasso? Yo tasmiṃ samaye phasso phusanā samphusanā”tiādinā [V 1.0257] (dha. sa. 2) uttānīkiriyā, paññāpanā ca. Mudindriyāpekkhametaṃ padadvayaṃ paṭiniddesabhāvato. “Paññāpanapaṭṭhapanavivaraṇavibhajanauttānīkaraṇapakāsanaatthapadasamāyogato”tipi pāṭho.

Here, regarding 'with meaning and with phrasing,' in order to show the meaning also by the method of the Netti, it is said: 'making clear... and so forth... with its phrasing.' Therein, although in the Netti the grasping of the meaning of an expression occurs by way of the expression, and thus the terms of expression are listed first, as in 'letter, word,' etc., here in this Pāḷi, however, since it is stated as 'with meaning and with phrasing,' the meaning-terms are shown first in order to demonstrate, and so it is said, 'making clear, making manifest,' etc. Therein, `saṅkāsana` is the showing, the illuminating, in brief, as in: "A bhikkhu who conceives is bound by Māra; one who does not conceive is freed," and so on. For by just that much, it has been penetrated by that bhikkhu. Therefore, he said: "It is understood, Blessed One," and so on. `Pakāsana` is the initial showing. For this prefix 'pa-' occurs in the sense of an initial act, as in "he makes known, he establishes," and so on. And this pair of terms pertains to those with sharp faculties, on account of being a summary statement (uddesa). For one with sharp faculties understands the meaning stated briefly and at the outset. The detailed statement of what is condensed, and the repetition of what is stated once, are `vivaraṇa` (unfolding) and `vibhajana` (analysis). For example, of the meaning stated briefly and only once as "wholesome states," the repetition in detail by way of unfolding and by way of analysis is: "What states are wholesome? At a time when a wholesome mind pertaining to the sense-sphere arises..." and so on. This pair of terms pertains to those with middling faculties, on account of being an exposition (niddesa). The more detailed explanation of what has been unfolded, the making known in various ways of what has been analyzed, and the gladdening of the minds of those to be trained, are `uttānīkaraṇa` (making plain) and `paññāpanā` (making known). For example, of the meaning that has been unfolded and analyzed, as in "there is contact," and so on, the making plain and making known is: "What at that time is contact? That which at that time is contact, touching, thorough touching..." and so on. This pair of terms pertains to those with dull faculties, on account of being a detailed exposition (paṭiniddesa). There is also the reading: "through the conjunction of the meaning-terms: making known, establishing, unfolding, analysis, making plain, and making manifest."

Kathaṃ panāyaṃ pāṭhavikappo jātoti? Vuccate – nettipāḷiyaṃ āgatanayena purimapāṭho. Tattha hi –

But how did this textual variant come about? It is said: The former reading arose according to the method that has come in the Netti Pāḷi. For there—

“Saṅkāsanā pakāsanā,

Vivaraṇā vibhajanuttānīkammapaññatti;

Etehi chahi padehi,

Attho kammañca niddiṭṭha”nti. (netti. 4 dvādasapada) –

"Concise showing, initial showing, unfolding, analysis, making plain, making known; by these six terms, both the meaning and the act are indicated."

Desanāhārayojanāya ca etassevatthassa “saṅkāsanā pakāsanā”tiādinā āgataṃ. Pacchimo pana “paññapeti paṭṭhapeti vivarati vibhajati uttānīkaroti ‘passathā’ti cāhā”ti (saṃ. ni. 2.20) sutte āgatanayena byañjanamattakato. Evañca nesaṃ dvinnaṃ pāṭhānaṃ viseso, na atthato. Tathā hi saṅkhepato “paṭhamaṃ ñāpanaṃ paññāpanaṃ, paṭhamameva ṭhapanaṃ paṭṭhapana”nti imāni padāni saṅkāsanapakāsanapadehi atthato avisiṭṭhāni. Yañca purimapāṭhe chaṭṭhaṃ padaṃ “pakārato ñāpana”nti paññāpanaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ dutiyapāṭhe pakāsanapadena “nibbisesaṃ pakārato kāsana”nti katvā. Yasmā ñāpanakāsanāni atthāvabhāsanasabhāvatāya abhinnāni, sabbesañca veneyyānaṃ cittassa tosanaṃ, buddhiyā ca nisānaṃ yāthāvato vatthusabhāvāvabhāsane jāyatīti. Evaṃ atthapadarūpattā pariyattiatthassa yathāvuttachaatthapadasamāyogato sātthaṃ sāsanaṃ.

And in the application of the Desanāhāra, this very meaning has come by way of "making clear, making manifest," and so on. The latter reading, however, is a matter of mere phrasing, following the method that has come in the sutta: "He makes known, establishes, unfolds, analyzes, makes plain, and says, ‘See!’" And thus the difference between these two readings is one of phrasing, not of meaning. For indeed, since `paññāpana` is 'making known at the outset' and `paṭṭhapana` is 'establishing at the very outset,' these terms are not different in meaning from the terms `saṅkāsana` and `pakāsanā`. And the sixth term in the former reading, `paññāpana`, was stated as 'making known in various ways'; that, in the second reading, is without difference from the term `pakāsana`, which is etymologized as 'showing in various ways'. This is because making known and showing are not different, due to their nature of illuminating the meaning, and because for all those to be trained, the gladdening of the mind and the sharpening of wisdom arises in the illumination of the true nature of the matter. Thus, because the meaning of the Pariyatti is of the nature of meaning-terms, the teaching is 'with meaning' through its connection with the six meaning-terms as stated.

Akkharapadabyañjanākāraniruttiniddesasampattiyāti [M 1.0273] ettha uccāraṇavelāyaṃ apariyosite pade vaṇṇo akkharaṃ. “Ekakkharaṃ padaṃ akkhara”nti eke “ā evaṃ kira ta”ntiādīsu ā-kārādayo viya. “Visuddhakaraṇānaṃ manasā desanāvācāya akkharaṇato akkhara”nti aññe. Vibhattiyantaṃ atthañāpanato padaṃ. Saṅkhepato vuttaṃ padābhihitaṃ atthaṃ byañjetīti byañjanaṃ, vākyaṃ. “Kiriyāpadaṃ abyayakārakavisesanayuttaṃ vākya”nti hi vadanti. Pakārato vākyavibhāgo [V 1.0258] ākāro. Ākārābhihitaṃ nibbacanaṃ nirutti. Nibbacanavitthāro nissesupadesato niddeso. Etesaṃ akkharādīnaṃ byañjanapadānaṃ sampattiyā sampannatāya sabyañjanaṃ.

Here, regarding 'the perfection of letters, words, phrasing, modes, etymologies, and expositions': At the time of utterance, a sound (vaṇṇa) in an uncompleted word is a 'letter' (akkhara). Some say, "A single-letter word is an 'akkhara'," like the letter 'ā' and so on in phrases such as "Ā, so it seems." Others say, "The teaching conceived in the mind of those with purified organs of speech is an 'akkhara' because it is not poured forth (a-kharaṇa) by speech." A 'word' (pada) is that which ends in an inflection and makes the meaning known. 'Phrasing' (byañjana) is that which clarifies the meaning indicated by the words stated briefly; it means a sentence (vākya). For they say, "A sentence (vākya) is a collection of words connected with a verb, indeclinables, and case-qualifiers." A 'mode' (ākāra) is the classification of sentences according to their kind. 'Etymology' (nirutti) is the derivation (nibbacana) indicated by the mode. 'Exposition' (niddesa) is the detailed explanation of the derivation, because it is a complete instruction. Through the perfection, the completeness, of these terms of phrasing, from 'letter' onwards, it is 'with phrasing' (sabyañjana).

Tatrāyamassa atthapadasamāyogo, byañjanasampatti ca – akkharehi saṅkāseti, padehi pakāseti, byañjanehi vivarati, ākārehi vibhajati, niruttīhi uttānīkaroti, niddesehi paññapeti, tathā akkharehi ugghāṭetvā padehi vineti ugghaṭitaññuṃ, byañjanehi vipañcetvā ākārehi vineti vipañcitaññuṃ, niruttīhi netvā niddesehi vineti neyyaṃ. Evañcāyaṃ dhammo ugghaṭiyamāno ugghaṭitaññuṃ vineti, vipañciyamāno vipañcitaññuṃ, niyyamāno neyyaṃ. Tattha ugghaṭanā ādi, vipañcanā majjhe, nayanamante. Evaṃ tīsu kālesu tidhā desito dosattayavidhamano guṇattayāvaho tividhaveneyyavinayanoti. Evampi tividhakalyāṇoyaṃ dhammo atthabyañjanapāripūriyā “sāttho sabyañjano”ti veditabbo “paripuṇṇo, parisuddho”ti ca.

Herein is its conjunction of meaning-terms and perfection of phrasing: with letters, one shows concisely; with words, one shows at the outset; with phrasing, one unfolds; with modes, one analyzes; with etymologies, one makes plain; with expositions, one makes known in detail. Likewise, having opened up concisely with letters, one trains with words the person who understands upon concise opening; having elaborated with phrasing, one trains with modes the person who understands upon elaboration; having guided with etymologies, one trains with expositions the person who is to be guided. And thus this Dhamma, when being opened up concisely, trains the one who understands upon concise opening; when being elaborated, it trains the one who understands upon elaboration; when being guided, it trains the one who is to be guided. Therein, the concise opening is at the beginning, the elaboration is in the middle, and the guiding is at the end. Thus taught in three ways at three times, it dispels the triad of faults, brings the triad of virtues, and trains the threefold group of those to be trained. In this way too, this Dhamma of threefold excellence, due to the completeness of its meaning and phrasing, should be understood as 'with meaning and with phrasing,' and as 'complete and purified.'

Atthagambhīratātiādīsu attho nāma tantiattho. Dhammo tanti. Paṭivedho tantiyā, tantiatthassa ca yathābhūtāvabodho. Desanā manasā vavatthāpitāya tantiyā desanā. Te panete atthādayo yasmā sasādīhi viya mahāsamuddo mandabuddhīhi dukkhogāhā, alabbhaneyyapatiṭṭhā ca, tasmā gambhīrā. Atha vā attho nāma hetuphalaṃ. Dhammo hetu. Desanā paññatti, yathādhammaṃ dhammābhilāpo, anulomapaṭilomasaṅkhepavitthārādivasena vā kathanaṃ. Paṭivedho abhisamayo, atthānurūpaṃ dhammesu, dhammānurūpaṃ atthesu, paññattipathānurūpaṃ paññattīsu avabodho, tesaṃ tesaṃ vā dhammānaṃ paṭivijjhitabbo salakkhaṇasaṅkhāto aviparītasabhāvo. Tepi cete atthādayo yasmā anupacitakusalasambhārehi duppaññehi [M 1.0274] sasādīhi viya mahāsamuddo dukkhogāhā, alabbhaneyyapatiṭṭhā ca, tasmā gambhīrā. Tesu paṭivedhassāpi atthasannissitattā vuttaṃ “atthagambhīratāpaṭivedhagambhīratāhi sāttha”nti atthaguṇadīpanato. Tāsaṃ dhammadesanānaṃ byañjanasannissitattā vuttaṃ “dhammagambhīratādesanāgambhīratāhi sabyañjana”nti tāsaṃ byañjanasampattidīpanato.

In the terms 'profound in meaning,' etc., 'meaning' (attha) is the meaning of the text (tanti). 'Dhamma' is the text. 'Penetration' (paṭivedha) is the true understanding of the text and of the meaning of the text. 'Teaching' (desanā) is the teaching of the text which has been determined by the mind. These, meaning and so forth, are profound because, like the great ocean for hares and other such creatures, they are difficult to enter and a footing is unobtainable for those of weak intellect. Alternatively, 'meaning' (attha) is the fruit of a cause. 'Dhamma' is the cause. 'Teaching' (desanā) is concept (paññatti), the expression of the Dhamma in accordance with its nature, or the explanation by way of forward and reverse order, concise and detailed methods, and so on. 'Penetration' (paṭivedha) is direct understanding (abhisamaya), the comprehension of dhammas in accordance with their meaning, of meanings in accordance with their dhammas, and of concepts in accordance with their proper paths; or it is the unperverted, true nature, called the 'own-characteristic', which is to be penetrated, of those respective dhammas. And these, meaning and so forth, are profound because, like the great ocean for hares and other such creatures, they are difficult to enter and a footing is unobtainable for those of little wisdom who have not accumulated the provision of the wholesome. Among these, because penetration is also dependent on meaning, it is said, 'It is endowed with meaning through profundity in meaning and profundity in penetration,' because this shows the quality of the meaning. Because profundity in Dhamma and profundity in teaching are dependent on the expression, it is said, 'It is endowed with expression through profundity in Dhamma and profundity in teaching,' because this shows the excellence of the expression.

Atthesu pabhedagataṃ ñāṇaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā. Atthadhammaniruttipaṭisambhidāsu pabhedagataṃ ñāṇaṃ paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāti imissāpi paṭisambhidāya atthavisayattā āha “atthapaṭibhānapaṭisambhidāvisayato sāttha”nti, atthasampattiyā asati tadabhāvato. Dhammoti tanti[V 1.0259]. Niruttīti tantipadānaṃ niddhāretvā vacanaṃ. Tattha pabhedagatāni ñāṇāni dhammaniruttipaṭisambhidāti āha “dhammaniruttipaṭisambhidāvisayato sabyañjananti, asati byañjanasampattiyā tadabhāvato. Parikkhakajanappasādakanti ettha iti-saddo hetuattho. Yasmā parikkhakajanānaṃ kiṃkusalagavesīnaṃ pasādāvahaṃ, tasmā sātthaṃ. Atthasampannanti phalena hetuno anumānaṃ nadīpūrena viya upari vuṭṭhippavattiyā. Sātthakatā panassa paṇḍitavedanīyatāya, sā paramagambhīrasaṇhasukhumabhāvato veditabbā. Vuttañhetaṃ “gambhīro duddaso”tiādi (mahāva. 8). Lokiyajanappasādakanti sabyañjananti yasmā lokiyajanassa pasādāvahaṃ, tasmā sabyañjanaṃ. Lokiyajano hi byañjanasampattiyā tussati, idhāpi phalena hetuno anumānaṃ. Sabyañjanatā panassa saddheyyatāya, sā ādikalyāṇādibhāvato veditabbā.

The knowledge that has reached distinction in meanings is the analytical knowledge of meaning (attha-paṭisambhidā). The knowledge that has reached distinction in the analytical knowledges of meaning, Dhamma, and language is the analytical knowledge of discernment (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā). Therefore, because this analytical knowledge of discernment also has meaning as its domain, he said, 'It is endowed with meaning (sāttha) by way of being the domain of the analytical knowledge of meaning and the analytical knowledge of discernment,' because in the absence of the accomplishment of meaning, these two do not arise. 'Dhamma' is the text of the teaching. 'Language' (nirutti) is the explanation, having extracted the words of the text of the teaching. Therein, the knowledges that have reached distinction are the analytical knowledges of Dhamma and language. Therefore, he said, 'It is endowed with expression (sabyañjana) by way of being the domain of the analytical knowledge of Dhamma and the analytical knowledge of language,' because in the absence of the accomplishment of expression, these two do not arise. In the phrase 'it inspires confidence in discerning people,' the word 'iti' has the meaning of 'because'. Because it brings inspiration to discerning persons who seek 'What is the wholesome?', therefore it is endowed with meaning. The inference of the cause—that it is endowed with meaning—is from the effect, like inferring the occurrence of rain upstream from a river's flood. However, its state of being endowed with meaning is to be known by the wise, and that state is to be known because of its extremely profound, subtle, and delicate nature. For it is said, 'Profound, hard to see,' etc. Regarding 'it inspires confidence in worldly people,' it is endowed with expression. Because it brings inspiration to worldly people, therefore it is endowed with expression. For a worldly person is pleased by the accomplishment of the expression, and here too, the cause is inferred from the effect. However, its state of being endowed with expression is due to its credibility, and that is to be known from its nature of being good in the beginning, etc.

Atha vā paṇḍitavedanīyato sāttha”nti paññāpadaṭṭhānatāya atthasampannataṃ āha, tato parikkhakajanappasādakaṃ. Saddheyyato sabyañjananti saddhāpadaṭṭhānatāya byañjanasampannataṃ, tato lokiyajanappasādakanti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Gambhīrādhippāyato sātthanti adhippāyato agādhāpāratāya atthasampannaṃ aññathā tadabhāvato. Uttānapadato sabyañjananti subodhasaddatāya byañjanasampannaṃ, paramagambhīrassapi atthassa veneyyānaṃ suviññeyyabhāvāpādanato. Sabbopesa paṭhamassa atthadvayassa pabhedo daṭṭhabbo, tathā ceva tattha tattha saṃvaṇṇitaṃ. Tathā hettha [M 1.0275] vikappassa, samuccayassa vā aggahaṇaṃ. Upanetabbassāti pakkhipitabbassa vodānatthassa avuttassa abhāvato. Sakalaparipuṇṇabhāvenāti sabbabhāgehi paripuṇṇatāya. Apanetabbassāti saṃkilesadhammassa.

Alternatively, by the phrase 'it is endowed with meaning because it is to be known by the wise,' he speaks of its accomplishment in meaning because it is a proximate cause for wisdom; therefore, it inspires confidence in discerning people. By the phrase 'it is endowed with expression because it is credible,' he speaks of its accomplishment in expression because it is a proximate cause for faith; therefore, it inspires confidence in worldly people. In this way also, the meaning should be understood here. As for 'it is endowed with meaning because its intention is profound,' it is accomplished in meaning because its intention is unfathomable and boundless; otherwise, that accomplishment in meaning would be absent. As for 'it is endowed with expression because its words are manifest,' it is accomplished in expression because its words are easy to understand, for it brings even a most profound meaning to a state of being easily understood by those to be trained. All this should be seen as an elaboration of the first pair of meanings, and it is explained just so in various places. For that reason, there is no taking up here of the word 'vā' in the sense of alternative, or 'ca' in the sense of conjunction. As for 'of that which is to be brought forward': because of the absence of an unstated meaning of purification to be inserted. By way of being entirely complete: because of being complete in all parts. As for 'of that which is to be removed': of a defiling quality.

Paṭipattiyāti sīlavisuddhiyādisammāpaṭipattiyā, tannimittaṃ. Adhigamabyattitoti saccapaṭivedhena adhigamaveyyattiyasabbhāvato sātthaṃ kapilavatādi viya tucchaṃ niratthakaṃ ahutvā atthasampannanti katvā. Pariyattiyāti pariyattidhammaparicayena. Āgamabyattitoti durakkhātadhammesu paricayaṃ karontassa viya sammohaṃ ajanetvā bāhusaccaveyyattiyasabbhāvato sabyañcanaṃ. Byañjanasampattiyā hi sati āgamabyattīti. Sīlādipañcadhammakkhandhayuttatoti sīlādīhi pañcahi dhammakoṭṭhāsehi avirahitattā. Kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ anavasesena samantato puṇṇaṃ pūritaṃ. Nirupakkilesatoti diṭṭhimānādiupakkilesābhāvato. Nittharaṇatthāyāti vaṭṭadukkhato nissaraṇāya. Lokāmisanirapekkhatoti kathañcipi taṇhāsannissayassa anissayanato.

As for 'by practice': by right practice such as purity of virtue; because of that cause. As for 'by mastery in realization': because of the existence of expertise in realization through the penetration of the truths, it is endowed with benefit (sāttha), not being empty and fruitless like the practice of the ascetic Kapila and others, but accomplished in benefit. As for 'by learning': by study of the Dhamma of the scriptures. As for 'by expertise in the scriptures': it is endowed with expression because of the existence of expertise in being widely learned, without generating familiarity with badly-taught doctrines. For when there is accomplishment in expression, there is expertise in the scriptures. As for 'because it is connected with the five aggregates of Dhamma such as virtue': because it is not devoid of the five portions of the Dhamma, beginning with virtue. Entirely complete: complete without remainder, filled from all around. As for 'because it is free from defilements': because of the absence of defilements such as wrong view and conceit. As for 'for the purpose of crossing over': for the sake of escape from the suffering of the round of rebirth. As for 'because it is without expectation for worldly gain': because of not depending in any way on craving as a support.

Evaṃ [V 1.0260] ādikalyāṇatādiapadesena satthu purimavesārajjadvayavasena dhammassa svākkhātataṃ vibhāvetvā idāni pacchimavesārajjadvayavasenāpi taṃ dassetuṃ “atthavipallāsābhāvato vā suṭṭhu akkhātoti svākkhāto”ti vatvā tamatthaṃ byatirekamukhena vibhāvento “yathā hī”tiādimāha. Tattha vipallāsamāpajjatīti tesaṃ dhamme “antarāyikā”ti vuttadhammānaṃ vipākādīnaṃ antarāyikattābhāvato ekaṃsena apāyūpapattihetutāya abhāvato. Niyyānikattābhāvatoti atammayatābhāvato, saṃsārato ca niyyānikāti vuttadhammānaṃ ekaccayaññakiriyāpakatipurisantaraññāṇādīnaṃ tato niyyānikattābhāvato viparīto eva hoti. Tenāti atthassa vipallāsāpajjanena. Te aññatitthiyā. Tathābhāvānatikkamanatoti kammantarāyādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ antarāyikabhāvassa ariyamaggadhammānaṃ niyyānikabhāvassa kadācipi anativattanato.

Having thus explained the well-proclaimed nature of the Dhamma by way of the Teacher's first two kinds of confidence, through the designation of its auspicious beginning, etc., now, to demonstrate it also by way of the last two kinds of confidence, having stated, 'Or, because there is no distortion of meaning, it is well-proclaimed,' and wishing to elaborate on that meaning by way of contrast, he said, 'For indeed,' etc. Therein, 'falls into distortion' means that in their doctrine, the things said to be 'obstructive'—such as their results—are not obstructive, because of the absence of being invariably a cause for arising in a state of loss. Because of the absence of leading out: this is due to the absence of being conclusive, and because the things said to be leading out from saṃsāra—such as certain sacrificial acts and the knowledge of the distinction between primordial nature and spirit—do not lead out from it, it is indeed the opposite. 'Therefore' means: because of falling into a distortion of the meaning. 'They' are the followers of other sects. 'Because of not transcending that state' means: because of never transcending the obstructive nature of the five things, such as karmic obstacles, and the leading-out nature of the doctrines of the noble path.

Nibbānānurūpāya paṭipattiyāti adhigantabbassa sabbasaṅkhatavinissaṭassa nibbānassa anurūpāya sabbasaṅkhāranissaraṇūpāyabhūtāya sapubbabhāgāya sammāpaṭipattiyā [M 1.0276] akkhātattāti yojanā. Paṭipadānurūpassāti sabbadukkhaniyyānikabhūtā ārammaṇakaraṇamattenāpi kilesehi anāmasanīyā yādisī paṭipadā, tadanurūpassa. Supaññattāti sīlādikkhandhattayasaṅgahitā sammādiṭṭhiādippabhedā micchādiṭṭhiādīnaṃ pahāyikabhāvena suṭṭhu sammadeva vihitā. Saṃsandati kilesamalavisuddhitāya sameti. Evaṃ magganibbānānaṃ paṭipadāpaṭipajjanīyabhāvehi aññamaññānurūpatāya svākkhātataṃ dassetvā idāni tividhassāpi lokuttaradhammassa paccekaṃ svākkhātataṃ dassetuṃ “ariyamaggo cetthā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha antadvayanti sassatucchedaṃ, kāmasukhaattakilamathānuyogaṃ, līnuddhaccaṃ, patiṭṭhānāyūhananti evaṃ pabhedaṃ antadvayaṃ. Anupagammāti anupagantvā, anupagamanahetu vā. Paṭipassaddhakilesānīti suṭṭhu vūpasantakilesāni, paṭipassaddhippahānavasena sammadeva pahīnadosāni. Sassatādisabhāvavasenāti “sassatañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi amatañca tāṇañca leṇañcā”tiādinā tesu tesu suttesu sassatādibhāvakittanavasena.

'By practice suitable for Nibbāna' means: the connection is that it is proclaimed as the right practice, together with its preliminary part, which is the means of escape from all conditioned things and is suitable for Nibbāna, which is to be attained and is liberated from all conditioned things. 'Of that which is suitable for the path' means: of that which is suitable for such a path as leads out from all suffering and is not touched by the defilements even by the mere act of taking it as an object. 'Well-proclaimed' means: it is established well and rightly by way of abandoning wrong views, etc., being comprised of the three aggregates of virtue, etc., and having divisions such as right view, etc. Thus, having shown the well-proclaimed nature through the mutual suitability of the path and Nibbāna by way of being the practice and that which is to be reached by the practice, now, to show the well-proclaimed nature of each of the threefold supramundane Dhamma, it was said, 'Herein, the noble path...' etc. Therein, 'the two extremes' means: the two extremes with divisions such as eternalism and annihilationism; indulgence in sensual pleasure and self-mortification; sloth and restlessness; and fixation and striving. 'Not approaching' means: not having approached, or because of the reason of not approaching. 'With pacified defilements' means: with thoroughly calmed defilements; with faults rightly abandoned by way of abandonment through pacification. 'By way of the nature of being eternal, etc.' means: by way of proclaiming the nature of being eternal, etc., in those various suttas with 'Monks, I will teach you the eternal Dhamma, the deathless, the refuge, the shelter,' etc.

148. “Rāgādīnaṃ abhāvaṃ karontena ariyapuggalena sāmaṃ daṭṭhabbo”ti iminā “ariyamaggena mama rāgādayo pahīnā”ti sayaṃ attanā anaññaneyyena daṭṭhabboti sandiṭṭhi, sandiṭṭhi eva sandiṭṭhiko.

148. By the statement, 'It is to be seen for oneself by the noble person who brings about the absence of lust, etc.,' it is meant that it is to be seen by oneself personally, not being led by another, thus: 'By this noble path, my lust and other defilements have been abandoned.' Therefore, it is 'visible here and now' (sandiṭṭhi). 'Visible here and now' itself is sandiṭṭhika.

Tena [V 1.0261] tena ariyasāvakena parasaddhāya parassa saddahanena paraneyyena gantabbataṃ hitvā ñāpetabbataṃ pahāya paccavekkhaṇañāṇena karaṇabhūtena. Pasatthā diṭṭhi sandiṭṭhi yathā sambojjhaṅgo. Ariyamaggo attanā sampayuttāya sandiṭṭhiyā kilese jayati, ariyaphalaṃ tāya eva attano kāraṇabhūtāya, nibbānaṃ ārammaṇakaraṇena attano visayībhūtāya sandiṭṭhiyā kilese jayatīti yojanā.

By each noble disciple, having abandoned the state of having to proceed through faith in another—through believing another, being led by another—and having given up the state of having to be made known by another, with the reviewing knowledge that has become the instrument. A praised view (diṭṭhi) is sandiṭṭhi, like the term sambojjhaṅga. The connection is as follows: The noble path conquers the defilements by the praised wisdom associated with itself; the noble fruit conquers the defilements by that very wisdom which has become its cause; Nibbāna conquers the defilements by the praised wisdom which has taken it as its object by way of making it an object.

Bhāvanābhisamayavasena maggadhammo. Sacchikiriyābhisamayavasena nibbānadhammo. Phalampi heṭṭhimaṃ sakadāgāmivipassanādīnaṃ paccayabhāvena upari maggādhigamassa upanissayabhāvato pariyāyato “dissamāno vaṭṭabhayaṃ nivattetī”ti vattabbataṃ labhati.

The path-Dhamma is by way of realization through development. The Nibbāna-Dhamma is by way of realization through direct experience. The lower fruit, too, by being a condition for the insight, etc., of the once-returner, and because of being a decisive support condition for the attainment of a higher path, figuratively obtains the state of being spoken of thus: 'When seen, it turns back the danger of the round of rebirth.'

149. Nāssa [M 1.0277] kāloti nāssa āgametabbo kālo atthi. Yathā hi lokiyakusalassa “upapajje, aparapariyāye”tiādinā phaladānaṃ pati āgametabbo kālo atthi, na evametassāti attho. Tenāha “na pañcāhā”tiādi. Pakaṭṭhoti dūro. Phaladānaṃ pati kālo pakaṭṭho assāti kāliko, kālantaraphaladāyī. Tenāha “attano phaladāne”ti. Pattoti upanīto. Idanti “akāliko”ti padaṃ.

149. 'There is no time for it' means: for this, there is no time that must be awaited. The meaning is that just as for worldly wholesome action there is a time that must be awaited for the giving of its fruit, as in 'in a future life, in a subsequent time,' it is not so for this. Therefore, he said, 'not five days,' etc. 'Pakaṭṭha' means distant. Because the time for giving its fruit is distant for it, it is 'temporal' (kālika); it gives fruit in another time. Therefore, he said, 'in giving its own fruit.' 'Patto' means brought near. 'This' refers to the word 'timeless' (akālika).

150. Vidhinti vidhānaṃ, “ehi passā”ti evaṃpavattavidhivacanaṃ. Vijjamānattāti paramatthato upalabbhamānattā. Parisuddhattāti kilesamalavirahena sabbathā visuddhattā. Amanuññampi kadāci payojanavasena yathāsabhāvappakāsanena dassetabbaṃ bhaveyyāti tadabhāvaṃ dassento āha “manuññabhāvappakāsanenā”ti.

150. 'Method' (vidhi) means arrangement; it is the word of the method that proceeds as 'Come and see.' 'Because it exists' means: because it is obtainable in an ultimate sense. 'Because it is pure' means: because it is pure in every way, being devoid of the stain of defilements. Because even something disagreeable might sometimes have to be shown by revealing its true nature for a specific purpose, to show the absence of that necessity, he said, 'by revealing its agreeable nature.'

151. Upanetabboti upaneyyo, upaneyyova opaneyyikoti imassa atthassa adhippetattā āha “upanetabboti opaneyyiko”ti. Citte upanayanaṃ uppādananti āha “idaṃ saṅkhate lokuttaradhamme yujjatī”ti. Citte upanayananti pana ārammaṇabhūtassa dhammassa ārammaṇabhāvūpanayane adhippete asaṅkhatepi yujjeyya “ārammaṇakaraṇasaṅkhātaṃ upanayanaṃ arahatīti opaneyyiko”ti. Allīyananti phusanaṃ. Nibbānaṃ upaneti ariyapuggalanti adhippāyo.

151. 'To be brought near' (upanetabba) means upaneyya; upaneyya itself is opaneyyika. Because this meaning is intended, he said, ''To be brought near' means opaneyyika.' He said that 'bringing near to the mind' is 'producing,' and 'this is applicable to the conditioned supramundane Dhamma.' However, if by 'bringing near to the mind' is intended the bringing of the Dhamma that has become an object to the state of being an object, then it would also be applicable to the unconditioned, thus: 'Because it is worthy of the bringing-near designated as making it an object, it is opaneyyika.' 'Allīyana' means touching. The intention is this: it leads the noble person to Nibbāna.

152. Viññūhīti [V 1.0262] vidūhi, paṭividdhasaccehīti attho. Te pana ekaṃsato ugghaṭitaññūādayo hontīti āha “ugghaṭitaññūādīhī”ti. “Paccatta”nti etassa “pati attanī”ti bhummavasena attho gahetabboti āha “attani attanī”ti. Veditabboti vuttaṃ, kathaṃ veditabboti āha “bhāvito me”tiādi. Tattha “me”ti iminā “paccatta”nti padena vuttamatthaṃ anvayato dassetvā puna byatirekena dassetuṃ “na hī”tiādi vuttaṃ, taṃ suviññeyyameva. “Viññūhī”ti idaṃ antogadhāvadhāraṇanti dassento “bālānaṃ pana avisayo cesā”ti āha.

152. “By the wise” (viññūhi) means by the discerning (vidūhi), that is, by those who have penetrated the truths (paṭividdhasaccehi). They are invariably those of quick understanding, etc.; hence it is said, “by those of quick understanding, etc.” The meaning of “paccatta” should be understood in the locative sense as “in each self” (pati attani); hence it is said, “in oneself, in oneself.” It is said, “it should be known.” As to how it should be known, it is said, “developed by me,” etc. Therein, by “me,” the meaning stated by the word “paccatta” is shown by way of accordance, and then to show it again by way of contrast, “for not,” etc., is said; that is easily understood. Indicating that “by the wise” (viññūhi) contains an implicit determination, it is said, “but this is beyond the scope of fools.”

Evaṃ ādikalyāṇatādinā aññamaññassa anurūpadesanāya dhammassa svākkhātataṃ dassetvā idāni purimassa purimassa pacchimaṃ pacchimaṃ padaṃ kāraṇavacananti dassento “apicā”tiādimāha. Tattha sandiṭṭhikattāti yasmā [M 1.0278] ayaṃ dhammo vuttanayena sāmaṃ daṭṭhabbo, sandiṭṭhiyā kilese viddhaṃseti, sandassanañca arahati, tasmā svākkhāto durakkhāte titthiyadhamme tadabhāvato. Iminā nayena sesapadesupi yathārahaṃ attho daṭṭhabbo.

Having thus shown the well-proclaimed nature of the Dhamma by its being good in the beginning, etc., and by the teaching being suitable for one another, now, to show that each succeeding word is a statement of the reason for each preceding word, it is said, “moreover,” etc. Therein, “because it is to be seen for oneself” (sandiṭṭhikattā) means: because this Dhamma is to be seen for oneself in the way that has been stated, it destroys defilements by the praised wisdom, and it is worthy of being seen; therefore it is well-proclaimed. This is not so in the ill-proclaimed doctrine of the sectarians because of the absence of that quality. In this way, the meaning of the remaining terms should be understood as appropriate.

153. Tassevantiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ buddhānussatiyaṃ vuttanayena veditabbaṃ.

153. In the passages beginning with “Tassevanti,” whatever should be stated, that should be understood in the manner stated in the discourse on the recollection of the Buddha.

3. Saṅghānussatikathāvaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Discourse on the Recollection of the Saṅgha

154. Ariyasaṅghaguṇāti ārakattā kilesehi, anaye na iriyanato, aye ca iriyanato, sadevakena ca lokena “saraṇa”nti araṇīyato ariyo ca so saṅgho ca, ariyānaṃ vā saṅgho ariyasaṅgho, tassa guṇā.

154. “The qualities of the Noble Saṅgha” (Ariyasaṅghaguṇā): because of being far (ārakattā) from defilements; because of not conducting oneself in what is unbeneficial (anaye na iriyanato) and conducting oneself in what is beneficial (aye iriyanato); and because of being fit to be approached (araṇīyato) as a “refuge” (saraṇa) by the world with its devas, that community is both noble (ariyo) and a Saṅgha. Or, the community (saṅgho) of the noble ones (ariyānaṃ) is the Noble Saṅgha (ariyasaṅgho); these are its qualities.

155. Yaṃ sammāpaṭipadaṃ paṭipanno “suṭṭhu paṭipanno”ti vuccati. Sā ariyamaggapaṭipadā paṭipakkhadhamme anivattidhamme katvā pajahanato payojanābhāvā sayampi anivattidhammā, adhigantabbassa ca nibbānassa ekaṃsato anulomīti. Tato eva apaccanīkā, anudhammabhūtā ca, tassā ca paṭipannattā ariyasaṅgho “suppaṭipanno”ti vuttoti dassetuṃ “suṭṭhu paṭipanno”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha “anivattipaṭipada”nti iminā ujuppaṭipattiṃ dasseti. Punappunaṃ nivattane hi sati ujuppaṭipatti na hoti. “Anulomapaṭipadaṃ apaccanīkapaṭipada”nti [V 1.0263] iminā ñāyappaṭipattiṃ. Paṭipajjitabbassa hi nibbānassa anulomanena, apaccanīkatāya cassā ñāyato. “Dhammānudhammapaṭipada”nti iminā sāmīcippaṭipattiṃ anucchavikabhāvadīpanato. Etena paṭhamapadassa papañcaniddeso, itarāni tīṇi padānīti dasseti. Tenāha “yasmā panā”tiādi.

155. One who has entered upon the right practice is called “one who practices well.” That noble path of practice, because it abandons opposing states having made them non-reverting, is itself of a non-reverting nature and is invariably conducive to Nibbāna which is to be attained. For that very reason, it is unopposed and is in accordance with the Dhamma. To show that because of having entered upon it, the Noble Saṅgha is called “well-practiced,” it is said, “one who practices well,” etc. Therein, by “non-reverting practice,” it indicates direct practice. For when there is repeated turning back, there is no direct practice. By “conducive practice, unopposed practice,” it indicates right practice. For, because it is conducive to the Nibbāna that should be attained and is unopposed to it, it is right. By “practice in accordance with the Dhamma,” it indicates harmonious practice, because it shows its suitability. By this, it is shown that the other three terms are a detailed explanation of the first term. Therefore, it is said, “but since,” etc.

Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjanena kiccasiddhito ariyabhāvāvahaṃ savanaṃ sakkaccasavanaṃ nāmāti vuttaṃ “sakkaccaṃ suṇantīti sāvakā”ti, tena ariyā eva nippariyāyato satthu sāvakā nāmāti dasseti. Sīladiṭṭhisāmaññatāyāti ariyena sīlena, ariyāya ca diṭṭhiyā samānabhāvena. Ariyānañhi sīladiṭṭhiyo majjhe bhinnasuvaṇṇaṃ viya ninnānākaraṇaṃ maggenāgatattā. Tena [M 1.0279] te yattha katthaci ṭhitāpi saṃhatāva. Tenāha “saṅghātabhāvamāpanno”ti. Māyāsāṭheyyādipāpadhammasamucchedena uju. Tato eva gomuttavaṅkābhāvena avaṅkā. Candalekhāvaṅkābhāvena akuṭilā. Naṅgalakoṭivaṅkābhāvena ajimhā. Avaṅkādibhāvena vā uju. Parisuddhaṭṭhena ariyā. Apaṇṇakabhāvena ñāyati kamati nibbānaṃ, taṃ vā ñāyati paṭivijjhīyati etenāti ñāyo. Vaṭṭadukkhaniyyānāya anucchavikattā. Anurūpattā sāmīci opāyikātipi saṅkhaṃ samaññaṃ gatā sammāpaṭipatti, tāya samaṅgitāya suppaṭipannā “sammā paṭipajjantī”ti katvā. Vattamānattho hi ayaṃ paṭipanna-saddo yathā “sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno”ti (pu. pa. 206). Atītaṃ paṭipadanti yathāvuttamaggasammāpaṭipattiṃ vadati. Ubhayena ca sāmaññaniddesena, “suppaṭipannā ca suppaṭipannā ca suppaṭipannā”ti ekasesanayena vā gahitānaṃ samūho “suppaṭipanno”ti vuttoti dasseti.

Because the task is accomplished by practicing as instructed, listening that brings about the noble state is called “attentive listening.” Thus it is said, “Disciples are those who listen attentively.” By this, it is shown that the noble ones alone are, in the primary sense, the Teacher's disciples. “By commonality in virtue and view” means by being the same in terms of noble virtue and noble view. For the virtue and views of the noble ones are not different, like a gold bar broken in the middle, because they have come about through the path. Therefore, wherever they may be, they are united. Thus it is said, “having attained to a state of unity.” By the complete cutting off of evil states such as deceit and craftiness, one is straight (uju). For that very reason, by the absence of crookedness like that of cow's urine, one is not crooked (avaṅka). By the absence of crookedness like that of the crescent moon, one is not bent (akuṭila). By the absence of crookedness like that of the tip of a plough, one is not twisted (ajimha). Or, by being not crooked, etc., one is straight. By the meaning of being pure, they are noble. By being unerring, one goes to Nibbāna; or by this, that Nibbāna is known and penetrated, therefore it is the “way” (ñāyo). Because it is suitable for the release from the suffering of the round of existence, and because it is appropriate, the right practice has attained the designations of “proper” (sāmīci) and “expedient” (opāyikā). Being endowed with that, they are “well-practiced” because “they practice rightly.” For this word “paṭipanna” has a present-tense meaning, as in “one practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.” “The path that has been traversed” refers to the right practice of the path as described. And it is shown that by both the general explanation, or by the method of ekasesa (retention of one) with the phrase “those practicing well and those who have practiced well are the well-practiced,” the group of those thus taken is called “well-practiced.”

Evaṃ ādipadatthaniddesabhāvena itarapadānaṃ atthaṃ vatvā idāni catunnampi padānaṃ avomissakaṃ atthaṃ dassetuṃ “apicā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha yathānusiṭṭhanti satthārā yathā anusiṭṭhaṃ, tathā anusāsanīanurūpanti attho. Apaṇṇakapaṭipadanti avirajjhanakapaṭipadaṃ, anavajjapaṭipattinti attho. Ettha ca svākkhāte dhammavinaye apaṇṇakapaṭipadaṃ paṭipannattāti evaṃ sambandhitabbaṃ. Purimapadena sambandhe dutiyapadaṃ na vattabbaṃ siyā, nanu ca dutiyapadena sambandhepi paṭhamaṃ padaṃ na vattabbaṃ siyāti? Na tassa paṭhamaṃ apekkhitattā. Sā pana sāvakānaṃ apaṇṇakapaṭipadā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipadāti dassanatthaṃ “yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipannattā”ti vattabbaṃ[V 1.0264]. Ubhayassāpi vā suppaṭipannabhāvasādhanattā ubhayaṃ vuttaṃ. Tathā hi pi-saddena ubhayaṃ samuccinoti.

Having thus stated the meaning of the other terms by way of a detailed explanation of the first term, now, in order to show the distinct meaning of all four terms, “moreover,” etc., was said. Therein, “as instructed” means: as it was instructed by the Teacher, thus in accordance with the instruction; this is the meaning. “The unerring path” means the practice that is not mistaken, the blameless practice; this is the meaning. And here, it should be connected thus: “because of practicing the unerring path in the well-proclaimed Dhamma and Discipline.” If there is a connection with the preceding term, the second term should not be stated. But surely, even with a connection to the second term, should not the first term not be stated? No, because that first term is depended upon first. But, in order to show that that unerring practice of the disciples is the practice “as instructed,” it should be said “because of practicing as instructed.” Or, because both establish the state of being well-practiced, both are stated. For so, by the particle “pi,” he combines both.

Kilesajimhavasena antadvayagāhoti sabbaso taṃ pahāya sammāpaṭipadā kāyādivaṅkappahāyinī ujuppaṭipatti hotīti āha “majjhimāya paṭipadāya…pe… ujuppaṭipanno”ti.

By the power of the crookedness that is defilement, there is the grasping of the two extremes. Therefore, having entirely abandoned that, the right practice, which abandons the crookedness of body and so on, is the straight practice. Thus, He said: 'By the middle way... one who is practicing directly.'

Ñāyo nāma yuttappattapaṭipatti, nibbānañca, sabbasaṅkhārasamathatāya ādittaṃ celaṃ, sīsaṃ vā ajjhupekkhitvāpi paṭipajjitabbamevāti āha “ñāyo vuccati nibbāna”nti. Nibbāyanakiriyāmukhena cettha nibbānaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ[M 1.0280], maggañāṇādīhi vā ñāyati paṭivijjhīyati sacchikarīyati cāti ñāyo nibbānanti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo.

The suitable and proper practice and Nibbāna are called the Method. Because it is the state of quenching of all formations, it must indeed be practiced, even disregarding a burning garment or one's head. Thus, He said: 'Nibbāna is called the Method.' And here, it should be understood that Nibbāna is spoken of through the principal means of the act of extinguishing. Or, because it is known, penetrated, and realized by means of path-knowledge and so on, Nibbāna is the Method. Thus, the meaning here should be understood in this way.

Guṇasambhāvanāya parehi kayiramānaṃ paccupaṭṭhānādisāmīcikammaṃ arahantīti sāmīcikammārahā.

Because they are worthy of proper actions, such as attending upon, which are performed by others out of esteem for their virtues, they are 'those worthy of proper actions'.

156. Yadidanti antogadhaliṅgavacanabhedo nipātoti tassa vacanabhedena atthamāha “yā imānī”ti. Evanti pakāratthe nipāto, iminā pakārenāti attho. Tena itarāni tīṇi yugaḷāni dassitāni hontīti āha “evaṃ cattāri purisayugaḷāni hontī”ti. Etanti etaṃ “purisapuggalā”ti bahuvacanavasena vuttaṃ padaṃ. Purisā ca te puggalā ca purisapuggalā. Tattha “purisā”ti iminā paṭhamāya pakatiyā gahaṇaṃ, “puggalā”ti pana dutiyāyapi sattasāmaññenāti evaṃ vā ettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ kīdisānaṃ? Ānetvā hunitabbānanti adhikārato pākaṭoyamattho. Dātabbanti vā paccattavacanaṃ “catunnaṃ paccayāna”nti padaṃ apekkhitvā sāmivasena pariṇāmetabbaṃ, aññathā yesaṃ kesañci catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ “āhuna”nti samaññā siyā. Āhunaṃ arahatīti vā āhuneyyo. Sakkādīnampi vā āhavananti sakkādīhipi diyyamānaṃ dānaṃ. Yattha hutaṃ mahapphalanti yasmiṃ āvahanīyaggimhi hutaṃ dadhiādi āhuneyyaggigahapataggidakkhiṇeyyaggīsu hutato uḷāraphalanti tesaṃ brāhmaṇānaṃ laddhi. Hutanti dinnaṃ. Nikāyantareti sabbatthikavādinikāye.

156. The term 'yadidaṃ' is a particle wherein distinctions of gender and number are included; therefore, He states its meaning with a distinction of number as 'yāni imāni.' The term 'evaṃ' is a particle in the sense of manner, meaning 'in this manner.' By that, the other three pairs are shown; thus, He said: 'Thus there are four pairs of men.' The term 'etaṃ' is the word 'purisapuggalā' stated in the plural. They are men and they are individuals, hence 'purisapuggalā.' Therein, by 'purisā,' the taking of the first nature (male) is meant; by 'puggalā,' however, the second nature (female) is also taken in the general sense of a being. Or, the meaning here should be understood in this way. Of what kind of four requisites? Of those to be brought and offered. This meaning is evident from the context. Or, the nominative word 'dātabbaṃ' should be changed into the genitive case in dependence on the word 'catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ'; otherwise, any four requisites whatsoever would have the designation 'āhuna.' Or, 'he is worthy of an offering (āhuna),' thus he is 'āhuneyyo.' Or, 'āhavana' is a gift given even by Sakka and others. 'Where an offering bears great fruit' refers to the doctrine of those brahmins that what is offered, such as curd, into the āvahanīya fire has a more magnificent fruit than what is offered into the āhuneyya, gahapati, and dakkhiṇeyya fires. 'Hutaṃ' means 'given.' 'Nikāyantare' means in the Sarvāstivāda school.

Ṭhapetvā 165 teti te piyamanāpe ñātimitte apanetvā, tesaṃ adatvāti adhippāyo. Esa eso. Ekabuddhantare ca dissatīti ekasmiṃ buddhantare vītivatte dissati. Ca-saddena kadāci asaṅkhyeyyepi kappe vītivatteti dasseti. Abbokiṇṇanti paṭipakkhehi avomissaṃ, kiriyāvisesakañcetaṃ. Piyamanāpattakaradhammā nāma sīlādayo, te ariyasaṅghe suppatiṭṭhitā. Ayaṃ hettha adhippāyo – ñātimittā vippayuttā na cirasseva samāgacchanti, anavaṭṭhitā ca tesu piyamanāpatā, na evamariyasaṅgho. Tasmā saṅghova pāhuneyyoti. Pubbakāranti aggakiriyaṃ. Sabbappakārenāti ādaragāravabahumānādinā, deyyadhammassa sakkaccakaraṇādinā [M 1.0281] ca sabbena pakārena. Svāyaṃ pāhavanīya-saddo “pāhuneyyo”ti vuccati pariyāyabhāvena.

'Excluding them' means having set aside those dear and beloved relatives and friends, not giving to them; this is the intention. 'This' refers to this Saṅgha.
