Among them: because it has no origination-end or cessation-end, it is endless; it is the unconditioned phenomenon. Because it is not an object for the taints, it is taintless. Because it is the domain of subtle knowledge, it is subtle. Because it does not decay through aging like a conditioned phenomenon, it is unaging. Because it is not impaired by sickness and so on, it is unimpaired. Because it is not knowable by eye-consciousness, it is invisible. Because it has the quality of never causing satiety, it is excellent. Because it is not common, it is marvelous. Because it has a nature that cannot be overcome by calamities and because it is a cause for the state without calamity, it is a calamity-free phenomenon. Because it is the cause for liberation from the suffering of the round of existence, it is liberation. Because it is a place of shelter for those who see saṃsāra as fearful, it is a shelter. Because it is the supreme destination for those very ones, it is the final resort. Because a footing is not obtained in it by ordinary knowledge, in the sense of being unfathomable, it is profound. Because it is to be understood with difficulty and hardship even by those who have made merit, it is difficult to understand. Because, leaving aside direct realization, it is not to be traversed by the knowledge of reasoning, it is beyond the sphere of reasoning. Because it is to be known and attained only by the wise, such as the Buddhas, it is to be experienced by the wise. Thus the meaning should be understood.

Ariyasāvakasseva [V 1.0329] ijjhati sacchikiriyābhisamayavasena nibbānaguṇānaṃ pākaṭabhāvato. Aṭṭhāne cāyaṃ eva-saddo vutto, ijjhati evāti yojanā. Sukhasiddhivasena vā evaṃ vuttaṃ “ariyasāvakassevā”ti. Tenevāha “evaṃ santepī”tiādi. Upasamagarukenāti nibbānaninnena. Manasi kātabbā yathāvuttā upasamaguṇā. Sukhaṃ supatītiādīsu vattabbaṃ mettākathāyaṃ āvi bhavissati. Paṇītādhimuttiko hoti nibbānādhimuttattā.

It is accomplished only for the noble disciple because the qualities of Nibbāna become manifest by means of realization and deep understanding. And this word 'eva' (only) is used in the wrong place; the connection should be 'ijjhati eva' (it is indeed accomplished). Or, it is said thus, “only for the noble disciple,” by means of easy accomplishment. Therefore, he said, “Even when it is so,” etc. “By one who holds peace as weighty” means by one inclined toward Nibbāna. The qualities of peace, as stated, should be borne in mind. What is to be said regarding “one sleeps happily,” etc., will become clear in the discourse on loving-kindness. One becomes one with sublime aspiration due to being resolved upon Nibbāna.

Anussatikammaṭṭhānaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Recollection Meditation Subjects is completed.

Iti aṭṭhamaparicchedavaṇṇanā.

Thus Ends the Commentary to the Eighth Chapter.

9. Brahmavihāraniddesavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Exposition of the Divine Abidings

Mettābhāvanākathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Discourse on the Development of Loving-kindness

240. Mettaṃ [M 1.0350][V 1.0330] brahmavihāraṃ. Bhāvetukāmenāti uppādetukāmena paccavekkhitabboti sambandho. Sukhanisinnenāti visamaṃ anisīditvā pallaṅkābhujanena sukhanisinnena.

240. Loving-kindness, the divine abiding. 'By one who wishes to develop it' means by one who wishes to produce it; this is connected with 'should be reflected upon'. 'By one comfortably seated' means by one seated comfortably by assuming the cross-legged posture, not sitting unevenly.

Kasmāti paccavekkhaṇāya kāraṇapucchā, aññaṃ adhigantukāmena aññattha ādīnavānisaṃsapaccavekkhaṇā kimatthiyāti adhippāyo. Mettā nāma atthato adoso. Tathā hi adosaniddese “metti mettāyanā mettāyitatta”nti (dha. sa. 1062) niddiṭṭhaṃ. Khantīti ca idha adhivāsanakkhanti adhippetā. Sā pana atthato adosappadhānā cattāro arūpakkhandhāti mettāya sijjhamānāya titikkhākhanti siddhā eva hotīti āha “khanti adhigantabbā”ti. Tena khantiyaṃ ānisaṃsapaccavekkhaṇā satthikāvāti dasseti. Abhibhūto pariyuṭṭhānena. Pariyādinnacitto kusaluppattiyā okāsālābhena. Ādīnavo daṭṭhabbo pāṇaghātādivasena diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikādianatthamūlabhāvato.

'Why?' is a question about the reason for reflection. The intention is: for one who wishes to attain something else, what is the purpose of reflecting on the danger and benefit in something else? Loving-kindness, by its intrinsic nature, is non-aversion. For thus it is stated in the exposition of non-aversion: 'Friendliness, the act of friendliness, the state of friendliness' (Dhammasaṅgaṇi §1056). And here, 'patience' is intended as the patience of endurance. But that patience, in essence, consists of the four mental aggregates which have non-aversion as their principal quality. Thus, when loving-kindness is being accomplished, patience as forbearance is indeed accomplished; therefore, he said, 'Patience should be attained.' By that, he shows that reflection on the benefit in patience is indeed purposeful. Overcome by obsession. With a mind completely seized, through not getting an opportunity for the arising of wholesome states. The danger should be seen in terms of killing living beings and so forth, because of its being the root of harm in the present life and in future lives.

Khantī paramaṃ tapoti parāpakārasahanādikā titikkhalakkhaṇā khanti uttamaṃ tapo akattabbākaraṇakattabbakaraṇalakkhaṇāya sammāpaṭipattiyā mūlabhāvato. Khantibalaṃ balānīkanti paramaṃ maṅgalabhūtā khanti eva balaṃ etassāti khantibalaṃ. Vuttañhi “khantibalā samaṇabrāhmaṇā”ti. Dosādipaṭipakkhavidhamanasamatthatāya anīkabhūtena teneva ca khantibalena balānīkaṃ. Khantyā bhiyyo na vijjatīti attano paresañca anatthapaṭibāhano, atthāvaho ca khantito uttari apassayo natthi.

'Patience is the highest austerity' means that patience, characterized by forbearance such as enduring harm from others, is the supreme austerity because it is the root of right practice, which is characterized by not doing what should not be done and doing what should be done. 'The power of patience is the foremost of powers' means that patience itself, which is the highest blessing, is the power of this one, hence 'the power of patience.' For it is said, 'Ascetics and brahmins have patience as their power.' And by that very power of patience, which is like an army due to its ability to destroy opposing factors such as aversion, it is the foremost of powers. 'There is nothing that surpasses patience' means there is no support superior to patience, which wards off harm and brings benefit to oneself and others.

Vivecanatthāyāti vikkhambhanatthāya. Khantiyā saṃyojanatthāya attānanti adhippāyo. Bhāvanaṃ [V 1.0331] dūsentīti dosā, puggalāyeva dosā puggaladosā. Yesu bhāvanā na sampajjati, aññadatthu vipajjateva, te eva [M 1.0351] vuttā. Paṭhamanti vakkhamānena koṭṭhāsato koṭṭhāsantarupasaṃharaṇanayena vinā sabbapaṭhamaṃ.

'For the purpose of discerning' means for the purpose of suppressing. The intention is 'for uniting oneself with patience.' 'They corrupt the development'—thus they are corruptions; the persons themselves are the corruptions, hence 'person-corruptions.' Those persons in whom the development does not succeed, but on the contrary only fails, are the ones spoken of. 'First' means first of all, without the method of transferring from one category to another, which will be explained.

Piyāyitabbo piyo, tappaṭipakkho appiyo. So saṅkhepato duvidho atthassa akārako, anatthassa kārakoti. Tattha yo attano, piyassa ca anatthassa kārako, so veripuggalo daṭṭhabbo. Yo pana attano, piyassa ca atthassa akārako, appiyassa ca atthassa kārako, “atthaṃ me nācarī”tiādinā (dha. sa. 1237), “appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acarī”tiādinā ca āghātavatthubhūto, so appiyo, ananukūlavuttiko aniṭṭhoti attho. Liṅgavisabhāgeti itthiliṅgādinā liṅgena visadise. Odhisoti bhāgaso. “Tissa dattā”tiādinā odhisakanti attho.

One who is to be loved is a dear one; his opposite is an undear one. In brief, he is of two kinds: one who does not bring about benefit, and one who brings about harm. Among them, one who brings about harm for oneself and for a dear one is to be seen as an enemy-person. But as for one who does not bring about benefit for oneself and for a dear one, and who brings about benefit for an undear one, he becomes a basis for resentment through such thoughts as, 'He did not act for my benefit,' and so on, and 'He acted for the benefit of one who is undear and displeasing to me,' and so on. Such a one is undear; the meaning is one of unfavorable conduct, an undesirable person. 'In one of a different gender' means in one dissimilar in gender, such as the female gender, and so on. 'Specifically' means by division. The meaning is making a specific designation, as in 'Tissā, Dattā,' and so on.

Idāni yathāvuttesu chasu puggalesu abhāvetabbatāya kāraṇaṃ dassento “appiyaṃ hī”tiādimāha. Tattha appiyaṃ hi piyaṭṭhāne ṭhapento kilamatīti dosena bhāvanāya saparissayatamāha. Appiyatā hi piyabhāvassa ujupaṭipakkhā, na ca tassa piyaṭṭhāne ṭhapanena vinā bhāvanā sijjhati. Atippiyasahāyakaṃ majjhattaṭṭhāne ṭhapento kilamatīti rāgena bhāvanāya saparissayatamāha atippiyasahāyassa gehassitapemaṭṭhānabhāvato. Tenāha “appamattakepī”tiādi. Majjhattaṃ iṭṭhāniṭṭhatāhi majjhasabhāvaṃ neva piyaṃ nāppiyanti attho. Garuṭṭhāne piyaṭṭhāne ca ṭhapento kilamati majjhatte sambhāvanīyapiyāyitabbatānaṃ abhāvā. Na hi ajjhupekkhitabbe bhāvanīyatā, manāpatā vā paccupaṭṭhāti, piyagarubhāvasampanne ca paṭhamaṃ mettā bhāvetabbā. Kodho uppajjati koṭṭhāsantarabhāvānupanayanato.

Now, showing the reason why loving-kindness should not be developed towards the six types of persons mentioned, he said, 'For an undear one,' and so on. Therein, by the words, 'For one becomes exhausted placing an undear one in the place of a dear one,' he stated the dangerousness of the development due to aversion. For being undear is the direct opposite of being dear, and without placing that person in the position of a dear one, the development does not succeed. By the words, 'One becomes exhausted placing an overly dear friend in the position of a neutral one,' he stated the dangerousness of the development due to lust, because an overly dear friend is a basis for household-based affection. For that reason, he said, 'even for a trifle,' and so on. A neutral person is one of a middle nature regarding the pleasant and the unpleasant; the meaning is one who is neither dear nor undear. One becomes exhausted placing a neutral person in the position of a respected one or a dear one, because in a neutral person there is an absence of venerability and lovability. For in one who should be regarded with equanimity, neither venerability nor agreeableness presents itself. And loving-kindness should first be developed towards one endowed with the qualities of being dear and respected. Anger arises from not bringing a person to the state of another category.

Tamevāti visabhāgaliṅgameva. Liṅgasabhāgeti avisesetvā “piyapuggale”ti āha. Bhittiyuddhamakāsīti sīlaṃ adhiṭṭhāya pihitadvāre gabbhe sayanapīṭhe nisīditvā mettaṃ bhāvento mettāmukhena uppannarāgena andhīkato bhariyāya santikaṃ gantukāmo dvāraṃ asallakkhetvā bhittiṃ bhinditvāpi nikkhamitukāmatāya bhittiṃ pahari. Tenāha [M 1.0352] “mettāyanāmukhena rāgo vañcetī”ti (netti. aṭṭha. 21), “andhatamaṃ tadā hoti, yaṃ rāgo sahate nara”nti ca.

'That very one' means one of a different gender. As for one of the same gender, without making a distinction, he said 'in a dear person.' Regarding 'he made war on the wall': Having undertaken the moral precepts, a man was sitting on a bed in a room with a closed door, developing loving-kindness. Blinded by lust that arose on the pretext of loving-kindness, he wanted to go to his wife. Not perceiving the door, he struck the wall, with the desire to get out even by breaking it. For that reason, it is said, 'Lust deceives on the pretext of loving-kindness,' and, 'When lust overcomes a man, then there is blinding darkness.'

Ādānanikkhepaparicchinne [V 1.0332] addhāpaccuppannabhūte dharamānatāya paccakkhato viya upalabbhamāne khandhappabandhe idha sattādiggahaṇaṃ, na tiyaddhagateti āha “kālakate panā”tiādi. Kasmā pana kālakate mettābhāvanā na ijjhatīti? Mettābyāpārassa ayogyaṭṭhānabhāvato. Na hi matapuggalo hitūpasaṃhārāraho. Yattha sati sambhave payogato hitūpasaṃhāro labbheyya, tattheva mānaso hitūpasaṃhāro yujjeyya. Dukkhāpanayanamodappavattīsupi eseva nayoti karuṇābhāvanādīnampi kālakate anijjhanaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Aññattha paguṇamettājhāno ācariyassa kālakatabhāvaṃ ajānanto taṃ mettāya pharitukāmo “ācariyaṃ ārabbha mettaṃ ārabhatī”ti vutto. Tenāha “paguṇāva me mettājhānasamāpattī”ti. Nimittanti ārammaṇaṃ. Gavesāhīti “yaṃ puggalaṃ uddissamettaṃ ārabhasi, so jīvati na jīvatī”ti jānāhīti attho. Mettāyantoti mettaṃ karonto, mettaṃ bhāventoti attho.

Here, in this matter of loving-kindness meditation, the term 'beings,' etc., in the context of the continuity of the aggregates—which is defined by rebirth-linking and death, has come to be in the present time, and is perceived as if directly due to its state of being presently existing—does not apply to one who has passed through the three periods of time; therefore, he said, 'But when one has passed away...' and so on. But why does the cultivation of loving-kindness not succeed for one who has passed away? Because it is an unsuitable basis for the operation of loving-kindness. Indeed, a deceased person is not worthy of having benefit brought to them. Only in a case where, there being a possible cause, the bringing of benefit could be obtained through effort, would the mental bringing of benefit be fitting. This is the same principle in the removal of suffering and the arising of joy; thus, it should be understood that the non-success of the cultivation of compassion and the like for one who has passed away is also stated. Elsewhere, one skilled in the loving-kindness jhāna, not knowing the fact of his teacher's death and wishing to pervade him with loving-kindness, is spoken of thus: 'He begins loving-kindness with his teacher as the object.' Therefore, he said, 'My attainment of the loving-kindness jhāna is well-practiced.' 'Sign' means the object. 'Seek!' means, 'Ascertain whether the person towards whom you are directing loving-kindness is alive or not'—this is the meaning. 'Practicing loving-kindness' means doing loving-kindness, developing loving-kindness—this is the meaning.

241. Attani bhāvanā nāma sakkhibhāvatthāti nānāvidhasukhānubandhaanavajjasukhaabyāsekasukhādi yaṃ attani upalabbhati, taṃ nidassento tassa vattamānatāya āha “ahaṃ sukhito homī”ti. Sarīrasukhaṃ nāma anekantikaṃ, īdisassa puggalassa anokāsaṃ cittadukkhanti tadabhāvaṃ sandhāyāha “niddukkhoti vā”ti. Homīti sambandho. Tathā averotiādīsu, visesato ca dukkhābhāve sukhasaññā. Sā panāyaṃ niddukkhatā verīnaṃ puggalānaṃ verasaññitānaṃ pāpadhammānaṃ abhāvato, visesato byāpādavirahato īghasaññitāya ītiyā abhāvato, anavajjakāyikasukhasamaṅgitāya ca hotīti dassento āha “avero abyāpajjo anīgho sukhī”ti. Attānaṃ pariharāmīti evaṃbhūto hutvā mama attabhāvaṃ pavattemi, yāpemīti attho.

241. The cultivation of loving-kindness towards oneself is for the purpose of being a witness. Therefore, indicating whatever happiness is found in oneself—such as happiness that has various kinds of associated happiness, blameless happiness, and happiness unmixed with defilements—and due to its present existence, one says, 'May I be happy.' Bodily happiness is uncertain, but for such a person, mental suffering has no opportunity to arise; therefore, referring to its absence, one says, 'or free from suffering.' The word 'homi' (may I be) is connected. It is the same in 'free from enmity,' etc., and especially, in the absence of suffering, there is the perception of happiness. But this freedom from suffering comes from the absence of hostile persons or of evil qualities perceived as enmity; especially from the absence of ill will, or from the absence of affliction perceived as distress, and from being endowed with blameless bodily happiness. Showing this, one says, 'free from enmity, free from ill will, free from distress, and happy.' 'I maintain myself' means: having become one of such a nature, I cause my individual existence to proceed, I sustain it—this is the meaning.

Evaṃ sante yaṃ vibhaṅge vuttaṃ, taṃ virujjhatīti sambandho. Evaṃ santeti evaṃ sati, yadi attanipi mettā bhāvetabbāti attho. “Yaṃ vibhaṅge vutta”nti vatvā [M 1.0353] vibhaṅgadesanāya samānagatikaṃ suttapadaṃ āharanto “kathañca bhikkhū”tiādimāha. Tassattho parato āgamissati.

'This being so, what was said in the Vibhaṅga is contradicted'—this is the connection. 'This being so' means: if it is thus, if loving-kindness is to be cultivated towards oneself also—this is the meaning. Having said, 'what was said in the Vibhaṅga,' he brings a Sutta passage that has a similar course to the Vibhaṅga exposition, saying, 'And how, bhikkhus...' and so on. Its meaning will come later.

Tanti vibhaṅgādīsu vacanaṃ. Appanāvasenāti appanāvahabhāvanāvasena. Idanti “ahaṃ sukhito homī”tiādivacanaṃ. Sakkhibhāvavasenāti ahaṃ viya sabbe sattā attano sukhakāmā, tasmā tesu mayā attani viya sukhūpasaṃhāro kātabboti evaṃ tattha attānaṃ sakkhibhāve [V 1.0333] ṭhapanavasena. Tenāha “sacepi hī”tiādi. Kasmā pana attani bhāvanā appanāvahā na hotīti? Attasinehavasena saparissayabhāvato. Koṭṭhāsantare pana bhāvitabhāvanassa tatthāpi sīmasambhedo hotiyeva.

'That' means the statement in the Vibhaṅga, etc. 'By way of absorption' means by way of the cultivation that brings absorption. 'This' means the statement, 'May I be happy,' etc. 'By way of being a witness' means: by way of placing oneself in the position of a witness in that matter, thus: 'Just as I, all beings desire their own happiness; therefore, for them, the bringing of happiness should be done by me as for myself.' Therefore, he said, 'Even if...' and so on. But why does the cultivation towards oneself not bring absorption? Because of its being accompanied by danger, by the power of craving which is love for oneself. But for one who has developed the cultivation in another section, even there [i.e., towards oneself] the breaking of boundaries certainly occurs.

Sabbā disāti anavasesā dasapi disā. Anuparigamma cetasāti cittena pariyesanavasena anugantvā. Nevajjhagā piyataramattanā kvacīti sabbussāhena pariyesanto atisayena attato piyataraṃ aññaṃ sattaṃ katthaci disāya neva adhigaccheyya na passeyya. Evaṃ piyo puthu attā paresanti evaṃ kassaci attato piyatarassa anupalabbhanavasena puthu visuṃ visuṃ tesaṃ tesaṃ sattānaṃ attā piyo. Tasmā tena kāraṇena, attakāmo attano hitasukhaṃ icchanto, paraṃ sattaṃ antamaso kunthakipillikampi, na hiṃse na haneyya, na viheṭheyyāti attho.

'All directions' means all ten directions without remainder. 'Having gone around with the mind' means having followed in sequence by way of searching with the mind. 'Nowhere did he find one dearer than self' means: searching with all effort, one would not find, would not see in any direction another being dearer than oneself to an exceeding degree. 'Thus the self is separately dear to others' means: thus, by way of not finding anyone dearer than oneself, the self is dear to those respective beings, separately and individually. Therefore, for that reason, one who desires their own self, wishing for their own welfare and happiness, should not harm, should not kill, should not vex another being, even down to a grub or an ant—this is the meaning.

Ayaṃ nayoti sabbehi sattehi, attano ca piyatarabhāvaṃ nidassetvā tesu karuṇāyanaṃ vadatā bhagavatā sukhesitāya “attānaṃ sakkhibhāve ṭhapetvā sattesu mettā bhāvetabbā”ti mettābhāvanāya nayadassanaṃ katamevāti attho.

'This is the method' means: The showing of the method for the cultivation of loving-kindness has indeed been done by the Blessed One, who, having pointed out that for all beings their own self is dearest, spoke with compassion for them, [teaching] thus: 'On account of the search for happiness, having established oneself as a witness, loving-kindness should be cultivated towards beings.' This is the meaning.

242. Sukhapavattanatthanti sukhena akicchena mettāya pavattanatthaṃ. Yvāssāti yo puggalo assa yogino. Piyoti iṭṭho. Manāpoti manavaḍḍhanako. Garūti guṇavisesavasena garukātabbo. Bhāvanīyoti sambhāvetabbo. Ācariyamattoti sīlādinā ācariyappamāṇo. Piyavacanādīnīti ādi-saddena atthacariyādike saṅgaṇhāti. Sīlasutādīnīti ādi-saddena saddhādike, dhutadhammajāgariyānuyogādike ca saṅgaṇhāti.

242. 'For the sake of easy arising' means for the purpose of the arising of loving-kindness easily, without difficulty. 'Whoever for him' means whatever person of that yogī. 'Dear' means desired. 'Pleasing' means one who increases [joy in] the mind. 'Respected' means to be revered by way of special qualities. 'To be esteemed' means to be praised or esteemed. 'Of the measure of a teacher' means having the measure of a teacher in virtue, etc. In 'by kind speech, etc.,' by the word 'etc.' it includes conduct for the welfare [of others], etc. In 'by virtue, learning, etc.,' by the word 'etc.' it includes qualities such as faith, etc., and the ascetic practices, the practice of wakefulness, etc.

Kāmanti [M 1.0354] yuttappattakāritāsukhasiddhidīpanoyaṃ nipāto. Tenetaṃ dīpeti – tādisaṃ puggalaṃ uddissa bhāvanaṃ ārabhanto yogī yuttappattakārī, sukhena cassa tattha bhāvanā ijjhati, tena pana yoginā tāvatā santoso na kātabboti. Tenāha “appanā sampajjatī”tiādi. Sīmāsambhedanti mariyādāpanayanaṃ, attā piyo majjhatto verīti vibhāgākaraṇanti attho. Tadanantaranti tato piyamanāpagarubhāvanīyato, tattha vā mettādhigamato anantaraṃ. Atippiyasahāyake mettā bhāvetabbāti sambandho, garuṭṭhānīye paṭiladdhaṃ mettāmanasikāraṃ atippiyasahāyake upasaṃharitabbanti attho. Sukhūpasaṃhārakatassa taṃ hoti pageva paṭipakkhadhammānaṃ [V 1.0334] vikkhambhitattā. Atippiyasahāyakato anantaraṃ majjhatte mettā bhāvetabbā majjhattaṃ piyagaruṭṭhāne ṭhapetuṃ sukarabhāvato. “Atippiyasahāyakato”ti ca idaṃ purimāvatthaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ. Paguṇamanasikārādhigamato paṭṭhāya hissa sopi piyaṭṭhāne eva tiṭṭhati. Majjhattato verīpuggaleti majjhattapuggale mettāyantena tattha paguṇamanasikārādhigamena piyabhāvaṃ upasaṃharitvā tadanantaraṃ verīpuggalaṃ bhāvanāya majjhatte ṭhapetvā tato majjhattato piyabhāvūpasaṃhārena verīpuggale mettā bhāvetabbā. “Verīpuggale”ti ca idaṃ purimāvatthaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ. Ekekasmiṃ koṭṭhāse muduṃ kammaniyaṃ cittaṃ katvāti piyagaruṭṭhānīyo, atippiyo, majjhatto, verīti catūsu puggalakoṭṭhāsesu paṭhamaṃ tāva piyagaruṭṭhānīye mettābhāvanaṃ adhigantvā vasībhāvappattiyā tathāpavattaṃ cittaṃ koṭṭhāsantarūpasaṃhāratthaṃ muduṃ kammaniyaṃ katvā tadanantaraṃ atippiyasahāye atippiyabhāvaṃ vikkhambhetvā piyabhāvamatte cittaṃ ṭhapentena bhāvanā upasaṃharitabbā, tampi vasībhāvāpādanena muduṃ kammaniyaṃ katvā tadanantaraṃ majjhatte udāsinabhāvaṃ vikkhambhetvā piyabhāvaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā bhāvanā upasaṃharitabbā, puna tampi vasībhāvāpādanena muduṃ kammaniyaṃ katvā tadanantaraṃ verimhi verīsaññaṃ vikkhambhetvā majjhattabhāvūpaṭṭhapanamukhena piyabhāvaṃ uppādentena bhāvanā upasaṃharitabbā. Tena vuttaṃ “tadanantare tadanantare upasaṃharitabba”nti, jhānacittaṃ upanetabbaṃ uppādetabbanti attho.

The word 'kāmaṃ' is a particle that indicates the state of being one who is accustomed to doing what is suitable and appropriate, and easy accomplishment. By this, the following is indicated: A yogī who begins meditation directed towards such a person is one who is accustomed to doing what is suitable and appropriate, and for that yogī, the meditation succeeds with ease. However, that yogī should not be content with just that. Therefore, it is said, 'absorption is attained,' and so on. 'Breaking of the boundary' means the removal of the limit; the meaning is not making the division: 'self, dear one, neutral one, enemy.' 'Immediately after that' means immediately after that dear, agreeable, and venerable person, or immediately after the attainment of loving-kindness towards them. The connection is that loving-kindness should be developed towards an extremely dear friend. The meaning is that the attention of loving-kindness obtained in regard to one in the position of a venerable person should be applied to an extremely dear friend. For that yogī, it is easy to apply that attention, because the opposing states have already been suppressed. Immediately after the extremely dear friend, loving-kindness should be developed towards a neutral person, because it is easy to place the neutral person in the position of a dear and venerable one. And this, 'from the extremely dear friend,' is said taking into account the previous stage. For, starting from the attainment of proficient attention, that person also stands for the yogī in the position of a dear one. 'From the neutral person to the enemy person' means: by one developing loving-kindness towards the neutral person, having applied the state of dearness to them through the attainment of proficient attention, and immediately after that, having placed the enemy person in neutrality by means of meditation, loving-kindness should be developed towards the enemy person by applying the state of dearness from that state of neutrality. And this, 'towards the enemy person,' is said taking into account the previous stage. 'Having made the mind soft and workable in each category' means: among the four categories of persons—the dear and venerable one, the extremely dear one, the neutral one, and the enemy—first, having attained the development of loving-kindness towards the dear and venerable one, and through the attainment of mastery, having made the mind so disposed soft and workable for the purpose of applying it to another category; immediately after that, the meditation should be applied by one who, towards the extremely dear friend, has suppressed the state of being extremely dear and has placed the mind merely in the state of dearness. Having made that mind also soft and workable by bringing it to mastery, immediately after that, the meditation should be applied by one who, towards the neutral person, has suppressed the state of indifference and established the state of dearness. Again, having made that mind also soft and workable by bringing it to mastery, immediately after that, the meditation should be applied by one who, towards the enemy, has suppressed the perception of an enemy and, by means of establishing the state of neutrality, produces the state of dearness. Therefore it is said, 'it should be applied immediately after, immediately after.' The meaning is: the jhāna-mind should be brought forth, should be produced.

Verīpuggalo vā natthi kammabalena vā etarahi payogasampattiyā vā sabbaso anatthakarassa abhāvato. Mahāpurisajātikattāti mahāpurisasabhāvattā [M 1.0355] cirakālaparicayasamiddhakhantimettānuddayādiguṇasampannatāya uḷārajjhāsayattāti attho. Tādiso hi sabbasaho parāparādhaṃ tiṇāyapi na maññati. Tena vuttaṃ “anatthaṃ karontepi pare verīsaññāva nuppajjatī”ti. Tenāti tena yoginā. Atthi verīpuggaloti sambandho.

Or, there is no enemy person, either due to the power of past kamma or due to the present accomplishment of effort, because of the complete absence of one who causes harm. 'Because of being of the nature of a great person' means: because of having the nature of a great person, because of being endowed with qualities such as patience, loving-kindness, and compassion, perfected through long-term practice, and because of having a noble disposition. For such a one is all-enduring and does not consider another's offense to be even as much as a blade of grass. Therefore it is said, 'Even when others do harm, the perception of an enemy does not arise.' 'By that' means by that yogī. The connection is: 'there is an enemy person'.

243. Purimapuggalesūti piyādīsu jhānassa ārammaṇabhūtesu purimesu puggalesu. Mettaṃ samāpajjitvāti paṭighaṃ vikkhambhetvā uppāditaṃ mettājhānaṃ samāpajjitvā. Mettāyantena paṭighaṃ paṭivinodetabbanti ettha keci pana “upacārajjhānaṃ sampādetvā”ti atthaṃ vadanti, tesaṃ upacārajjhānato vuṭṭhānampi icchitabbaṃ siyā “vuṭṭhahitvā”ti vuttattā. Pubbe tasmiṃ puggale asatiyā amanasikārena paṭighaṃ anuppādentassa sādhāraṇato taṃ vikkhambhetvā jhānassa uppādanaṃ, samāpajjanañca vuttaṃ. Idāni pana taṃ anussarantassapi manasi karontassapi yathā paṭighaṃ [V 1.0335] na uppajjati, taṃ vidhiṃ dassetuṃ idaṃ vuttaṃ “taṃ puggalaṃ mettāyantena paṭighaṃ vinodetabba”nti. Mettāyanameva hi idha paṭighavinodanaṃ adhippetaṃ. Na nibbātīti na vūpasammati.

243. 'In the previous persons' means in the previous persons, such as the dear one, who have become the object of the jhāna. 'Having attained loving-kindness' means having attained the loving-kindness jhāna that was produced by suppressing aversion. Regarding 'Aversion should be dispelled by one developing loving-kindness,' here some say the meaning is 'having accomplished access jhāna.' In their view, emergence from access jhāna should also be intended, because it is said 'having emerged.' Previously, for one who does not produce aversion towards that person through inattention and non-attention, the production and attainment of jhāna by suppressing it in a general way was spoken of. But now, in order to show the method whereby aversion does not arise even when recollecting and paying attention to that person, this was said: 'Aversion should be dispelled by developing loving-kindness towards that person.' For here, the very developing of loving-kindness is intended as the dispelling of aversion. 'It is not extinguished' means it does not subside.

Anusāratoti anugamanato, paccavekkhaṇatoti attho. Ghaṭitabbanti vāyamitabbaṃ.

'By recollecting' means by following after or by reviewing. 'One should strive' means one should make an effort.

Tañca kho ghaṭanaṃ vāyamanaṃ. Iminā idāni vakkhamānena ākārena.

And that striving, that effort, should be done in this manner that will now be explained.

Ubhato dvīsu ṭhānesu daṇḍo etassāti ubhatodaṇḍakaṃ, tena. Ocarakā lāmakācārā pāpapurisā. Tatrāpīti tesupi aṅgamaṅgāni okkantesupi. Tenāti manopadosena. Na sāsanakaro. Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṃ hi sāsanaṃ. Tassevāti tatopi. Nissakke hi idaṃ sāmivacanaṃ, samuccaye ca eva-saddo, paṭhamaṃ kuddhapurisatopīti attho. Tenāti kujjhanena. Pāpiyoti pāpataro. Sārambhādikassa kilesānubandhassa vatthubhāvato kodhassa sāvajjataṃ ñatvāpi kujjhanato sace kodhe anavajjasaññī kuddhassa puggalassa na paṭikujjheyyāti keci. Ubhinnanti dvinnaṃ puggalānaṃ. Tenāha “attano ca parassa cā”ti. Atha vā ubhinnanti ubhayesaṃ lokānaṃ, idhalokaparalokānanti attho.

This saw has a handle in two places on both sides, thus it is an 'ubhatodaṇḍaka' (a saw with handles on both ends); by means of that. 'Ocarakā' means those of base conduct, evil men. 'Even there' means even towards those who are cutting off one's major and minor limbs. 'By that' means by corruption of mind. One who gets angry is not a doer of the teaching. For the non-doing of all evil is the teaching. 'Of that very one' means 'than that one.' For this genitive is in the sense of the ablative. And the word 'eva' is in the sense of inclusion. The meaning is: 'even than the first angry person.' 'By that' means by getting angry. 'More evil' means more wicked. Because it is the basis for the sequence of defilements such as contention, and because one gets angry even after knowing the faultiness of anger. Some say that if one perceives no fault in anger, one would not get angry back at an angry person. 'Of both' means of two persons. Therefore he said, 'of oneself and of another.' Alternatively, 'of both' means of both worlds, that is, this world and the next world.

Sapattakantāti [M 1.0356] paṭisattūhi icchitā. Sapattakaraṇāti tehi kātabbā. Kodhananti kujjhanasīlaṃ. Kodhanāyanti kodhano ayaṃ, ayanti ca nipātamattaṃ. Kodhaparetoti kodhena anugato, parābhibhūto vā. Dubbaṇṇova hotīti pakatiyā vaṇṇavāpi alaṅkatapaṭiyattopi mukhavikārādivasena virūpo eva hoti etarahi, āyatiṃ cāti. Kodhābhibhavassa ekantikamidaṃ phalanti dīpetuṃ “dubbaṇṇo vā”ti avadhāraṇaṃ katvā puna “kodhābhibhūto”ti vuttaṃ. Na pacuratthoti na pahūtadhano. Na bhogavāti upabhogaparibhogavatthurahito. Na yasavāti na kittimā.

'Sapattakanta' means desired by adversaries. 'Sapattakaraṇa' means to be made by them. 'Kodhana' means one whose nature is to be angry. 'Kodhanāyaṃ' is parsed as 'kodhano ayaṃ,' and 'ayaṃ' is merely a particle. 'Kodhapareta' means followed by anger, or overwhelmed by it. 'He becomes ugly indeed' means that even if one is naturally handsome, even if adorned and prepared, by means of facial distortion and so on, he becomes ugly indeed, both now and in the future. To show that this result is the certain outcome of being overcome by anger, having made the emphasis with 'he is ugly indeed,' it is said again, 'overcome by anger.' 'Not of many things' means not having abundant wealth. 'Not having possessions' means devoid of things for use and enjoyment. 'Not having renown' means not famous.

Chavālātanti chavadahanālātaṃ, citakāyaṃ santajjanummukkantipi vadanti. Ubhatopadittanti ubhosu koṭīsu daḍḍhaṃ. Majjhe gūthagatanti vemajjhaṭṭhāne sunakhassa vā siṅgālassa vā uhadena gūthena makkhitaṃ. Kaṭṭhatthanti dārukiccaṃ. Neva pharati na sādheti. Tathūpamāhanti tathūpamaṃ tādisaṃ ahaṃ. Imanti “so ca hoti abhijjhālū”tiādinā (itivu. 92) heṭṭhā vuttaṃ sandhāya satthā [V 1.0336] vadati, tasmā kāmesu tibbasārāgatādinā sīlarahitanti adhippāyo. Idha pana byāpannacittaṃ paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappatāvasena yojetabbaṃ.

'Chavālāṭa' means a firebrand for burning a corpse; some also say it is a terrifying firebrand on a funeral pyre. 'Burning at both ends' means burnt at both ends. 'Smeared with dung in the middle' means smeared in the middle part with dung excreted by a dog or a jackal. 'For the purpose of wood' means it does not accomplish the purpose of wood. 'I am of such a simile' means: one of such a simile, of such a kind. Regarding this, the Teacher speaks with reference to what was said previously, beginning with 'And he is covetous...' Therefore, the intention is: devoid of virtue due to intense passion for sensual pleasures and so on. Here, however, it should be connected by way of having a corrupt mind and a defiled mental intention.

So dāni tvantiādi yathāvuttehi suttapadehi attano ovadanākāradassanaṃ.

'So now you' and so forth is a demonstration of the manner of admonishing oneself by means of the sutta passages as stated.

244. Yo yo dhammoti kāyasamācārādīsu yo yo sucaritadhammo. Vūpasantoti saṃyato. Parisuddhoti kilesamalavigamena visuddho. Kilesadāhābhāvena vā upasanto, anavajjabhāvena parisuddho, kāyasamācārasseva upasamo cirakālaṃ saṃyatakāyakammatāya veditabbo. Evaṃ sesesupi.

244. 'Whatever quality' means whatever good conduct among bodily conduct and so on. 'Calmed' means restrained. 'Pure' means purified by the removal of the stain of defilements. Or, 'calmed' due to the absence of the burning of defilements, and 'pure' due to being blameless. The calming of bodily conduct itself should be understood as having restrained bodily action for a long time. Thus it is also for the remaining cases.

Teti vacīmanosamācāre.

'Te' refers to verbal and mental conduct.

Soti upasantavacīsamācāro puggalo. Paṭisanthārakusaloti yathā parehi chiddaṃ na hoti, evaṃ paṭisantharaṇe kusalo. Sakhiloti adhivāsanakhantisaṅkhātena [M 1.0357] sakhilabhāvena samannāgato. Sukhasambhāsoti piyakatho. Sammodakoti sammodanīyakathāya sammodanasīlo. Uttānamukhoti vikuṇitamukho ahutvā pītisomanassavasena vikasitamukho. Pubbabhāsīti yena kenaci samāgato paṭisanthāravasena paṭhamaṃyeva ābhāsanasīlo. Madhurena sarena dhammaṃ osāreti sarabhaññavasena. Sarabhāṇaṃ pana karonto parimaṇḍalehi paripuṇṇehi padehi ca byañjanehi ca abyākulehi dhammakathaṃ katheti.

'He' is a person whose verbal conduct is calmed. 'Skilled in hospitality' means skilled in welcoming in such a way that no fault is found by others. 'Amiable' means endowed with amiability characterized by forbearance and patience. 'Pleasant in conversation' means one who has pleasant speech. 'One who greets cordially' means one who has the nature of greeting with cordial speech. 'With an open countenance' means not having a contracted face, but having a beaming face by means of joy and gladness. 'First to speak' means having the nature of speaking first by way of greeting when meeting with anyone. He recites the Dhamma with a sweet voice in the manner of chanting. Moreover, when reciting, he gives a Dhamma talk with words and phrases that are well-rounded, complete, and not confused.

Sabbajanassa pākaṭo sakkaccakiriyāyāti adhippāyo. Tenāha “yo hī”tiādi. Okappetvāti saddahitvā. Okappanalakkhaṇā hi saddhā. Ohitasototi avahitasoto, sussusantoti attho. Aṭṭhiṃkatvā atthaṃ katvā, atthiko vā hutvā.

The intention is: he becomes manifest to all people through his respectful conduct. Therefore, He said, 'For whoever...' and so on. 'Having placed faith' means having believed. For faith has the characteristic of settling upon and believing. 'With ear applied' means with attentive ear; the meaning is 'desiring to hear.' 'Having taken it to heart' means having made it the goal, or having become one who has need of it.

“Ekopi na vūpasanto hotī”ti pāṭho, evarūpo puggalo nirayato nirayaṃ upapajjanto bahukālaṃ tattheva saṃsaratīti dassetuṃ “aṭṭhamahānirayasoḷasaussadanirayaparipūrako bhavissatī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha sañjīvādayo aṭṭha mahānirayā. Avīcimahānirayassa dvāre dvāre cattāro cattāro katvā kukkuḷādayo soḷasa ussadanirayā. Kāruññaṃ upaṭṭhapetabbaṃ mahādukkhabhāgibhāvato. Yasmiṃ [V 1.0337] puggale avihesābhūtā dukkhāpanayanakāmatā upatiṭṭhati, tattha paṭigho anokāsovāti āha “kāruññampi paṭicca āghāto vūpasammatī”ti.

The reading is 'Not even one is calmed.' To show that such a person, being reborn from one hell to another, wanders there for a long time, it is said, 'He will be a filler of the eight great hells and the sixteen subsidiary hells.' Therein, the eight great hells are Sañjīva and so on. At each and every gate of the Avīci great hell, there being four each, are the sixteen subsidiary hells, Kukkuḷa and so on. Compassion should be established because of their state of partaking in great suffering. In whatever person the desire to remove suffering, which arises from non-harming, is present, in that person aversion has no opportunity. Therefore, it is said, 'On account of compassion, too, hatred is calmed.'

Imassa ca atthassāti “yo yo dhammo”tiādinā vuttassa atthassa.

'And of this meaning' refers to the meaning of that which was stated beginning with 'whatever quality...'

245. Yaṃ verī dukkhāpetuṃ sakkoti, so tassa vasena “attano visaye”ti vutto bhikkhuno kāyo. Kinti kiṃ kāraṇaṃ. Tassāti verino. Avisayeti dukkhaṃ uppādetuṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya agocare. Sacitteti attano citte. Mahānatthakaranti idhalokatthaparalokatthaparamatthānaṃ virādhanavasena mahato vipulassa, nānāvidhassa ca diṭṭhadhammikādibhedassa anatthassa kāraṇaṃ. Mūlanikantananti sīlassa mūlāni nāma hirottappakhantimettānuddayā, tesaṃ chindanaṃ. Kodho hi uppajjamānova pāṇātipātādivasena hirottappādīni ucchindati. Jaḷoti andhabālo.

245. Whatever body of a bhikkhu an enemy is able to cause suffering to, that body is said to be 'in his own domain' by the enemy's power. 'Why?' means 'what is the reason?' 'His' means of the enemy. 'Not in his domain' means not his resort, due to the inability to produce suffering. 'In one's own mind' means in one's own mind. 'A doer of great harm' means: by way of obstructing the benefits of this world, the next world, and the ultimate benefit, it is a cause of great, extensive, and various kinds of harm, distinguished as that visible in the present life and so on. 'Cutting the roots' means the cutting of the roots of virtue, namely, moral shame, moral dread, patience, loving-kindness, and compassion. For anger, just as it arises, by way of killing living beings and so on, cuts off moral shame, moral dread, and so on. 'A dull person' means a blind fool.

Anariyaṃ [M 1.0358] kammanti verinā katamahāparādhamāha. Yo sayanti yo tvaṃ sayampi. Dosetukāmoti kodhaṃ uppādetukāmo. Yadi kari yadi akāsi. Dosuppādenāti dosassa uppādanena. Dukkhaṃ tassa ca nāmāti dukkhañca nāma tassa aparādhakassa. Nāmāti asambhāvane nipāto, tena tassa kāraṇaṃ anekantikanti dasseti. Tenāha “kāhasi vā na vā”ti, karissasi na vā karissasīti attho. Ahitaṃ magganti attano ahitāvahaṃ duggatimaggaṃ.

By 'an ignoble deed,' he speaks of the great offense done by the enemy. 'You yourself' means 'you who yourself.' 'Desiring to provoke anger' means desiring to arouse anger. 'If you did' means if you have done so. 'By the arising of anger' means by the production of anger. 'Suffering indeed for him' means suffering indeed for that offender. 'Nāma' is a particle in the sense of improbability or censure; by that, it shows that causing it is not certain. Therefore, He said, 'Will you do it or not?' The meaning is: you might do it, or you might not do it. 'The unbeneficial path' means the path to a woeful destination that brings what is not beneficial to oneself.

Aṭṭhāneti doso tava appiyassa kārāpako, sattu pana tassa vasavattitāya dāsasadisoti aṭṭhānaṃ paccāpakiriyāya. Tasmā tameva dosaṃ chindassu ucchinda. Khaṇikattāti udayavayaparicchinno attano pavattikālasaṅkhāto khaṇo etesaṃ atthīti khaṇikā, tabbhāvato khaṇapabhaṅgubhāvatoti attho. Kassa dānīdha kujjhasīti aparādhakassa santāne yehi khandhehi te aparādho kato, te taṃkhaṇaṃyeva sabbaso niruddhā. Idāni pana aññe tiṭṭhantīti kassa tvaṃ idha kujjhasi. Na hi yuttaṃ anaparādhesu kujjhananti adhippāyo. Taṃ vinā kassa so kareti yo puggalo yassa dukkhaṃ karoti, taṃ dukkhakiriyāya visayabhūtaṃ puggalaṃ vinā kassa nāma so dukkhakārako dukkhaṃ kare kareyya. Sayampi dukkhahetu tvamitīti evaṃ sayampi tvaṃ etassa dukkhassa [V 1.0338] hetu, evaṃ samāne tassa tuyhañca tassa dukkhassa hetubhāve kiṃ kāraṇā tassa kujjhasi na tuyhanti attho.

‘Unfitting’ means: Anger is the maker of what is unpleasing to you; the enemy, however, being under its control, is like a slave. Therefore, it is an unfitting occasion for retaliation. Therefore, cut off, destroy that very anger. ‘Momentary’ means: for these aggregates there is a moment defined by arising and passing away, therefore they are called momentary; the meaning is because of that state, because of the state of breaking up in a moment. ‘For whom will you now be angry here?’ means: in the continuum of the offender, by whichever aggregates the offense was done to you, those aggregates have ceased completely at that very moment. Now, however, other aggregates exist. Therefore, at whom are you angry here? Indeed, it is not proper to be angry at the non-offending ones; this is the intention. ‘Without him, for whom would he do it?’ means: whatever person causes suffering to someone, without that person who is the object of the act of causing suffering, to whom indeed could that doer of suffering cause suffering? ‘You yourself are also a cause of suffering’ means: in this way, you yourself are also a cause of this suffering. When it is the same that both he and you are causes of that suffering, for what reason are you angry at him and not at yourself? This is the meaning.

246. Paralokepi anugāmibhāvato kammaṃyeva sakaṃ santakaṃ etesanti kammassakā, tesaṃ bhāvo kammassakatā. Paccavekkhaṇā nāma nisedhanatthā, nisedhanañca bhāvino kammassāti āha “yaṃ kammaṃ karissasī”ti. Paṭighavasena pana pavattakammaṃ pākaṭabhāvato āsannaṃ, paccakkhañcāti āha “idañcā”ti. Ca-saddo byatireke, so tassa kammassa phalanissandena “neva sammāsambodhi”ntiādinā byatirekato vuccamānamevatthaṃ joteti. Neva samatthanti sambandho. Niraye niyuttaṃ, jātanti vā nerayikaṃ. Attānaṃyeva okirati dosarajenāti adhippāyo.

246. Because it follows even into the next world, kamma alone is their own possession; therefore, they are ‘owners of their kamma.’ Their state is ‘ownership of kamma.’ ‘Reflection’ is for the purpose of prevention, and the prevention is of future kamma; therefore, it says, ‘whatever kamma you will do.’ However, kamma that has occurred through aversion, because it is manifest, is near and directly perceptible; therefore, it says, ‘and this.’ The word ‘ca’ is in the sense of contrast; it illuminates the meaning—which is about to be stated in contrast as the fruit-result of that kamma—with ‘never perfect enlightenment,’ etc. The connection is with ‘not capable.’ ‘Nerayikaṃ’ means bound to hell, or born there. The intention is: one scatters the dust of aversion upon oneself.

247. Satthu [M 1.0359] pubbacariyaguṇā paccavekkhitabbā, satthu gāravenāpi paṭighaṃ vūpasameyyāti.

247. The Teacher’s virtues of former conduct should be reflected upon; even through reverence for the Teacher, aversion may be allayed.

Bodhisattopi samāno nanu te satthā cittaṃ nappadūsesi, pageva abhisambuddhoti adhippāyo. Deviyā paduṭṭhenāti deviyā saddhiṃ padubbhinā micchācāravasena aparaddhena. Yattha susāne chavasarīraṃ chaḍḍīyati, taṃ āmakasusānaṃ. Nikhaññamānoti nikhaṇiyamāno. Purisakāraṃ katvāti āvāṭato nikkhamanatthāya bāhubalena purisakāraṃ katvā. Yakkhānubhāvenāti aḍḍavinicchayena ārādhitacittassa yakkhassa ānubhāvena. Sirigabbhanti vāsāgāre.

Even as a Bodhisatta, your Teacher did not corrupt his mind, did he not? How much more so when fully enlightened? This is the intention. ‘By the one who transgressed with the queen’ means: by the one who offended through misconduct, having transgressed with the queen. A charnel ground where a corpse is discarded, that is a ‘raw charnel ground.’ ‘Being buried’ means being interred. ‘Having made a man's effort’ means: having made a man's effort with the strength of his arms in order to get out of the pit. ‘By the power of the yakkha’ means: by the power of the yakkha whose mind was pleased by the half-judgment. ‘In the royal chamber’ means: in the dwelling house.

Āsīsethevāti yathādhippete atthe ñāyato anavajjato āsaṃ kareyya. Na nibbindeyyāti “evaṃ kicchāpannassa me kuto sotthibhāvo”ti na nibbindeyya. Vuttañhi “āpadāsu kho, mahārāja, thāmo veditabbo”ti (udā. 53). Yathā icchinti yena pakārena kassaci pīḷaṃ akatvā rajje patiṭṭhitaṃ attānaṃ icchiṃ, tathā ahaṃ ahunti passāmi. Voti hi nipātamattaṃ.

‘One should aspire’ means: one should make an aspiration for the desired goal rightly and blamelessly. ‘One should not become weary’ means: one should not become weary, thinking, ‘For me, who has fallen into such distress, whence could there be a state of well-being?’ For it has been said: ‘Indeed, O great king, in adversities, strength is to be known.’ ‘As I wished’ means: In whatever way I wished for myself to be established in the kingdom without harming anyone, in that way I have become; thus I see. ‘Vo’ is indeed just a particle.

Kāsiraññāti kalābunā kāsirājena. Sakaṇṭakāhīti ayakaṇṭakehi sakaṇṭakāhi.

‘By the king of Kāsi’ means: by the king of Kāsi, Kalābu. ‘With thorny ones’ means: with thorny ones, with iron thorns.

Mahallakoti vuddho vayoanuppatto. Rujjhantīti nirujjhanti.

‘Old’ means: aged, having reached old age. ‘They are broken’ means: they cease.

Cittapariggaṇhanakāloti [V 1.0339] visevanaṃ kātuṃ adatvā cittassa sammadeva damanakālo.

‘The time for restraining the mind’ means: not giving an opportunity for opposition, it is the time for rightly taming the mind.

Puthusallenāti vipulena sallena. Nāgoti hatthināgo. Vadhīti vijjhi, māresīti vā attho. Imaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgantvā mayi evaṃ karaṇaṃ nāma na tava vasena hoti, tasmā kassa vā rañño, rājamattassa vā ayaṃ payogo uyyojanāti attho.

‘With a broad dart’ means: with a large dart. ‘Nāga’ means: the elephant-nāga. ‘He struck’ means: he pierced, or it means he killed. The meaning is: ‘Having come to this place, this act against me is not of your own accord. Therefore, whose instigation or urging is this? The king’s or a royal minister’s?’ This is the meaning.

Chabbaṇṇarasmīti nīlapītalohitādivasena chabbaṇṇamayūkhā. Chabbaṇṇakiraṇavantadantatāya hi te hatthī “chaddantā”ti vuccanti, na chaddantavantatāya.

‘Six-colored rays’ means: six-colored rays such as blue, yellow, and red. Indeed, because they have tusks possessing six-colored rays, those elephants are called ‘Chaddanta,’ not because they possess six tusks.

Chātoti jighacchito. Khādeyyāti khādeyyaṃ, ayameva vā pāṭho. Āhitoti [M 1.0360] suhito. Sambalanti maggāhāraṃ. Taṃ pana yasmā upacārena pathassa hitanti vuccati, tasmā “pātheyya”ntipi vuttaṃ. “Mittadubbhī vatāyaṃ andhabālo”ti kāruññena assupuṇṇehi nettehi taṃ purisaṃ udikkhamāno.

‘Hungry’ means: famished. ‘I would eat’ means: I would eat, or this is the actual reading. ‘Satisfied’ means: well-fed. ‘Provision’ means: provision for a journey. And since that is figuratively called ‘beneficial for the path,’ therefore it is also called ‘pātheyya’ (viaticum). Looking up at that man with eyes full of tears out of compassion, thinking, ‘Alas, this blind fool is a traitor to a friend!’

Mā ayyosi me bhadanteti ettha māti nipātamattaṃ, māti vā paṭikkhepo, tena upari tena kātabbaṃ vippakāraṃ paṭisedheti. Ayyo meti ayyirako tvaṃ mama atithibhāvato. Bhadanteti piyasamudācāro. Tvaṃ nāmetādisaṃ karīti tvampi evarūpaṃ akāsi nāma.

In ‘Mā ayyosi me bhadante,’ ‘mā’ is just a particle, or ‘mā’ is a prohibition; with it, he prohibits the harm to be done by him later on. ‘Ayyo me’ means: you are my master because you are a guest. ‘Bhadante’ is an affectionate address. ‘You indeed did such a thing’ means: even you have indeed done such a thing.

Tiracchānabhūtopi pana mahākapi hutvā khemantabhūmiṃ sampāpesīti yojanā.

Furthermore, even though he was an animal, being a great monkey, he brought them to the land of safety. This is the connection.

Peḷāya pakkhipantepīti khuddakāya peḷāya pādehi koṭetvā pakkhipantepi. Maddantepīti dubbalabhāvakaraṇatthaṃ nānappakārehi maddantepi. Alampāneti evaṃnāmake ahituṇḍike.

‘Even when putting him in a basket’ means: even when putting him into a small basket, having kicked him with the feet. ‘Even when crushing him’ means: even when crushing him in various ways in order to make him weak. ‘In Alampāna’ means: in the snake charmer of that name.

Pītaṃ vāti ettha vā-saddo avuttatthavikappe, tena odātamañjiṭṭhādiṃ avuttaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Cittānuvattantoti cittaṃ anuvattanto. Homi cintitasannibho evamayaṃ bahulābhaṃ labhatūti. Ānubhāvena pana thalaṃ kareyya udakaṃ…pe… chārikaṃ kare. Evaṃ pana yadi cittavasī hessaṃ…pe… uttamattho na sijjhatīti tadā attanā tattha diṭṭhaṃ ādīnavaṃ dasseti bhagavā. Tattha uttamatthoti buddhabhāvamāha. Bhojaputtehīti luddaputtehi.

Here in ‘pītaṃ vā,’ the word ‘vā’ is for an alternative of something unstated; by it, it includes the unstated colors like white, madder, etc. ‘Following the mind’ means: following the mind. ‘May I become of a color similar to what is thought, so that this person may get much gain.’ However, by his power, he could make dry land into water… make ashes. ‘However, if I were to become a master of the mind in this way… the highest goal would not be achieved.’ Thus, the Blessed One shows the danger seen by himself therein at that time. Therein, by ‘highest goal,’ he speaks of the state of a Buddha. ‘By the Bhojaputtas’ means: by the sons of hunters.

Aḷārāti [V 1.0340] yena sayaṃ tadā luddahatthato mocito, taṃ satthavāhaṃ nāmena ālapati. Atikassāti nāsāya āvutarajjuṃ ākaḍḍhitvā. Samparigayhāti kāḷavettalatādīhi sabbaso pariggahetvā, acchariyāni dussahānaṃ sahanavasenāti adhippāyo.

He addresses by name, as 'Āḷāra,' that caravan leader by whom he himself was at that time freed from the hands of hunters. ‘Atikassāti’ means having pulled the rope tied on the nose. ‘Samparigayhāti’ means having completely taken hold of with black rattan vine and the like; the meaning is the wonders achieved by the power of enduring unbearable things.

Ativiya ayuttaṃ appatirūpaṃ paṭighacittuppādanena kenaci appaṭisamakhantiguṇassa satthusāsanāvokkamanappasaṅgato.

Exceedingly improper and unsuitable, because of the liability of straying from the dispensation of the Teacher, who possesses the quality of incomparable patience, through the arising of a mind of aversion towards anyone.

248. “Anamataggoyaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro”tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 2.124; 3.99, 100; 3.5.520; kathā. 75) āgatāni suttapadāni anamataggasaddo, tadattho vā etesanti anamataggiyāni.

248. The sutta phrases that come in texts beginning with 'Without discoverable beginning is this saṃsāra, monks...' are called Anamataggiyāni because for them there is the word anamatagga or its meaning.

Ajehi [M 1.0361] gamanamaggo ajapatho. Saṅkū laggāpetvā te ālambitvā gamanamaggo saṅkupatho. Saṅkūti aṅkusākārena katadīghadaṇḍo vuccati. Ādi-saddena papātamaggaduggamaggādike saṅgaṇhāti. Ubhatobyūḷheti sampahāratthaṃ dvīhipi pakkhehi gāḷhasannāhe. Aññāni ca dukkarāni karitvā dhanāsāya pabbatavidugganadīviduggādipakkhandanavasenāti adhippāyo. Maṃ posesi, upakāraṃ akāsi, tatra nappatirūpaṃ manaṃ padūsetunti evaṃ cittaṃ uppādetabbanti sambandho. Evaṃ cittuppādanañca etarahi dissamānena puttādīnaṃ posanādinā atītassa anumānato gahaṇavasena veditabbaṃ.

The path traveled by goats is a goat-path. The path traveled by making hooks cling and holding onto them is a hook-path. A ‘saṅkū’ is said to be a long-handled instrument made in the shape of a goad. By the word ‘ādi’ (etc.), it includes precipice-paths, difficult-to-travel paths, and so on. ‘Ubhatobyūḷho’ (drawn up on both sides) means armies with firmly fastened armor on both flanks for the purpose of battle. The meaning is that one endures by the power of forcibly traversing difficult mountain paths, difficult river paths, and so on, out of a desire for wealth, having also performed other difficult deeds. The connection is thus: 'He nourished me,' 'He did me a favor'; it is unsuitable to corrupt the mind towards such a person; thus, such a thought should be aroused. And this arising of thought should be understood by way of grasping it through inference about the past from the presently seen nurturing of children and so on.

249. Mettāyāti mettāsaṅkhātāya, mettāsahitāya vā. Cetovimuttiyāti cittasamādhāne. Āsevitāyāti ādarena sevitāya. Bhāvitāyāti vaḍḍhitāya. Bahulīkatāyāti punappunaṃ katāya. Yānīkatāyāti yuttayānaṃ viya katāya. Vatthukatāyāti adhiṭṭhānavatthuṃ viya katāya. Anuṭṭhitāyāti adhiṭṭhitāya. Paricitāyāti pariciṇṇāya ciṇṇavasībhāvāya. Susamāraddhāyāti suṭṭhu sampāditāya. Pāṭikaṅkhāti icchitabbā avassaṃbhāvino. Sesaṃ parato āgamissati.

249. ‘Mettāya’ means: that which is designated as loving-kindness, or that which is accompanied by loving-kindness. ‘Cetovimuttiyā’ means: in the concentration of mind, or in the jhāna of concentration which is the cause for the good placement of the mind. ‘Āsevitāya’ means: cultivated with care. ‘Bhāvitāya’ means: developed. ‘Bahulīkatāya’ means: done repeatedly. ‘Yānīkatāya’ means: made like a yoked vehicle. ‘Vatthukatāya’ means: made like a foundation. ‘Anuṭṭhitāya’ means: firmly established. ‘Paricitāya’ means: familiarized, brought to a state of mastery. ‘Susamāraddhāya’ means: well accomplished. ‘Pāṭikaṅkhā’ means: they are to be expected, they will certainly come to be. The rest will come later.

250. Dhātuvinibbhogoti sasambhārasaṅkhepādinā dhātūnaṃ vinibbhujanaṃ. Aparādho nāma aparajjhantassa puggalassa rūpadhammamukhena gayhatīti katvā āha “kiṃ kesānaṃ kujjhasī”tiādi, kesādivinimuttassa aparajjhanakassa puggalassa abhāvato. Idāni nibbattitaparamatthadhammavaseneva [V 1.0341] vinibbhogavidhiṃ dassetuṃ “atha vā panā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Pañcakkhandhe upādāya, dvādasāyatanāni upādāyāti paccekaṃ upādāya-saddo yojetabbo. Kodhassa patiṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ na hotīti yathā āragge sāsapassa, ākāse ca cittakammassa patiṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ natthi, evamassa “verī”ti parikappite puggale kodhassa patiṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ na hoti, kesādīnaṃ akujjhitabbato, tabbinimuttassa ca puggalassa abhāvato.

250. ‘Analysis of elements’ means the individual analysis of the elements by means of summary with their components, and so on. An offense is grasped primarily through the material phenomena of the offending person; having considered this, it was said, 'Why are you angry at the hairs?' and so on, because of the absence of an offending person who is separate from hair and the like. Now, in order to show the method of analysis solely by the power of the ultimate realities that have been produced, 'Or alternatively...' and so on was said. The word ‘upādāya’ should be connected to each term individually: 'with reference to the five aggregates,' 'with reference to the twelve sense bases,' and so on. There is no place of establishment for anger: just as there is no place of establishment for a mustard seed on the tip of an awl, or for a painting in the sky, so too, for this person, there is no place of establishment for anger towards a person conceived of as an 'enemy.' This is because hair and so on are not a proper object of anger, and because of the absence of a person separate from them.

251. Saṃvibhāgoti āmisasaṃvibhāgo. Parassāti paccatthikassa. Bhinnājīvoti aparisuddhājīvo. Tassevaṃ karototi evaṃ saṃvibhāgaṃ karontassa tassa dāyakassa. Itarassāti paṭiggāhakassa. “Mama mātarā upāsikāya [M 1.0362] dinno”ti idaṃ “dhammiyalābho”ti etassa kāraṇavacanaṃ. Tena pana tassa āgamanasuddhiṃ dasseti.

251. 'Sharing' (saṃvibhāgo) means the sharing of material things. 'For another' (parassa) means for an adversary. 'Of corrupt livelihood' (bhinnājīvo) means of impure livelihood. 'For one who does so' (tassevaṃ karoto) means for that donor who makes such a sharing. 'For the other' (itarassa) means for the recipient. The statement, 'It was given by my mother, the laywoman devotee,' is the causal statement for the phrase 'a righteous gain.' And by this, he shows the purity of its origin.

Sabbatthasādhakanti “attattho parattho diṭṭhadhammiko attho samparāyiko attho”ti (mahāni. 69; cūḷani. mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa 85; paṭi. ma. 3.5) evamādīnaṃ sabbesaṃ atthānaṃ, hitānaṃ, payojanānañca nipphādakaṃ. Unnamanti dāyakā. Namanti paṭiggāhakā.

'Accomplishing all purposes' (sabbatthasādhakaṃ) means that which accomplishes all purposes (attha), benefits (hita), and aims (payojana), such as 'one's own welfare, the welfare of others, welfare in the present life, and welfare in the life to come' (Mahāni. 69, etc.). Donors rise up. Recipients bow down.

252. Evanti yathāvuttehi kakacūpamovādānussaraṇādīhi attano ovadanākārehi. Vūpasantapaṭighassāti paṭisaṅkhānabalena vinoditāghātassa. Tasmimpīti verīpuggalepi. Verī-gahaṇeneva cettha appiyapuggalassāpi gahaṇaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ verimhi mettāya siddhāya tasmimpi mettāsiddhito, piyato pana atippiyasahāyakassa visuṃ gahaṇaṃ āsannapaccatthikassa dubbinimocayabhāvadassanatthaṃ. Mettāvasenāti mettāyanavasena. Samacittatanti hitūpasaṃhārena samānacittataṃ. Sīmāsambhedo sā eva samacittatā. Imasmiṃ puggaleti mettākammaṭṭhānikapuggale. Nisinneti bhāvenabhāvalakkhaṇe bhummaṃ.

252. 'Thus' (evaṃ) means: by the aforementioned ways of admonishing oneself, such as the recollection of the advice in the Kakacūpama Sutta. 'Of one whose aversion is calmed' (vūpasantapaṭighassa) means: of one whose anger has been dispelled by the power of reflective wisdom. 'Even towards him' (tasmimpi) means: even towards an enemy person. And here, by the taking of an 'enemy,' the taking of an 'unliked person' should also be understood. Why? Because when loving-kindness towards an enemy is accomplished, loving-kindness towards that unliked person is also accomplished. However, the separate mention of a 'very dear companion' from a 'dear person' is for the purpose of showing the nature of a proximate adversary (i.e., attachment) as something difficult to be free from. 'By the power of loving-kindness' (mettāvasena) means: by the power of practicing loving-kindness. 'Even-mindedness' (samacittataṃ) means: the state of having an equal mind by applying benefit. The 'breaking of boundaries' (sīmāsambhedo) is precisely that even-mindedness. 'In this person' (imasmiṃ puggale) means: in the person who is the meditation subject of loving-kindness. 'Seated' (nisinne) is a locative case in the sense of the locative absolute (bhāvena bhāva lakkhaṇa).

Hitamajjhatteti piye, majjhatte ca. Catubbidheti catubbidhe jane, yattha katthacīti adhippāyo. Nānattanti piyamajjhattādinānākaraṇaṃ. Hitacittova pāṇinanti kevalaṃ sattesu hitacitto evāti pavuccati, na pana “mettāya nikāmalābhī”ti vā “kusalī”ti vā pavuccati. Kasmā? Yasmā attādīsu passati nānattanti. Kasmā panāyaṃ hitacitto kusalīti na vuccatīti? Sātisayassa kusalassa vasena kusalibhāvassa adhippetattā. Imassa ca [V 1.0342] puggalassa mettābhāvanā na visesavatī. Atha vā na nikāmalābhī mettāya yato attādīsu passati nānattaṃ. Kusalīti pavuccati, yasmā hitacittova pāṇinanti evamettha attho daṭṭhabbo. Gāmasīmādayo viya gāmantarādīhi sattasaṅkhāte mettāvisaye bhāvanāya pubbe aññamaññaṃ asaṃkiṇṇamariyādārūpena ṭhitattā attādayo idha sīmā nāmāti āha “catasso sīmāyo”ti. Sambhinnā hontīti ettha vuttaṃ sambhedaṃ dassetuṃ “samaṃ pharati mettāyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Mahāvisesoti mahanto bhāvanāya viseso atisayo. Purimena purimato attādinānattadassinā. Na nāyatīti na ñāyati.

'Towards the dear and the neutral' (hitamajjhatte) means towards the dear and the neutral. 'Fourfold' (catubbidhe) refers to four kinds of people, the meaning being in any person whatsoever. 'Diversity' (nānattaṃ) means making the various distinctions such as dear, neutral, and so on. 'One with a mind of goodwill towards beings' (hitacittova pāṇinaṃ) is simply called one with a mind of goodwill towards beings, but not 'one who obtains loving-kindness at will' or 'one who is skillful.' Why? Because one sees diversity in oneself and others. But why is this person with goodwill not called skillful? Because the state of being skillful is intended in the sense of superior skillfulness. Moreover, this person’s development of loving-kindness is not excellent. Alternatively, one is not an obtainer of loving-kindness at will, since one sees diversity in oneself and others. One is not called skillful because one is merely 'one with a mind of goodwill towards beings'—this is how the meaning should be understood here. Just as village boundaries and so on stand unmixed with other villages, so too, because before the development of loving-kindness, oneself and others stand with unmixed boundaries in relation to one another within the sphere of loving-kindness designated as 'beings', they are here called 'boundaries'. Therefore, it is said, 'four boundaries.' To show the breaking of boundaries spoken of in the phrase 'they become broken,' it is said, 'one pervades equally with loving-kindness,' and so on. 'Great distinction' (mahāviseso) means a great distinction, an excellence, through development, compared to the former person who sees diversity in oneself and others. 'Is not led' (na nāyati) means 'is not known' (na ñāyati).

253. Nimittanti [M 1.0363] yathā kasiṇakammaṭṭhānādīsu taṃtaṃkasiṇamaṇḍalādipariggahamukhena bhāvanāvasena laddhaṃ uggahanimittaṃ nissāya jhānassa gocarabhāvena paṭibhāganimittaṃ upatiṭṭhati, na evamidha upaṭṭhitaṃ nimittaṃ nāma atthi. Yo panāyaṃ yathāvutto sīmāsambhedo laddho, sveva nimittaṃ viyāti nimittaṃ. Tasmiṃ hi laddhe bhāvanāya sātisayattā nīvaraṇāni vikkhambhitāneva honti, kilesā sannisinnāva, upacārasamādhinā cittaṃ samāhitameva. Tenāha “nimittañca upacārañca laddhaṃ hotī”ti. Tameva nimittanti sīmāsambhedavasena pavattasamathanimittaṃ. Appakasireneva akiccheneva, pageva paripanthassa visodhitattā.

253. Regarding the sign (nimitta): Just as in meditation subjects such as the kasiṇas, the counterpart sign arises as the object-domain for jhāna, depending on the learning sign that was obtained through the power of development by means of apprehending the respective kasiṇa disks and so on, so here there is no such thing as a sign that has arisen in this way. Rather, this breaking of the boundaries that has been obtained as described, because it is like a sign, is called the sign. For when that is obtained, due to the excellence of the development, the hindrances are indeed suppressed, the defilements are indeed calmed, and the mind is indeed concentrated with access concentration. Therefore, it is said, 'The sign and access concentration are obtained.' That very sign is the sign of serenity that proceeds by way of the breaking of the boundaries. [One attains absorption] with little trouble and without difficulty, because the dangers have already been cleared away.

Ettāvatāti ettakena bhāvanānuyogena. Anena yoginā. Pañcaṅgavippahīnantiādīnaṃ padānaṃ attho heṭṭhā vutto eva.

'By this much' (ettāvatā) means 'by this much application to development.' By this yogi. The meaning of the terms 'having abandoned the five factors' and so on has already been stated below.

“Paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ aññataravasenā”ti idaṃ vakkhamānāya vikubbanāya tesaṃ sādhāraṇatāya vuttaṃ. Appanāppattacittasseva na upacāramattalābhino. Paguṇabalavabhāvāpādanena vepullādivisesappattassa odhiso, anodhiso ca disāpharaṇādivasena jhānassa pavijambhanā vikubbanā vividhā kiriyāti katvā.

'Through the power of one or another of the first jhāna, etc.' This is said because of their commonality with the transformation that will be spoken of. This is only for one whose mind has reached absorption, not for one who has obtained mere access concentration. By bringing it to a state of proficiency and strength, the manifestation of the jhāna that has attained distinctions such as vastness—both limited and unlimited, by way of pervading the directions, etc.—is 'transformation' (vikubbanā), because it is 'diverse action' (vividhā kiriyā).

254. Mettāsahagatenāti uppādato yāva bhaṅgā mettāya saha pavattena saṃsaṭṭhena sampayuttenāti attho. Yasmā pana taṃ vuttanayena mettāya sahagataṃ, tāya ekuppādādividhinā sammadeva āgataṃ hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ “mettāya samannāgatenā”ti. Ceto-saddo “adhicetaso”tiādīsu (pāci. 153; udā. 37) samādhipariyāyopi hotīti tato visesetuṃ [V 1.0343] “cetasāti cittenā”ti vuttaṃ. Etanti etaṃ padaṃ. Disodhipariggaho sattodhipariggahamukheneva hotīti dassento āha “ekissā disāya paṭhamapariggahitaṃ sattaṃ upādāyā”ti. Disāsu hi ṭhitasattā disāgahaṇena gahitā. Tenāha “ekadisāpariyāpannasattapharaṇavasena vutta”nti. Pharaṇañca sārammaṇassa dhammassa attano ārammaṇassa phassanā paccakkhato dassanaṃ gahaṇaṃ ārammaṇakaraṇamevāti āha “pharitvāti phusitvā ārammaṇaṃ katvā”ti. Brahmavihārādhiṭṭhitanti mettājhānupatthambhitaṃ. Tathāti niyamanaṃ. Taṃ [M 1.0364] aniyamāpekkhasambandhībhāvato upamākāraniyamanaṃ. Dutiyanti upameyyadassanaṃ, upameyyañca nāma upamaṃ, tena sambandhañca vinā natthīti tadubhayampi dassetuṃ “yathā puratthimādīsū”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tathā dutiyanti ettha pharitvā viharatīti ānetvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Evaṃ tatiyaṃ catutthanti etthāpi. Tadanantaranti ca pharaṇāpekkhaṃ anantaraggahaṇaṃ, na pharitabbadisāpekkhaṃ disānaṃ aniddiṭṭharūpattā. Pharaṇānukkamena hi tāsaṃ dutiyāditā, na sarūpato. Tenevāha “yaṃ kiñci ekaṃ disa”nti. Itīti evaṃ yathāvuttaṃ catasso, evaṃ uddhaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatīti attho. Tenāha “eteneva nayenā”ti. Idampi iti-saddasseva atthadassanaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ (ma. ni. 3.309; 3.230; vibha. 642) adho tiriyanti ettha pi-saddo luttaniddiṭṭhoti dassetuṃ “adhodisampi tiriyaṃ disampī”ti vuttaṃ. Eteneva “dutiya”ntiādīsupi pi-saddassa luttaniddiṭṭhatā dīpitāti veditabbaṃ. Evamevāti idampi iti-saddasseva atthadassanaṃ. Ettha ca “adho”ti iminā yathā nirayesu, nāgabhavanādīsu, yattha tattha vā attano heṭṭhimadisāya sattā gayhanti, evaṃ “uddha”nti iminā devaloke, yattha tattha vā attano uparimadisāyaṃ sattā gahitāti veditabbaṃ.

254. 'Accompanied by loving-kindness' means that from its arising until its cessation, it occurs together with, is mingled with, and is associated with loving-kindness—this is the meaning. And since, in the way described, it is accompanied by loving-kindness, and properly comes along with it through having a single arising and so on, therefore it is said, 'endowed with loving-kindness.' The word `ceto` can also be a synonym for concentration, as in phrases like `adhicetaso`; to distinguish from that, it is said, '`cetasā` means `cittena` (with the mind).' Showing that the delimitation of directions occurs only by means of the delimitation of beings, he said, 'taking as basis the beings first delimited in one direction.' For beings situated in the directions are included by the taking of the directions. Therefore he said, it is 'stated in terms of pervading the beings included in one direction.' And pervasion is the touching, direct seeing, grasping, the making into an object, of its own object by a mental phenomenon that has an object. Therefore, it is said, 'having pervaded' means 'having touched, having made it an object.' 'Established in the divine abodes' means supported by the jhāna of loving-kindness. 'Thus' (`tathā`) is a particle of specification. Because it is related by depending on the unspecified particle (`yathā`), it is a specification of the manner of the simile. 'Second' indicates the object of comparison. And since the object of comparison does not exist without the simile and its connection with it, to show both of these, it is said, 'as in the eastern direction, etc.' There, in the phrase 'so the second,' the words 'having pervaded, one dwells' should be supplied and connected. Likewise for 'the third' and 'the fourth.' And in 'immediately after that,' the taking of 'immediately after' is with reference to the pervasion, not with reference to the direction to be pervaded, because the directions have no specified form. For their being 'second,' etc., is by the sequence of pervasion, not by their intrinsic nature. Therefore he said, 'any single direction.' The word `iti` means: thus, as was said for the four directions, so 'having pervaded the upward direction, one dwells.' Therefore he said, 'by this same method.' This too shows the meaning of the word `iti`. In the Pāli text, in the phrase 'downward, across,' to show that the word `pi` ('also') is elided, it is said, 'the downward direction also, and the across direction also.' By this it should be known that the elision of the word `pi` is also indicated in 'second,' etc. 'In this same way': this too shows the meaning of the word `iti`. And here, by 'downward' should be understood beings in the lower direction, wherever they may be, such as in the hells or in the abodes of the nāgas. Likewise, by 'upward' are taken beings in the upper direction, wherever they may be, such as in the deva world.

Majjhattādīti ādi-saddena itthipurisaariyānariyadevamanussādike pabhede saṅgaṇhāti. Īsakampi bahi avikkhipamānoti appakampi kammaṭṭhānato bahi vikkhepaṃ anāpajjanto hitūpasaṃhārato aññathā thokampi avattamāno. Sabbattatāyāti vā sabbena attabhāvena yathā sabbabhāvena attani attano attabhāve hitesitā, evaṃ sabbadhi sabbasattesu mettāya pharitvā viharatīti attho. Mettāya vuccamānattā sattavisayo sabba-saddo, so ca dīghaṃ katvā vutto, tasmā sabbasattakāyasaṅkhātā pajā etassa atthīti sabbāvantoti padatthato dassento “sabbāvantanti sabbasattavanta”nti āha. Ettha ca sabbadhīti disodhinā, desodhinā ca anodhisopharaṇaṃ vuttaṃ, sabbattatāya sabbāvantanti sattodhinā. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “anodhiso dassanattha”nti[V 1.0344]. Ekamevatthaṃ pakārato pariyāyenti ñāpentīti pariyāyā, vevacanāni. Vipulādisaddā cettha tādisāti adhippāyo. Tenāha “vipulenāti evamādipariyāyadassanato”ti. Pariyāyadassane ca pubbe gahitapadānipi [M 1.0365] puna gayhanti, yathā “saddhā saddahanā”ti (dha. sa. 12) ettha vuttampi saddhāpadaṃ puna indriyādipariyāyadassane “saddhā saddhindriya”nti (dha. sa. 12) vuttaṃ. Tathāsaddo vā itisaddo vā na vuttoti “mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharatī”ti etassa anuvattako tathā-saddo ca iti-saddo ca tesaṃ pharaṇānantarādiṭṭhānaṃ aṭṭhānanti katvā te na vuttāti puna “mettāsahagatena cetasāti vutta”nti attho. Vuttassevatthassa puna vacanaṃ nigamananti āha “nigamanavasena vā etaṃ vutta”nti. Nanu ca samāpanavasena vuttassevatthassa puna vacanaṃ nigamananti? Nāyaṃ doso odhisoanodhisopharaṇānaṃ samāpane eva vuttattā. Vipulenāti mahantena, mahattañcassa asubhakammaṭṭhānādīsu viya ārammaṇassa ekadesameva aggahetvā anavasesaggahaṇavasenāti āha “pharaṇavasena vipulatā daṭṭhabbā”ti.

In "Majjhattādi" (neutral, etc.), by the word "ādi" (etc.), it includes distinctions such as female, male, noble, ignoble, deva, human, and so on. "Not being distracted even slightly outwardly" means not falling into distraction even a little from the meditation object, and not acting otherwise even a little from bringing about benefit. Or, "with all of one's being" (`sabbattatāya`) means: just as there is a desire for one's own welfare in oneself, in one's own being, with every part, in the same way, one dwells pervading all beings everywhere with loving-kindness; this is the meaning. Because loving-kindness is being spoken of, the word "sabba" (all) has beings as its domain, and it is stated with a long vowel. Therefore, showing the meaning of the word `sabbāvanta` as derived from "possessing all (`sabbā`) beings," he said, "`sabbāvanta` means `sabbasattavanta` (possessing all beings)." And here, by the word "sabbadhi" (everywhere), boundless pervasion is stated by way of directional and regional specification; by the words "sabbattatāya" and "sabbāvanta," it is stated by way of the specification of beings. For so it was said: "for the purpose of showing the boundless." Because they make known one and the same meaning in different ways, they are called synonyms (`pariyāyā`) or alternative terms (`vevacanāni`). The words `vipula` (expansive), etc., here are of such a nature; this is the intention. Therefore, he said, "`vipulena`, etc., from showing such synonyms." And in showing synonyms, words already taken up are taken up again; just as in "saddhā saddahanā" (faith, confidence), the word `saddhā`, though already stated, is stated again in showing the synonyms for faculties, etc., as "saddhā saddhindriya" (faith, the faculty of faith). The words `tathā` (thus) or `iti` (so) are not stated. The meaning is: the words `tathā` and `iti`, which would follow the phrase "dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness," are not stated because their position—the basis for what comes after the pervasion—is not the appropriate place for them. Therefore, "with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness" is stated again. The repetition of a meaning already stated is a conclusion (`nigamana`). Therefore, he said, "Or this is stated by way of conclusion." But is not the repetition of a meaning already stated a conclusion by way of completion? This is not a fault, because it is stated in the very conclusion of the limited and boundless pervasions. "Vipulena" means by the great. And its greatness consists in not grasping just one part of the object, as in the meditation subjects of foulness, etc., but in grasping it completely without remainder. Therefore, he said, "Expansiveness should be seen by way of pervasion."

Kilesavikkhambhanasamatthatādīhi mahattaṃ gataṃ, mahantehi vā uḷāracchandacittavīriyapaññehi gataṃ paṭipannanti mahaggataṃ. Tayidaṃ yasmā ekantato rūpāvacaraṃ, tasmā vuttaṃ “bhūmivasena mahaggata”nti. Niruḷho hi rūpārūpāvacaresu mahaggatavohāro. Paguṇavasenāti pakārato guṇitaṃ bahulīkataṃ paguṇaṃ, tassa vasena, subhāvitabhāvenāti attho. Taṃ hi pamāṇaṃ gahetuṃ asakkuṇeyyatāya appamāṇaṃ nāma hoti. Appamāṇasattārammaṇavasenāti aparimāṇasattārammaṇakaraṇavasena. Sayampi verarahitattā, taṃsamaṅgino verābhāvahetuttā ca averaṃ. Tayidaṃ dvayaṃ yato labhati, taṃ dassetuṃ “byāpādapaccatthikappahānenā”ti vuttaṃ. Cetaso byāpattivasena hananato byāpajjaṃ, cetasikaṃ asātaṃ, tadabhāvato abyāpajjaṃ. Tenāha “niddukkha”nti. Taṃ panassa abyāpajjattaṃ pañcaviññāṇādīnaṃ viya na sabhāvato, atha kho paccatthikavivekatoti dassento “domanassappahānato”ti āha. Ayanti idha yathānītaṃ appamaññāvibhaṅge (vibha. 642), tesu tesu ca suttapadesesu (ma. ni. 1.459; 2.309, 315) āgataṃ mettābrahmavihāravikubbanamāha.

It has gone to greatness (`mahattaṃ gataṃ`) through the ability to suppress defilements, etc.; or, it is gone to, practiced (`gataṃ paṭipannaṃ`), by great ones (`mahantehi`) endowed with lofty aspiration, consciousness, energy, and wisdom; therefore, it is `mahaggata` (sublime). Because that is exclusively of the fine-material sphere, it is said, “sublime by way of plane.” Indeed, the designation `mahaggata` is established in relation to the fine-material and immaterial spheres. “By way of proficiency” (`paguṇavasena`) means: that which is multiplied in various ways, made frequent, is `paguṇa`. By way of that, meaning by way of being well-developed. Indeed, because it is impossible to grasp its measure, it is called `appamāṇa` (immeasurable). “By way of having immeasurable beings as its object” (`appamāṇasattārammaṇavasena`) means by way of making immeasurable beings its object. It is `avera` (without enmity) because it is itself free from enmity, and because it is a cause for the absence of enmity in one endowed with it. To show from where it obtains this twofold reason, it is said, “through the abandoning of ill will, the adversary.” `Byāpajja` (affliction) is so called because it harms (`hananato`) by way of afflicting (`byāpattivasena`) the mind; it is mental displeasure. Due to its absence, it is `abyāpajja` (unafflicted). Therefore, he said, `niddukkha` (without suffering). But its state of being unafflicted is not so by its intrinsic nature, like that of the five sense-consciousnesses and so on; rather, it is due to seclusion from the adversary. Showing this, he said, “from the abandoning of displeasure.” By `ayaṃ` (this), he speaks of the manifold expression of the loving-kindness Brahmā-vihāra that has come down in the Appamaññāvibhaṅga as cited here (Vibh. 642), and in various Sutta passages (M. Ni. 1.459; 2.309, 315).

255. “Tathā”ti iminā imissā “pañcahākārehi, sattahākārehi, dasahākārehī”ti ākāravibhāgena paṭisambhidāyaṃ (paṭi. ma. 2.22) vuttāya ca vikubbanāya [M 1.0366] majjhe bhinnasuvaṇṇassa [V 1.0345] viya bhedābhāvamupasaṃharati odhisopharaṇaanodhisopharaṇadisāpharaṇavasena desanāya āgatattā. Kevalaṃ panettha paṭisambhidāmagge (paṭi. ma. 2.22) viya sattodhi na gahitoti ayameva viseso. Yampīti vikubbanaṃ sandhāyāha.

255. By this word “Tathā” (thus), he brings together the absence of division—like that of a gold bar broken in the middle—between this manifold expression and the manifold expression spoken of in the Paṭisambhidāmagga (Paṭi. Ma. 2.22) with its analysis of modes as “by five modes, by seven modes, by ten modes,” because the teaching has come down by way of limited pervasion, boundless pervasion, and directional pervasion. Only, here, the specification of beings (`sattodhi`) is not taken up as it is in the Paṭisambhidāmagga (Paṭi. Ma. 2.22); this alone is the difference. When it says “Yampi” (and whatever), he says it with reference to the manifold expression.

Idāni bhedābhāvadassanamukhena uddesato ānītaṃ paṭisambhidāmaggapāḷiṃ niddesato dassetvā tassā anuttānapadavaṇṇanaṃ kātuṃ “tattha cā”tiādimāha.

Now, by means of showing the absence of division, having presented in detail the Paṭisambhidāmagga Pāḷi that was introduced in summary, in order to provide a commentary on its words with non-obvious meanings, he begins with “tattha ca,” etc.

256. Tattha sabbe sattāti sabba-saddo kāmaṃ padesasabbavisayo, na sabbasabbavisayo yathā “sabbaṃ jānātīti sabbaññutaññāṇa”nti (paṭi. ma. 1.119-120), “sattā”ti pana padena paricchinnaṃ attano visayaṃ asesetvāva pariyādiyatīti āha “anavasesapariyādānameta”nti.

256. Therein, in “sabbe sattā” (all beings), the word “sabba” (all) indeed has a partial ‘all’ as its domain; it does not have a total ‘all’ as its domain, as in “the knowledge of omniscience because one knows all” (Paṭi. Ma. 1.119–120). However, by the word “sattā” (beings), it encompasses its own delimited domain without remainder. Therefore, he said, “This is an encompassing without remainder.”

Tatrāti tasmiṃ rūpe. Sattoti sajjanakiccena chandādipariyāyena lobhena āsatto laggo. Tatrāti vā karaṇe bhummaṃ, tena chandādināti attho.
